Chapter 11 was about linear kinematics—how to describe the motion of object, without concerning ourselves with the “cause” of the motion, its orientation, or how we might go about simulating that object on a computer. The main goals of this chapter are to address those three topics.
第 11 章讲的是线性运动学——如何描述物体的运动，而不考虑运动的“原因”、运动的方向，也不考虑如何在计算机上模拟该物体。本章的主要目标是讨论这三个主题。

  • Section 12.1 identifies and quantifies the “cause” of motion, force, and presents three physical laws formalized more than 400 years ago by Isaac Newton in his masterwork the Principia.
    第 12.1 节识别并量化了运动和力的“原因”，并提出了艾萨克·牛顿在其杰作《自然哲学的数学原理》中于 400 多年前正式提出的三条物理定律。
  • Section 12.2 discusses a few particularly important and simple types of forces.
    第 12.2 节讨论了一些特别重要且简单的力量类型。
  • Section 12.3 introduces momentum and presents the important relationship between force and momentum.
    第 12.3 节介绍动量并阐述力和动量之间的重要关系。
  • Section 12.4 is about collisions and impulses, which are large forces that act for short durations.
    第 12.4 节讨论碰撞和冲击，它们是短时间内作用的巨大力量。
  • Section 12.5 considers the rotation of objects and the angular analogs of the linear concepts introduced up to this point.
    第 12.5 节考虑物体的旋转以及到目前为止介绍的线性概念的角度类似物。
  • Section 12.6 turns to matters of implementation, looking at some basic problems that a digital simulation needs to address. It gives an overview of how contemporary real-time rigid body simulations solve them.
    第 12.6 节探讨了实施问题，探讨了数字模拟需要解决的一些基本问题。它概述了当代实时刚体模拟如何解决这些问题。

12.1Newton's Three Laws  12.1 牛顿三定律

Sir Isaac Newton established three simple laws that provide a framework, commonly known as Newtonian mechanics, for understanding such diverse physical systems as an apple falling from a tree, the motion of the planets, and the physical interactions that happen in a video game. Newtonian mechanics is also called classical mechanics, and that name should alert you to the fact that the laws we are about to study are wrong, in the sense that they do not agree with the result of experiments conducted at very high speed (which require relativistic mechanics) or at very small scale (which require quantum mechanics).1 For everyday phenomena (and for the phenomena we need to simulate in a video game), the discrepancy between the results predicted by Newtonian mechanics and the correct results (as correctly predicted by quantum-relativistic mechanics) is generally less than can be detected with the most accurate instruments. The differences in the predictions become significant only at speeds very close to the speed of light and at scales approaching the size of an atom; otherwise, all the theories are in great agreement with each other and with experimental results. It was precisely because Newtonian mechanics has such a long and decorated history of accurate predictions that it was so shocking to find out that the laws were in need of correction. It should be clear that these laws, having been sufficient to describe the motions of the heavenly bodies to a great deal of accuracy, will also be quite sufficient for our purposes here.
艾萨克·牛顿爵士建立了三条简单的定律，它们提供了一个框架，通常称为牛顿力学，用于理解各种各样的物理系统，例如苹果从树上掉下来、行星的运动以及视频游戏中发生的物理相互作用。牛顿力学也称为经典力学，这个名称应该提醒你，我们即将研究的定律是错误的，因为它们与以非常高的速度（需要相对论力学）或非常小的尺度（需要量子力学）进行的实验的结果不一致。1 对于日常现象（以及我们需要在视频游戏中模拟的现象），牛顿力学预测的结果与正确结果（量子相对论力学正确预测的结果）之间的差异通常小于用最精确的仪器可以检测到的差异。只有在非常接近光速的速度和接近原子大小的尺度上，预测的差异才会变得显著；除此之外，所有理论彼此之间以及与实验结果都高度一致。正因为牛顿力学有着悠久而辉煌的精确预测历史，所以当人们发现这些定律需要修正时，才感到如此震惊。显而易见的是，这些定律足以相当准确地描述天体的运动，因此对于我们这里的目的来说，也同样足够了。

12.1.1Newton's First Two Laws: Force and Mass
12.1.1 牛顿前两条定律：力和质量

Chapter 11 noted that mass measures the degree to which an object resists being accelerated. This resistance is called inertia, and the physical quantity needed to overcome it and create an acceleration is called force. In other words, all of those “causes of motion” that we so scrupulously avoided mentioning in the previous chapter actually go by the collective name force.
第十一章指出，质量衡量的是物体抵抗加速的程度。这种阻力被称为惯性，而克服惯性并产生加速度所需的物理量被称为力。换句话说，我们在上一章中刻意回避的所有“运动原因”，实际上都被统称为力。

The idea that objects resist acceleration is summarized by Newton's first law.
牛顿第一定律概括了物体抵抗加速度的思想。

Newton's First Law  牛顿第一定律
Every body persists in its state of being at rest or of moving uniformly straight forward, except insofar as it is compelled to change its state by force impressed.
任何物体都会保持其静止状态或匀速直线运动状态，除非受到外力的作用而改变其状态。

This seems like quite a simple statement, even in the anachronistic translation of Newton's original Latin. But consider how audacious it was for Newton to assert this, when it so clearly is at odds with the commonsense observations we all have from our daily lives! A more “commonsense” way to think about force is to assume that force is needed not only to start an object in motion, but also to maintain its motion. (This is the rule under so-called Aristotelian dynamics.) After all, once we stop applying the force, eventually the object will stop moving, right? According to Newton, once an object is set in motion, it does not require any force to continue this motion. In fact, Newton claims that the force is required to stop the object, and absent this stopping force, the object will continue on indefinitely.
即使是用牛顿拉丁文原文的过时翻译来看，这似乎也是一个相当简单的陈述。但想想牛顿断言这一点是多么大胆，因为它显然与我们日常生活中的常识性观察相悖！思考力的更“常识”的方式是假设力不仅是物体开始运动所必需的，也是物体维持运动所必需的。（这就是所谓的亚里士多德动力学规则。）毕竟，一旦我们停止施加力，物体最终就会停止运动，对吗？根据牛顿的理论，一旦物体开始运动，它就不需要任何力来继续运动。事实上，牛顿声称需要力来停止物体，如果没有这种阻止力，物体将无限期地继续运动。

Of course, the reason Newton's first law seems counterintuitive is that in our everyday experience, when we set objects in motion, they are always brought to a stop by the ubiquitous force of friction. But we can argue that Newton's law is correct, even though objects always come to a stop through friction, with a simple thought experiment. Imagine we apply a certain amount of force and set an object in motion across a surface. The object will travel a certain distance and eventually come to a stop. Did it stop due the lack of continued pushing force, or due to some force that acted to slow it down? If we perform the same experiment on different surfaces, performing the initial push in the same manner in each case, we find that the object travels farther on a smoother surface, and less distance on a rougher surface. You probably aren't surprised at these ”commonsense” results, but notice how they actually contradict the notion that a force is required to keep the object in motion and validate Newton's laws.
当然，牛顿第一定律之所以看起来违反直觉，是因为在我们的日常经验中，当我们使物体运动时，它们总是会因为无处不在的摩擦力而停止。但是，即使物体总是因为摩擦力而停止，我们也可以证明牛顿定律是正确的，只需一个简单的思想实验即可。假设我们施加一定量的力，使一个物体在一个表面上运动。物体会移动一段距离并最终停止下来。它停止是因为缺乏持续的推力，还是因为有某种力使它减速？如果我们在不同的表面上进行相同的实验，并在每种情况下以相同的方式施加初始推力，我们会发现物体在光滑的表面上移动得更远，而在粗糙的表面上移动得更短。你可能不会对这些“常识性”的结果感到惊讶，但请注意，它们实际上与“需要力来保持物体运动并验证牛顿定律”这一概念相矛盾。

Newton clarified the precise relationship among mass, acceleration, and net force in his second law.
牛顿在他的第二定律中阐明了质量、加速度和净力之间的精确关系。

Newton's Second Law  牛顿第二定律
The acceleration of a body is proportional to (and in the same direction as) the net external force acting on the body, and inversely proportional to the mass of the body:
物体的加速度与作用于物体的净外力成正比（且方向相同），与物体的质量成反比：
(12.1) f =m a .

This simple equation is the most important one in this chapter. You should certainly memorize it. It basically says that whenever a particle with mass m is seen accelerating at a rate a , you can be sure that there is a net force f acting on the particle. Likewise, whenever there is a net force, the object will accelerate, because net force and acceleration always go together. There are no exceptions to this rule. The acceleration of an object is always proportional to the net force acting on it at that moment.
这个简单的等式是本章中最重要的一个，你一定要记住它。它的基本意思是，每当一个质量为 m 的粒子以 a 的速率加速时，可以肯定有一个净力 f 作用于该粒子。同样，只要有净力，物体就会加速，因为净力和加速度总是相辅相成的。这条规则没有例外。物体的加速度总是与当时作用于它的净力成正比。

Now this does not mean that when there are any forces on an object, it will necessarily accelerate. Nor does it mean that if an object is not accelerating, then there are no forces acting on it. The f in f =m a is the net force. Consider the tremendous forces exerted on the beams at the bottom of a skyscraper. Clearly there is a force that wants to accelerate the beam downward. However, since the beams do not in fact accelerate downward, we know by Newton's second law that this downward force must be exactly opposed by some other force acting in the opposite direction.
这并不意味着当物体受到任何力时，它必然会加速。也不意味着如果物体没有加速，就没有力作用在它身上。 f =m a 中的 f 是净力。想象一下摩天大楼底部横梁上施加的巨大力。显然，有一个力想要使横梁向下加速。然而，由于横梁实际上并没有向下加速，根据牛顿第二定律，我们知道这个向下的力一定与另一个作用在相反方向的力正好相反。

What sort of quantity is force? First of all, force has magnitude and direction, and so it is a vector quantity, just like acceleration (although at times it is easier to study force in a one-dimensional setting, just like we did with acceleration). And force must have the same dimensions (1D, 2D, or 3D, depending on the “world” in which we are working) as the acceleration a for Equation (12.1) to make sense, because m is a scalar quantity.
力是什么样的量？首先，力有大小和方向，所以它是一个矢量，就像加速度一样（尽管有时在一维环境中研究力更容易，就像我们研究加速度一样）。力必须具有与加速度 a 相同的维度（一维、二维或三维，取决于我们工作的“世界”），这样公式 (12.1) 才有意义，因为 m 是一个标量。

Let's use dimensional analysis to determine the physical units that we should use to measure force. Mass is one of our fundamental quantities, denoted M , and from the previous chapter we know that acceleration has units L / T2 . Therefore (dropping the bold to indicate vector quantities), force must have units
让我们利用量纲分析来确定测量力的物理单位。质量是我们的基本量之一，用 M 表示，从上一章我们知道加速度的单位是 L / T2 。因此（去掉粗体以表示矢量），力必须有单位

Dimensional analysis of force
力的量纲分析
f=ma=(M)(L / T2).

When measuring with the SI units—mass in kilograms, length in meters, and time in seconds—force has the units of “kilogram meter per second squared.” This is quite a mouthful, so it goes by a special name, the Newton, denoted N:
当使用国际单位制（SI）测量时——质量以千克为单位，长度以米为单位，时间以秒为单位——力的单位是“千克·米/平方秒”。这个单位比较拗口，所以它有一个特殊的名字——牛顿，记为 N：

The Newton is an SI unit of force
牛顿是力的国际单位
1  N =1  kg m s 2.

If you're having trouble grasping just what a “kilogram meter per second squared” is, just remember that a Newton is the amount of force required to accelerate a mass of 1 kg at a rate of 1 m/ s 2 .
如果您无法理解“千克米每平方秒”的具体含义，只需记住，1 牛顿就是使 1 千克的质量以 1 米/ s 2 的速度加速所需的力。

There's a common misunderstanding that we'd like to cut off as early as possible. Force creates an acceleration on a body, and it acts over time. For example, the question, “How much force does it take to get a 100 lb object to go 100 mi/hr?” does not make sense. Force doesn't produce velocity directly, it causes the velocity to change over time. This can be especially confusing when you consider collisions, such as a ball bouncing on the floor or being struck by a bat. Although the velocity appears to have changed instantaneously, what is really happening is that a very large force is acting for a very short (but finite) duration. We study collisions in more detail in Section 12.3. Typically in digital simulations impulsive forces are handled differently from more persistent forces that act over several simulation steps, so for now, don't think of a force as an impact; instead, think of it as more of a gradual push or pull that could be provided by, for example, a spring, the wind, or gravity.
我们希望尽早消除一种常见的误解。力会在物体上产生加速度，并且会随时间推移而作用。例如，“需要多大的力才能使一个 100 磅的物体以 100 英里/小时的速度运动？”这个问题本身就不合理。力不会直接产生速度，它会导致速度随时间变化。考虑到碰撞，例如球在地板上弹跳或被球棒击中，这种现象尤其令人困惑。虽然速度看起来瞬间发生了变化，但实际上是一个非常大的力在很短（但有限）的时间内作用。我们将在第 12.3 节更详细地研究碰撞。通常，在数字模拟中，脉冲力的处理方式与在多个模拟步骤中作用的持久力不同，因此现在不要将力视为冲击力；相反，应该将其视为一种渐进的推力或拉力，例如弹簧、风或重力。

We said that Equation (12.1) is the traditional way to express the relationship among force, mass, and acceleration. However, written in that way, with force on the left-hand side, you might get the idea that the common situation is for us to know the mass and acceleration, and use Newton's laws to compute the force. In fact, especially in digital simulations, the more common scenario is that we have calculated the forces acting on a body, and we wish to predict the body's response to those forces. In other words, we'll usually use Newton's second law in the form
我们说过，公式 (12.1) 是表达力、质量和加速度之间关系的传统方法。然而，如果这样写，力在公式左边，你可能会觉得，通常的情况是，我们知道质量和加速度，然后用牛顿定律来计算力。事实上，尤其是在数字模拟中，更常见的情况是，我们已经计算出作用在物体上的力，并希望预测物体对这些力的响应。换句话说，我们通常会使用牛顿第二定律，其形式如下：

We usually use this form of Newton's second law
我们通常使用牛顿第二定律的这种形式
(12.2) a = f / m.

Most physics textbooks teach the important conceptual tool known as a free-body diagram. Newton's second law, especially as expressed in Equation (12.2), is at the heart of this exercise. The basic procedure is as follows, starting with a representation of the object.
大多数物理教科书都会教授一个重要的概念工具，即自由体图。牛顿第二定律，尤其是公式 (12.2) 中表达的定律，是这项练习的核心。基本步骤如下，首先从物体的表述开始。

  1. Draw and label all the forces acting on it.
    绘制并标记作用于其上的所有力。
  2. Sum up those forces (using vector addition) to compute the net force.
    将这些力相加（使用矢量加法）来计算净力。
  3. Use Newton's second law (Equation (12.2)) to compute the acceleration of the object.
    利用牛顿第二定律（公式 (12.2)）计算物体的加速度。
  4. Integrate the acceleration to determine the motion of the object. When solving problems analytically, this means solving differential equations. We don't use any differential equations in this book because there are only a few simple cases that we will look at analytically. Numerical methods of integration must be used. Later, we examine Euler integration, which is the most simple method imaginable, but also the one used by most real-time rigid body simulators.
    对加速度进行积分以确定物体的运动。解析求解问题时，这意味着求解微分方程。本书不使用任何微分方程，因为我们只讨论几个简单的解析解案例。必须使用数值积分方法。之后，我们将研究欧拉积分，这是最简单的方法，也是大多数实时刚体模拟器所使用的方法。

The above procedure is a very important tool that we use several times in Section 12.2; it's also essentially how most digital physics simulations work inside a computer. Of course, the simplicity with which we've described this 4-step process hides many troublesome difficulties. The forces in Equation (12.2) may vary continuously over time; be dependent on time, position, and velocity; exhibit nonlinearities or discontinuities; and in general be difficult to compute exactly or express and integrate in closed form. Section 12.6 deals with physics simulations, but for now the key point that we want to emphasize is that Newton's second law is the fundamental driving equation.
上述过程是一个非常重要的工具，我们在 12.2 节中多次使用；它也是大多数数字物理模拟在计算机内部工作的本质方式。当然，我们描述的这 4 步过程的简单性背后隐藏着许多棘手的难题。方程 (12.2) 中的力可能随时间连续变化；可能依赖于时间、位置和速度；可能表现出非线性或不连续性；并且通常难以精确计算或以封闭形式表达和积分。12.6 节讨论了物理模拟，但现在我们要强调的重点是牛顿第二定律是基本的驱动方程。

12.1.2Inertial Reference Frames
12.1.2 惯性参考系

If we take the special case where f = 0 , then according to Newton's second law, a = 0 . This is a restatement of his first law. So we see that if Newton had been just a bit more clever, he could have said the same thing in only two laws instead of three. Of course, Newton not only broke through the barrier of “common sense” to create elegant formulas that explain the workings of every physical system in the entire universe, he also simultaneously invented a complete branch of the mathematics needed to fully explore these ideas—calculus. So perhaps he was a clever guy after all. We assume he had a good reason for keeping his first law; we interpret it as a statement about reference frames.
如果我们考虑 f = 0 的特殊情况，那么根据牛顿第二定律， a = 0 。这是他第一定律的重述。因此我们看到，如果牛顿再聪明一点，他就可以只用两条定律而不是三条定律来表达同样的道理。当然，牛顿不仅突破了“常识”的障碍，创建了优雅的公式来解释整个宇宙中每个物理系统的运作，他还同时发明了充分探索这些思想所需的一个完整的数学分支——微积分。所以也许他毕竟是个聪明人。我们假设他保留第一定律是有充分理由的；我们将其解释为关于参考系的陈述。

The vectors a and f are specified in some reference frame, and if we choose a bad reference frame, the equation does not hold. Reference frames in which the basic mechanical laws hold (especially f =m a ) are known as inertial reference frames. Coordinate spaces for which this law does not hold unless we invent fictional forces are called noninertial frames.
向量 a 和 f 是在某个参考系中指定的，如果我们选择一个错误的参考系，该方程将不成立。基本力学定律（尤其是 f =m a ）成立的参考系被称为惯性参考系。除非我们引入虚构力，否则该定律不成立的坐标空间被称为非惯性系。

Figure 12.1  图 12.1 A robot in a falling elevator is in a non-inertial frame. He must invent a fictitious upward force to counteract gravity to explain why his herring sandwich doesn't fall.
一个机器人在下落的电梯中处于非惯性系中。他必须虚构一个向上的力来抵消重力，才能解释为什么他的鲱鱼三明治不会掉下来。

For example, imagine a robot eating a herring sandwich in an elevator. Someone cuts the elevator cables, and the elevator, robot, and sandwich begin to fall. Now, this robot has been programmed with the knowledge that it likes to eat herring sandwiches,2 but without any general sense of self-preservation, so it does not panic. It looks at the herring sandwich floating in mid-air instead of falling to the elevator floor, as it would reasonably expect. The robot, having also been programmed with an incomplete understanding of Newton's laws, thinks to itself, “My goodness, this is quite unusual! I know gravity must be pulling this sandwich downwards and I know f =m a , and since the sandwich is not accelerating downwards, the net force acting on it must be zero. Therefore, there must be some upward force acting on this sandwich. Quite fascinating! What might be the source of this force? Now, if I calculate…” CRASH!
例如，想象一个机器人在电梯里吃鲱鱼三明治。有人剪断了电梯电缆，电梯、机器人和三明治开始下落。这个机器人已经被编程为喜欢吃鲱鱼三明治，2 但没有任何自我保护意识，所以它不会惊慌。它看着鲱鱼三明治漂浮在半空中，而不是像它合理预期的那样掉到电梯地板上。这个机器人也是根据对牛顿定律的不完全理解而被编程的，它心想：“天哪，这太不寻常了！我知道重力一定在把这个三明治向下拉，而且我知道 f =m a ，由于三明治没有向下加速，作用在它上的净力一定为零。因此，一定有一个向上的力作用在这个三明治上。真有趣！这个力的来源可能是什么？现在，如果我计算……”崩溃！

Figure 12.2  图 12.2 An alien watching the elevator fall as Earth moves past will not see anything to contradict Newton's three laws, assuming the time period is short enough so that Earth's rotation and curved path are not significant factors.
当外星人看到电梯在地球经过时下落时，他不会看到任何与牛顿三大定律相矛盾的东西，假设时间段足够短，以至于地球的自转和弯曲路径不是重要因素。

A viewer on the ground would not see any need to invent a fictitious force to explain the sandwich's behavior. Using a reference frame with the origin fixed at the bottom of the building, the viewer sees the sandwich as accelerating downward, and has no reason to think anything is amiss.3 The person driving by in a car also doesn't see any problems. In the reference frame of the car, the sandwich appears to travel in a parabolic motion. But the relation f =m a seems to hold, and so the driver observes that Newton's laws are valid in her reference frame. Likewise for the advanced alien civilization watching from their cloaked spaceship as Earth whizzes past (see Figure 12.2). From their4 perspective, everything seems to be obeying Newton's laws. To the alien, Earth is moving with a constant linear velocity and the elevator's trajectory is parabolic, just as we would predict using the projectile equations developed in Section 11.6. (Actually, we are ignoring some finer points, such as Earth's rotation, the curved path it takes as it orbits the sun, and the do-si-do it does with the moon. These deviations from constant linear velocity are the exceptions that prove the rule: they are the reason why a reference frame fixed to Earth's surface is not quite an inertial frame. Experiments such as Foucault's pendulum can detect the difference, even though it is slight.)
地面上的观察者认为没有必要虚构一种力来解释三明治的行为。使用以建筑物底部为原点的参考系，观察者看到三明治向下加速，并且没有理由认为有什么不对劲。3 开车经过的人也没有发现任何问题。在汽车的参考系中，三明治似乎在做抛物线运动。但关系 f =m a 似乎成立，因此驾驶员观察到牛顿定律在她的参考系中是有效的。对于从隐形飞船上观看地球呼啸而过的先进外星文明来说也是如此（见图 12.2）。从他们的 4 视角来看，一切似乎都遵循牛顿定律。对外星人来说，地球以恒定的线速度运动，电梯的轨迹是抛物线，正如我们根据第 11.6 节中提出的抛射方程所预测的那样。 （实际上，我们忽略了一些更细微的点，比如地球的自转、绕太阳公转的曲线路径，以及它绕月球公转的轨迹。这些偏离恒定线速度的现象是例外，却证明了这条规则：它们就是为什么固定在地球表面的参考系不完全是惯性系的原因。诸如傅科摆之类的实验可以检测到这种差异，即使这种差异很小。）

In summary, if a reference frame is accelerating or rotating, the motion of objects described using that reference frame will not be consistent with mechanical laws. An inertial reference frame must be stationary or moving at a constant linear velocity.
总而言之，如果一个参考系正在加速或旋转，那么用该参考系描述的物体运动将不符合力学定律。惯性参考系必须是静止的，或者以恒定的线速度运动。

12.1.3Newton's Third Law  12.1.3 牛顿第三定律

Newton's third law is often misunderstood in spite of being the one most often quoted. It has a certain zen-like justice to it.5
牛顿第三定律虽然被引用次数最多，却常常被误解。它本身就带有一种禅宗般的正义感。5

Newton's Third Law  牛顿第三定律
To every action there is always an equal and opposite reaction. Or, the forces of two bodies on each other are always equal and are directed in opposite directions.
任何作用力都必然伴随一个大小相等、方向相反的反作用力。或者说，两个物体相互作用的力总是大小相等、方向相反的。

This law basically says that there is no such thing as a single unilateral force. If object A pushes or pulls on object B , then object B always pushes or pulls back on object A with a force of the same magnitude but opposite direction. If gravity is pulling me towards Earth, it's also pulling Earth towards me! A force is always part of an interaction between two bodies.
这条定律的基本意思是，不存在单一的单向力。如果物体 A 推或拉物体 B ，那么物体 B 总是会以大小相同但方向相反的力推或拉物体 A 。如果引力将我拉向地球，那么它也会将地球拉向我！力始终是两个物体相互作用的一部分。

In diagrams, we often draw a force as an arrow, since it is a vector. But really, these diagrams would be more accurate if both ends of the arrow had arrowheads. When we leave off the other side of the arrow, it's because it is acting on an object in which we have no interest. When you see a single-sided arrow that represents a force in a diagram, you can always fill in the other half in your mind.
在图中，我们经常把力画成箭头，因为它是矢量。但实际上，如果箭头两端都有箭头，这些图会更准确。当我们省略箭头的另一侧时，是因为它作用于一个我们不感兴趣的物体上。当你在图中看到表示力的单侧箭头时，你总是可以在脑海中填补另一侧的空白。

One source of misunderstanding of Newton's third law is the word “reaction.” The purpose of this word is to describe the forces as being in opposition to one another. It is not meant to imply a causal link between them; neither force is a “cause” or “effect.” The two opposing forces act simultaneously and, so far as the laws of physics are concerned, have equal status.
对牛顿第三定律的一个误解是“反作用”一词。该词的目的是描述力彼此相反的状态，并不意味着它们之间存在因果关系；两种力都不是“原因”或“结果”。这两种相反的力同时作用，就物理定律而言，它们的地位是平等的。

But aside from this mistaken inference of cause and effect, the third law is just plain counterintuitive. Let's say a guy named Moe pushes a box forward on the ground. The box weighs twice as much as Moe, and he has placed it on a cart that rolls with very little friction. According to Newton's third law, the box pushes back on Moe. But then why does the box accelerate and Moe doesn't? It doesn't look like there are “equal and opposite actions” happening here.
但撇开这种错误的因果推论不谈，牛顿第三定律本身就违反直觉。假设一个名叫莫的人在地上向前推一个箱子。箱子的重量是莫的两倍，他把箱子放在一辆摩擦力很小的推车上。根据牛顿第三定律，箱子会反推莫。但为什么箱子会加速，而莫却没有呢？这看起来似乎不存在“大小相等、方向相反的作用力”。

Conundrums such as these are always resolved by considering all the forces acting on both bodies. In the example just discussed, Moe is not floating in midair, or else he would have been accelerated backwards just as Newton's third law predicts he would. (Consider what would happen if Moe and the box were on ice.) No, Moe is standing on the ground. Through the force of friction, Moe pushes against the Earth and the Earth pushes back on Moe. In fact, if we assume that Moe makes some forward progress instead of just being stuck there grunting, then the force of the Earth pushing against him must exceed the force of the box pushing back against him, and he accelerates forward. This is illustrated in Figure 12.3.
这类难题总是可以通过考虑作用于两个物体上的所有力来解决。在刚才讨论的例子中，莫并非漂浮在半空中，否则他就会像牛顿第三运动定律预测的那样，向后加速。（想象一下，如果莫和盒子在冰上会发生什么。）不，莫站在地上。通过摩擦力，莫推着地球，地球也推着莫。事实上，如果我们假设莫向前移动了一些，而不是只是被困在那里咕哝，那么地球对他的推力必定会超过盒子对他的推力，于是他向前加速。如图 12.3 所示。

Figure 12.3  图 12.3The four forces involved in Moe pushing the box
莫伊推箱子所涉及的四种力量

An inquisitive reader might wonder about the previous scenario, “Why doesn't the Earth then accelerate?” The short answer is, “It does!” A medium-length answer is, “It does, in the short run.” For the full length answer, we have to wait until Section 12.3, which tells us a little bit about momentum.
好奇的读者可能会对之前的情况感到疑惑：“为什么地球不加速旋转？” 简短的回答是：“它会！” 中等长度的回答是：“在短期内它会加速旋转。” 要得到完整的答案，我们必须等到第 12.3 节，其中会稍微介绍一下动量。

Of course, these theoretical questions are certainly interesting to ponder, but what practical application is there for Newton's third law? The most important application, for our purposes, is the justification to simplify a rigid body and treat it as a single particle. For example, earlier we considered the forces acting on a large beam in a skyscraper. What if the beam is not a single solid piece, but instead it is really two beams that have been bolted together? Then really what is happening is that forces push down on the top part of the beam, which pushes down on the bottom part of the beam, which pushes down on the Earth. Likewise, the Earth is pushing back up on the bottom part of the beam, which pushes up on the top part of the beam.
当然，这些理论问题确实值得思考，但牛顿第三定律有什么实际应用呢？就我们的目的而言，最重要的应用是证明简化刚体并将其视为单个粒子的合理性。例如，之前我们考虑了作用在摩天大楼一根大梁上的力。如果这根梁不是一整块实心的，而是两根用螺栓连接在一起的梁，会怎么样？那么实际发生的情况是，力向下推梁的顶部，顶部向下推梁的底部，底部向下推地球。同样，地球向上推梁的底部，底部向上推梁的顶部。

But why stop there? Isn't any object actually composed of not just two or three pieces, but trillions of molecules? How can we possibly calculate all these complicated quantum-electrical forces? This is where Newton's third law comes in. We are justified in the treatment of this spliced beam as a single rigid body, and we can ignore all the internal forces, provided that the body stays rigid, which means that all pairs of points within the object maintain a fixed distance from each other. In this situation, the parts are not accelerating relative to each other, and this means that the internal forces must be exactly balanced. In other words, all the internal forces cancel each other out and thus make no contribution to the net force, which is why we can ignore them. Of course, to the extent that the pieces do accelerate relative to each other, any calculations we make ignoring the internal forces will be inaccurate. If the bending or compression of the object is very slight, then our calculations will not be perfect, but they will be very close; if the object breaks apart, then our calculations will be meaningless.
但为什么要止步于此呢？任何物体实际上不都是由两三块，而是数万亿个分子组成的吗？我们怎么可能计算出所有这些复杂的量子电力呢？这时，牛顿第三运动定律就派上用场了。我们有理由将这根拼接梁视为一个单一的刚体，并且只要物体保持刚性，我们就可以忽略所有内力，这意味着物体内部的所有点对彼此之间都保持固定的距离。在这种情况下，各个部分不会相对加速，这意味着内力必须完全平衡。换句话说，所有内力相互抵消，因此对净力没有任何贡献，这就是我们可以忽略它们的原因。当然，如果各个部分确实相对加速，那么我们忽略内力进行的任何计算都将是不准确的。如果物体的弯曲或压缩非常轻微，那么我们的计算结果就不会完美，但会非常接近完美；如果物体破裂，那么我们的计算将毫无意义。

We can generalize arguments such as this even further to the case where the parts are moving relative to each other. Of course, an object with moving internal parts is the opposite of a rigid body; however, we'll see that in many respects we are still able treat these complicated systems as “particles.” Section 12.3 discusses this idea and how it allows us to resolve the conundrum of Moe and his box.
我们可以将这样的论证进一步推广到部件相对运动的情况。当然，内部部件运动的物体与刚体相反；然而，我们将看到，在很多方面，我们仍然可以将这些复杂系统视为“粒子”。第 12.3 节讨论了这一思想，以及它如何帮助我们解决莫伊和他的盒子的难题。

12.2Some Simple Force Laws
12.2 一些简单的力定律

Many different types of forces are at work in our universe.6 In a real-time simulation, we often ignore certain forces, make approximations to them, and even invent fictional7 forces to achieve a desired effect (such as forcing a trajectory to obey an animator's constraints, or helping the AI or the player hit the target). Although our guiding principle is always f =m a , the methods used to define f can vary greatly.
我们的宇宙中存在着许多不同类型的力。6 在实时模拟中，我们经常会忽略某些力，对其进行近似计算，甚至虚构一些力来达到预期效果（例如，强制轨迹遵循动画师的约束，或帮助 AI 或玩家击中目标）。虽然我们的指导原则始终是 f =m a ，但定义 f 的方法却千差万别。

This section discusses three important forces that exist in the real world and are often used in physics simulations. Gravity, friction, and springs are the subjects of Section 12.2.1, Section 12.2.2, and Section 12.2.3, respectively. Of course, a computer simulation may need to consider many more real-world forces, such as buoyancy, drag, or lift. The goal of this book is to give an overview of the most important topics and not to be exhaustive; however, sources that cover these types of forces are listed in the suggested reading in Section 12.7.
本节讨论现实世界中存在的三种重要力，它们经常用于物理模拟。重力、摩擦力和弹簧分别在第 12.2.1 节、第 12.2.2 节和第 12.2.3 节中讨论。当然，计算机模拟可能需要考虑更多现实世界的力，例如浮力、阻力或升力。本书旨在概述最重要的主题，而非详尽无遗；不过，涵盖这些类型力的资料已在第 12.7 节的推荐阅读中列出。

One other extremely important force that appears in physics simulations is the contact force, also known as a normal force. This is the force that prevents objects from penetrating each other. When a box is resting on a table, the force the table exerts on the box, counteracting the force of gravity and preventing the box from accelerating downwards, is called a contact force. Contact forces in a physics engine are inherently tied up with the engine's method for resolving collisions and are usually handled in a way that forms a compromise between the stability of the simulation and physical reality. As such, the details for how contact forces are computed can vary from one physics engine to another; indeed, resolving collisions is a very active area of research.
物理模拟中出现的另一种极其重要的力是接触力，也称为法向力。这种力阻止物体相互穿透。当一个盒子放在桌子上时，桌子施加在盒子上的力，抵消重力并阻止盒子向下加速，这被称为接触力。物理引擎中的接触力本质上与引擎解决碰撞的方法紧密相关，并且通常以在模拟稳定性和物理现实之间形成折衷的方式处理。因此，不同物理引擎计算接触力的细节可能有所不同；事实上，解决碰撞是一个非常活跃的研究领域。

12.2.1Gravitational Force
12.2.1 引力

In Principia, Newton stated all sorts of laws in addition to the three for which he is the most famous. One such law, which he discovered through analysis of the motions of the planets, is the law of universal gravitation, which states that all objects in the universe feel an attractive force to each other. This force is proportionate to the product of their masses and inversely proportionate to the square of the distance between the objects and can be calculated by Equation (12.3).
在《自然哲学的数学原理》中，牛顿除了阐述他最著名的三条定律外，还阐述了其他各种定律。其中一条定律是他通过分析行星运动发现的，那就是万有引力定律。该定律指出，宇宙中的所有物体都相互产生吸引力。这种吸引力与物体质量的乘积成正比，与物体之间距离的平方成反比，可以用公式 (12.3) 计算。

Law of Universal Gravitation
万有引力定律
(12.3)f=G m1m2 d2.

In this equation, f is the magnitude of the force, m1 and m2 are the masses of the two objects, and d is the distance between their centers of mass. (We'll have more to say about exactly what the center of mass is in Section 12.3.2.) G is a physical constant of the universe, approximately equal to 6.673×10 −11   N   m 2  kg −2 .
在这个方程中， f 是力的大小， m1 和 m2 是两个物体的质量， d 是它们质心之间的距离。（我们将在 12.3.2 节中详细解释质心的具体含义。） G 是宇宙的一个物理常数，约等于 6.673×10 −11   N   m 2  kg −2 。

The law of universal gravitational attraction is very helpful if you want to understand planetary motion or the tides, or just need a cheesy pick-up line.8 However, most simulations are confined to a fairly small region close to Earth's surface. When we make the typical assumption that one Cartesian axis points “down,” we are ignoring the curvature of Earth and also locking in the direction of the force of gravity to a constant. It's also common to ignore the slight decrease in the strength of gravity that occurs at higher altitudes, and assume a constant value for d . Thus, if we let m1 stand for Earth's mass, then the only variable in Equation (12.3) is m2 , the mass of the object being simulated. In most video games, the force of gravity is computed using Equation (12.4).
如果您想了解行星运动或潮汐，或者只是需要一句俗气的搭讪台词，万有引力定律将非常有用。8 然而，大多数模拟都局限于靠近地球表面的一个相当小的区域。当我们做出一个笛卡尔轴指向“下方”的典型假设时，我们忽略了地球的曲率，也将重力方向锁定为一个常数。我们通常会忽略在较高海拔处重力强度的轻微下降，并假设 d 为一个常数。因此，如果我们让 m1 代表地球的质量，那么方程 (12.3) 中唯一的变量就是 m2 ，即被模拟物体的质量。在大多数视频游戏中，重力是使用方程 (12.4) 计算的。

Video Game Gravity  电子游戏《地心引力》
(12.4) f =m g .

In Equation (12.4), m is the mass of the object and g is a constant vector pointing in the downward direction. Notice that the force of gravity is proportional to the mass, but Newton's second law says that the acceleration due to any force is inversely proportional to mass. Therefore, g specifies the acceleration due to gravity for all objects in free fall. (Notice the similarity between Equation (12.4) and Newton's second law, f =m a .)
在公式 (12.4) 中， m 表示物体的质量， g 表示指向下方的常数矢量。注意，重力与质量成正比，但牛顿第二定律指出，任何力产生的加速度都与质量成反比。因此， g 表示所有自由落体物体的重力加速度。（注意公式 (12.4) 与牛顿第二定律 f =m a 的相似性。）

Chapter 11 told you what the magnitude of g is in the real world, but let's see if we can derive it from the universal law of gravitation. Earth's mass is approximately m1=5.98×10 24   kg , and its mean radius is 6,371 km:
第 11 章告诉了你现实世界中 g 的大小，但让我们看看能否从万有引力定律中推导出它。地球的质量约为 m1=5.98×10 24   kg ，其平均半径为 6,371 千米：

Calculating the force of gravity near Earth's surface from the law of universal gravitation
根据万有引力定律计算地球表面附近的重力
f=G m1m2 d2= (6.673×10 −11 N   m 2 kg 2 ) (5.98×10 24   kg )m2 (6.371×106  m )2 ≈(9.83  N )m2 kg ≈ (9.83  m s 2) m2.

But wait, this value is larger than the value of 9.81 quoted earlier! The reason for the difference is that, while Earth's gravity provides a centripetal force, its rotation creates an apparent centrifugal force, which partly counteracts gravity. We calculated the magnitude of the acceleration required to keep objects from spinning out into space in Section 11.8. At the equator, Earth's rotation requires that gravity provide a centripetal acceleration of 0.03369  m   s −2 . Thus a small part of the force of gravity that makes objects feel heavy is being counteracted by the spinning of Earth, which makes them feel lighter.
但是等等，这个值比之前引用的 9.81 还要大！造成这种差异的原因是，地球引力虽然提供了向心力，但其自转却产生了表观离心力，这部分抵消了重力。我们在第 11.8 节中计算了阻止物体旋转到太空所需的加速度大小。在赤道处，地球自转需要重力提供 0.03369  m   s −2 的向心加速度。因此，使物体感觉沉重的重力的一小部分被地球自转所抵消，从而使物体感觉更轻。

Subtracting this apparent centrifugal force from the force of gravity gives us 9.83−0.03369≈9.796 , but now the value is too small, not the 9.81 we were looking for. The reason is that gravity exhibits variations in magnitude over Earth's surface. The biggest source of this variation is the centripetal acceleration we have just calculated; it varies with latitude. We computed its magnitude assuming r was Earth's radius; the resulting value for gravity of 9.796 is actually the correct strength of gravity at the equator. As the latitude increases and we move towards the poles, the radius r of the circular path (which has constant latitude) decreases. At the poles, the radius shrinks to zero, and objects rotate but do not move in a circular path. Thus there is no apparent centrifugal force at the poles, and the force of gravity is equal to the 9.83 value we computed above. The value 9.81 is known as the “standard value,” and is the average force of gravity at sea level at a latitude of about 45°.
从重力中减去这个表观离心力，我们得到 9.83−0.03369≈9.796 ，但是现在这个值太小了，不是我们想要的 9.81。原因是重力的大小在地球表面会发生变化。这种变化的最大来源是我们刚刚计算的向心加速度；它随纬度而变化。我们计算它的大小时假设 r 是地球半径；得到的重力值 9.796 实际上是赤道处的正确重力强度。随着纬度的增加，我们向两极移动，圆形路径（纬度恒定）的半径 r 会减小。在两极，半径缩小到零，物体会旋转但不会沿圆形路径运动。因此，两极没有表观离心力，重力等于我们上面计算的 9.83 值。 9.81 这个值被称为“标准值”，是纬度约 45° 的海平面平均重力。

Now that we've discussed at some length the strength of gravity in the real world, let's talk about how this number is often completely irrelevant in video games. In certain genres, such as racing or flight simulators, realism is important. However, in most other video games, the first law of video game physics applies. (Hey, Newton made up some laws, so why can't we?)
既然我们已经详细讨论了现实世界中的引力强度，那么我们来谈谈这个数字在电子游戏中通常完全无关紧要的原因。在某些类型的游戏中，例如赛车或飞行模拟器，真实感很重要。然而，在大多数其他电子游戏中，电子游戏物理第一定律仍然适用。（嘿，牛顿创造了一些定律，我们为什么不能呢？）

First Law of Video Game Physics
电子游戏物理第一定律
Reality is overrated.   现实被高估了。

For example, first-person shooters are notorious for poor jumping mechanics. The most important reason is probably the fundamental fact that you cannot see your feet, yet some first-person games have for some reason added jumping puzzles. But even many third-person shooters that adopt an over-the-shoulder camera also have jumping mechanics that just don't feel right. Why? In most first-person shooters, when you jump, you are given an initial burst of upward velocity, and then your position is simulated just like every other airborne object in the world, using gravity, which causes your motion to be parabolic. Compare this to the jump mechanic in most third-person action games. Most of these games do not simulate jumps using a constant acceleration. Instead, your character will spring up almost instantaneously after you hit the button, and reach a maximum height very quickly. In many games, the character will hover at that maximum height for a duration, and then slam back down on the ground as quickly as it rose up, perhaps leaving a crater behind. This is clearly not physically accurate, but then again, neither is being able to jump two or three times your own height, steer in midair, or double jump. When it comes to jumping in video games, reality is not just overrated, it's completely ignored. It just doesn't feel right.
例如，第一人称射击游戏以糟糕的跳跃机制而臭名昭著。最重要的原因可能是玩家看不到自己的脚，但有些第一人称游戏却不知何故添加了跳跃谜题。但即使是许多采用过肩视角的第三人称射击游戏，其跳跃机制也感觉不太对劲。为什么？在大多数第一人称射击游戏中，跳跃时，玩家会获得一个向上的初始速度，然后系统会像世界上其他空中物体一样，利用重力模拟玩家的位置，使玩家的运动呈抛物线状。将此与大多数第三人称动作游戏中的跳跃机制进行比较。大多数这类游戏并非使用恒定加速度来模拟跳跃。相反，玩家的角色会在按下按钮后几乎瞬间弹起，并迅速达到最大高度。在许多游戏中，角色会在最大高度悬停一段时间，然后以与上升速度相同的速度重重落回地面，留下一个弹坑。这显然不符合物理规律，但话说回来，能够跳到自身身高两三倍的高度、在空中转向或二段跳也同样不符合物理规律。在电子游戏中，跳跃不仅被高估，甚至被完全忽略。感觉就是不对劲。

If simulating a jump mechanic using gravity makes for a bad jump mechanic, simulating a jump mechanic using a value of 9.8  m / s 2 is even worse. The basic problem is that most players expect a jump to take a certain amount of time but also expect to be capable of jumping to unrealistic heights. When real-world gravity is used to attain these heights, the player is in the air too long, and it feels “floaty.” Many arcade racing games also increase gravity to get the car back on the ground more quickly. Whether it be racing games or character games, the player wants to be in full control again as quickly as possible, and waiting for real-world gravity to get them back down usually takes too long. And then there are other racing games that use a value of gravity that is less than the real world value, to facilitate unrealistic jumps at realistic vehicle speeds.
如果使用重力模拟跳跃机制会导致跳跃机制不佳，那么使用 9.8  m / s 2 值模拟跳跃机制则更糟糕。基本问题是大多数玩家都认为跳跃需要一定的时间，但也期望能够跳到不切实际的高度。当使用真实世界的重力来达到这些高度时，玩家会在空中停留太长时间，感觉“飘飘欲仙”。许多街机赛车游戏也会增加重力，让汽车更快地回到地面。无论是赛车游戏还是角色游戏，玩家都希望尽快重新完全控制汽车，而等待真实世界的重力让他们重新落下通常需要很长时间。还有一些赛车游戏使用小于真实世界的重力值，以便在真实的车速下进行不切实际的跳跃。

There are also reasons to fiddle with gravity for non-player-character objects as well. Sometimes real-world gravity can create an “objects made of styrofoam” feeling for simulated objects in general,9 so gravity is increased to get an object to tip over and come to rest more quickly. In other situations, an artificially low value of gravity can make a large object seem even more massive (especially when accompanied by the right sound effects), because acceleration on Earth is constant and is one of a few cues humans instinctively use to establish an absolute scale for objects in the distance.10
对于非玩家角色的物体，调整重力也是有原因的。有时，现实世界的重力会让模拟物体产生一种“泡沫塑料”的感觉，9 因此需要增加重力，使物体更快地倾倒并静止下来。在其他情况下，人为降低重力值会使大型物体看起来更加巨大（尤其是在配上合适的音效时），因为地球上的加速度是恒定的，这是人类本能地用来为远处的物体建立绝对比例的少数线索之一。10

Hopefully, while reading the preceding design discussion you absorbed a general message rather than focusing on our specific opinions. What “feels right” is a subjective matter; furthermore—and this is the key point—it is based more on player expectation than physical reality. In the end, what matters most in a video game is not what's going on in the CPU or even on the screen, but what is going on in the player's mind. And the human mind is highly susceptible to suggestion. When creating video games, always remember that the quest for realism should never be an end unto itself, but rather a successful video game will harness realism only where it serves the ultimate goal, which is entertainment. In fact, realism is quite often opposed to this goal. Video game makers (especially programmers!) often get these priorities confused and end up creating an impressive technical demo that isn't any fun.
希望您在阅读前面的设计讨论时，能够理解一个普遍的理念，而不是仅仅关注我们的具体观点。“感觉正确”是一个主观问题；而且——关键在于——它更多地基于玩家的期望，而非物理现实。归根结底，电子游戏中最重要的并非 CPU 或屏幕上发生的事情，而是玩家脑海中发生的事情。而人类的思维很容易受到暗示的影响。在创作电子游戏时，请始终牢记，追求真实感永远不应成为最终目标，成功的电子游戏只会在服务于最终目标——娱乐性——的地方运用真实感。事实上，真实感往往与这一目标背道而驰。电子游戏制作者（尤其是程序员！）经常混淆这些优先级，最终创作出令人印象深刻但毫无趣味性的技术演示。

12.2.2Frictional Forces  12.2.2 摩擦力

If we take an object such as a bowl of petunias and slide it along a surface, we know that it will eventually come to a stop. We also know that if we place this bowl on a surface that isn't quite level, it won't necessarily slide downhill unless the angle of inclination exceeds a certain threshold. These two phenomena are slightly different aspects of the force of friction. We are accustomed to thinking of friction as an onerous enemy of productivity, the evil cause of wear on machines and more frequent trips to the gas station. But keep in mind that without friction, we wouldn't be able to walk across a room or pick up a child (or a bowl of petunias). Without friction, our cars might have better fuel efficiency, but the transmission wouldn't work and the tires would spin in place instead of propelling the car forward.
如果我们拿着一个物体，比如一碗矮牵牛，让它在一个表面上滑动，我们知道它最终会停下来。我们还知道，如果我们把这个碗放在一个不太平的表面上，除非倾斜角度超过某个阈值，否则它不一定会滑下坡路。这两种现象是摩擦力略有不同的方面。我们习惯于认为摩擦力是生产力的死敌，是机器磨损和更频繁地去加油站的罪魁祸首。但请记住，如果没有摩擦力，我们就无法穿过房间或抱起一个孩子（或一碗矮牵牛）。没有摩擦力，我们的汽车可能会有更好的燃油效率，但变速器将无法工作，轮胎只会在原地打转，而不是推动汽车前进。

Here we consider the two modes of the standard dry friction model, which is sometimes called Coulomb friction. Although several thinkers contributed to our understanding of friction, Charles-Augustin de Coulomb (1736–1806) is the guy who got his name to stick. When an object is at rest on top of another object, a certain amount of force is required to get it unstuck and set it in motion. If any less force is applied to the object, the force of friction will push back with a counteracting force up to some maximum amount. This type of friction is known as static friction, and it prevents bowls of petunias sitting on slightly inclined tables from sliding off. Once static friction is overcome and the object is moving, friction continues to push against the relative motion of the two surfaces, but the magnitude of this force, known as kinetic friction, is less than that of static friction. Kinetic friction is what causes a bowl of petunias to eventually come to a stop after we set it in motion.
这里我们讨论标准干摩擦模型的两种模式，这种模型有时也称为库仑摩擦。虽然许多思想家都对我们对摩擦的理解做出了贡献，但查尔斯·奥古斯丁·德·库仑（1736-1806）的名字才得以流传。当一个物体静止在另一个物体之上时，需要一定的力才能使其脱离粘连并开始运动。如果对物体施加较小的力，摩擦力就会以反作用力将其推回，反作用力的最大值不超过某个值。这种摩擦力称为静摩擦力，它可以防止放在略微倾斜的桌子上的矮牵牛花盆滑落。一旦静摩擦力被克服，物体开始运动，摩擦力会继续阻碍两个表面的相对运动，但这种力的大小（称为动摩擦力）小于静摩擦力。动摩擦力就是我们让一盆矮牵牛花开始运动后最终停下来的原因。

Friction is the result of complicated interactions at the microscopic level, and so it is somewhat surprising that its macroscopic behavior can be described by relatively simple equations. Let's consider static friction first. Like any force, static friction is a vector. The direction of static friction is always in the direction that opposes any forces that would otherwise cause objects to move relative to each other. This might seems a bit like cheating (“How does the friction always know the correct direction to push?”), but remember that the force is actually the aggregate result of many electrical forces acting at the microscopic level. The forces are the result of molecular bonds that have formed between the objects as they came in contact, and these bonds need a force to pull them apart.
摩擦力是微观层面复杂相互作用的结果，因此令人惊讶的是，它的宏观行为可以用相对简单的方程来描述。我们先来考虑静摩擦力。与任何力一样，静摩擦力是一个矢量。静摩擦力的方向始终与任何会导致物体相对运动的力的方向相反。这听起来可能有点像作弊（“摩擦力如何总是知道正确的推动方向？”），但请记住，这种力实际上是许多电力在微观层面作用的集合结果。这些力是物体接触时之间形成的分子键的结果，而这些分子键需要一种力来将它们拉开。

A good approximation for the maximum magnitude of static friction is computed with Equation (12.5).
使用公式 (12.5) 可以很好地近似计算静摩擦的最大值。

Static Friction  静摩擦力
(12.5)fs=μsn.

The dimensionless constant μs is known as the coefficient of static friction, and n is the magnitude of the normal force. Let's talk about each of these in more detail.
无量纲常数 μs 称为静摩擦系数， n 是法向力的大小。让我们更详细地讨论一下这两个常数。

From our perspective, μs is certainly the easier of the two to deal with: just look it up in a table! Table 12.1 shows just such a table. Note that we are jumping ahead a bit and showing coefficients for both static and kinetic friction. Ignore the kinetic friction column for now.
从我们的角度来看， μs 显然更容易处理：直接查表就行了！表 12.1 就是这样一个表格。请注意，我们稍微跳过了前面的内容，列出了静摩擦系数和动摩擦系数。暂时忽略动摩擦系数这一列。

Material 1  材料 1 Material 2  材料 2 μs (Static)   μs （静态） μk (Kinetic)   μk （动能）
Aluminum  铝 Steel  钢 0.61 0.47
Copper  铜 Steel  钢 0.53 0.36
Leather  皮革 Metal  金属 0.4 0.2
Rubber  橡皮 Asphalt (dry)  沥青（干） 0.9 0.5–0.8
Rubber  橡皮 Asphalt (wet)  沥青（湿） 0.25–0.75
Rubber  橡皮 Concrete (dry)  混凝土（干） 1.0 0.6–0.85
Rubber  橡皮 Concrete (wet)  混凝土（湿） 0.30 0.45–0.75
Steel  钢 Steel  钢 0.80
Steel  钢 Teflon  特氟龙 0.04
Teflon  特氟龙 Teflon  特氟龙 0.04
Wood  木头 Concrete  具体的 0.62
Wood  木头 Clean metal  清洁金属 0.2–0.6
Wood  木头 Ice  冰 0.05
Wood  木头 Wood  木头 0.25–0.5
Wood (waxed)  木材（上蜡） Dry snow  干雪 0.04
Table 12.1  表 12.1Static and kinetic coefficients of friction
静摩擦系数和动摩擦系数

Of course, somebody actually has to fill out these tables! The methods for obtaining these data are interesting and rather elegant but they are not our primary concern here. What is very important for us is that the coefficients of static and kinetic friction depend on the properties of both interacting surfaces. In other words, Table 12.1 is indexed not by a single surface type, but by a pair of interacting surfaces. So, for example, although using this table we can find the coefficient of static friction for rubber against asphalt, we cannot use this information to say anything about, for example, rubber against ice, or wood against asphalt. The coefficient of static friction for each pair of surfaces has to be measured experimentally because of the complexity of the microscopic interactions.
当然，这些表格确实需要有人来填写！获取这些数据的方法很有趣，也相当精妙，但它们不是我们这里主要关注的。对我们来说，非常重要的是，静摩擦系数和动摩擦系数取决于相互作用表面的性质。换句话说，表 12.1 不是由单一的表面类型索引，而是由一对相互作用的表面索引。因此，例如，虽然我们可以使用此表找到橡胶与沥青的静摩擦系数，但我们不能用这些信息来说明橡胶与冰或木材与沥青等相互作用。由于微观相互作用的复杂性，每对表面的静摩擦系数必须通过实验测量。

Also, note that Equation (12.5) tells us the maximum strength of the static friction force. The actual force exerted at any instant will meet the magnitude of any forces acting on the objects that tend to induce lateral relative motion, up to this maximum. Once this maximum is exceeded, the static friction ceases to operate, and kinetic friction takes over.
另外，请注意，公式 (12.5) 给出了静摩擦力的最大值。任何时刻施加的实际力都会与作用于物体上任何倾向于引起横向相对运动的力的大小相等，直至达到最大值。一旦超过最大值，静摩擦力就失效，动摩擦力取而代之。

The other factor in Equation (12.5) is the magnitude of the normal force, which is the force acting perpendicular to the surfaces that prevent them from penetrating each other. One common situation occurs when an object (such as a bowl of petunias) is resting on top of another object (such as a table). The normal force in this case is simply the force required to counteract gravity. To be more precise, it is the force required to counteract the component of gravity that acts perpendicular to the surfaces and wants to smash them together. If the table is at an incline, then we can separate gravity into a normal component and a lateral component, as shown in Figure 12.4. (Inside a computer, we'd probably describe the orientation of the table with a normal vector, and use the dot product to separate gravity into the relative and normal components, as we described in Section 2.11.2.) Since the bowl and the table do not accelerate relative to each other, we know that the normal force of the table pushing against the bowl must be exactly equal to the normal component of the force of gravity pulling the bowl towards the table.
公式 (12.5) 中的另一个因素是法向力的大小，法向力是垂直于表面作用的力，阻止物体相互穿透。一种常见的情况是，一个物体（例如一碗矮牵牛花）放在另一个物体（例如桌子）上。在这种情况下，法向力就是抵消重力所需的力。更准确地说，它是抵消垂直于表面作用并试图将它们撞在一起的重力分力所需的力。如果桌子是倾斜的，那么我们可以将重力分为法向分力和横向分力，如图 12.4 所示。 （在计算机内部，我们可能会用法线矢量来描述桌子的方向，并使用点积将重力分离为相对分量和法线分量，正如我们在第 2.11.2 节中所述。）由于碗和桌子彼此之间没有相对加速度，我们知道桌子推碗的法线力必须恰好等于将碗拉向桌子的重力的法线分量。

Figure 12.4  图 12.4 Free-body diagrams of a bowl of petunias on a table at various angles of inclination.
桌子上一碗矮牵牛以各种倾斜角度摆放的自由体图。

Figure 12.4 shows several free-body diagrams of identical bowls of petunias resting on tables at various angles of inclination. Notice that in each figure, the force of gravity acting on the bowl, labeled g , is the same. The normal and lateral components of gravity have been broken out in blue. The actual force of static friction is the black vector labeled f s . On the left, the maximum amount of friction available is labeled “max f s ,” in the middle and right-hand images the maximum amount of friction is being applied.
图 12.4 展示了几幅相同的矮牵牛花盆以不同倾斜角度放置在桌子上的自由体受力图。请注意，在每幅图中，作用在花盆上的重力（标记为 g ）是相同的。重力的法向分量和横向分量已用蓝色标出。实际的静摩擦力是标记为 f s 的黑色矢量。左侧图中，可用的最大摩擦力标记为“max f s ”，中间和右侧图中则表示施加了最大摩擦力。

In the first scenario, there is more friction available than necessary to stop the sliding. However, as the angle of inclination increases, the normal component of gravity decreases, which reduces the amount of friction available. Meanwhile, as the perpendicular component of gravity is decreasing, the lateral component is increasing, which makes the bowl want to slide. The force of static friction must counter this lateral component if the bowl is to remain in equilibrium. The center image shows the critical angle at which the lateral force of gravity is exactly equal to the to the maximum amount of friction. On the right, we imagine that we have tilted the table while holding the bowl in place, and then let go of the bowl. The maximum available friction is being applied, but it's less than was available in the center picture due to the decrease in the normal force and isn't enough to overcome the increased lateral component of gravity. Just after this picture was taken, friction switched from static mode into kinetic mode, the bowl slid off the table and shattered, and a cartoon cleaning robot scurried in through a little door in the wall to clean up themess.
在第一种情况下，可用的摩擦力大于停止滑动所需的摩擦力。然而，随着倾斜角度的增加，重力的法向分力减小，从而减少了可用的摩擦力。同时，随着重力的垂直分力减小，横向分力增大，这使得碗有滑动的趋势。如果碗要保持平衡，静摩擦力必须抵消这个横向分力。中间的图像显示了临界角，此时重力的横向力恰好等于最大摩擦力。在右侧，我们假设我们握住碗，将桌子倾斜，然后松开碗。此时施加了最大可用摩擦力，但由于法向力减小，摩擦力小于中间图中的摩擦力，不足以克服增加的横向分力。这张照片刚拍完，摩擦就从静态模式转变为动态模式，碗从桌子上滑落摔碎，一个卡通清洁机器人从墙上的一个小门跑进来清理现场。

Calculating kinetic friction is essentially identical to static friction. The only difference is that we replace the subscript s with a k .
计算动摩擦力本质上与计算静摩擦力相同。唯一的区别在于我们将下标 s 替换为 k 。

Kinetic Friction  动摩擦
(12.6)fk=μkn.

The direction of the force of kinetic friction is always opposed to the relative motion of the surfaces. (Remember, according to Newton's third law, there are actually two forces, one pushing against the bowl, and the other against the table, and they are in opposite directions.) As we said earlier, the coefficient of kinetic friction is usually less than the coefficient of static friction. Thus, if we increase the angle of the table ever so slowly so that static friction is just overcome, the petunias will begin to accelerate, based on this difference between kinetic and static friction. Coulomb's primary contribution to the theory, sometimes called Coulomb's law of friction, was that the force of kinetic friction does not depend on the relative velocities of the surfaces, so, unlike static friction, there is no distinction between the effective force and the maximum force.
动摩擦力的方向始终与表面的相对运动方向相反。（记住，根据牛顿第三定律，实际上存在两种力，一种推碗，另一种推桌面，它们的方向相反。）如前所述，动摩擦系数通常小于静摩擦系数。因此，如果我们缓慢地增加桌面的角度，直到刚好克服静摩擦力，矮牵牛就会开始加速，这是基于动摩擦力和静摩擦力之间的差异。库仑对该理论（有时称为库仑摩擦定律）的主要贡献在于，动摩擦力与表面的相对速度无关，因此，与静摩擦力不同，动摩擦力没有有效力和最大力之间的区别。

Notice that the amount of area that the two objects are in contact does not appear in Equations (12.5) or (12.6). For example, let's say we repot the petunias in a taller bowl with a smaller footprint but the same weight. We have reduced the surface area where the bowl and table are in contact, but all of the forces depicted in the free-body diagrams in Figure 12.4 remain the same. Doing this would not change the angle at which the bowl would begin to slide! Although it might seem like a larger surface area would give the objects more to “grab” with, this is offset by the decrease in pressure, since the same total normal force is now distributed over a smaller contact area. Now, a very tall bowl may begin to tip over before it begins to slide. But this is a matter of rotation, the increase in the tendency to rotate being caused by an increase in the lever arm resulting in a greater torque. We cover these issues in Section 12.5.
请注意，两个物体接触的面积并未出现在公式 (12.5) 或 (12.6) 中。例如，假设我们将矮牵牛移栽到一个更高的碗中，碗的占地面积更小，但重量相同。我们减少了碗和桌子的接触表面积，但图 12.4 中自由体图所示的所有力保持不变。这样做并不会改变碗开始滑动的角度！虽然更大的表面积似乎会让物体有更多“抓取”的空间，但这会被压力的降低所抵消，因为相同的总法向力现在分布在更小的接触面积上。现在，一个非常高的碗可能会在开始滑动之前先倾倒。但这与旋转有关，旋转趋势的增加是由于杠杆臂的增加导致了更大的扭矩。我们将在 12.5 节中讨论这些问题。

12.2.3Spring Forces  12.2.3 弹簧力

There's one more class of force that is important enough to discuss in its own section: the forces exerted by a spring disturbed from its equilibrium position. Why do we discuss this admittedly peculiar class of force? Have springs suddenly become prominent features in video games and their accurate simulation an important gameplay feature? Actually, yes. Even if you don't see very many literal springs in a video game, there are likely very many “virtual springs” at work. Springs exhibit a general behavior that is very useful for enforcing constraints, preventing objects from penetrating, and the like.
还有一类力非常重要，值得单独讨论：弹簧偏离平衡位置时产生的力。我们为什么要讨论这种公认的特殊力呢？弹簧是否突然成为电子游戏中的突出特征，而其精确模拟是否已成为一项重要的游戏特色？事实上，是的。即使你在电子游戏中很少看到真正的弹簧，也可能有很多“虚拟弹簧”在起作用。弹簧表现出一种普遍的行为，这对于强制约束、防止物体穿透等非常有用。

This section presents the classic equations of motion for damped and undamped oscillation. It covers undamped oscillation first, and then damped. It's often the case in a video game that programmers use a virtual spring (often in the form of a spring-damper system) when really what they are using is a control system. There are certain advantages to be had when the physical nature of the problem is dropped and we think of it purely in mathematical terms. (Indeed, many times the problem was never really physical to begin with, and was only recast in physical terms so that the spring-damper apparatus could be applied.)
本节介绍阻尼振动和非阻尼振动的经典运动方程。首先介绍非阻尼振动，然后介绍阻尼振动。在电子游戏中，程序员经常使用虚拟弹簧（通常是弹簧阻尼系统的形式），而实际上他们使用的是一个控制系统。当我们抛开问题的物理本质，纯粹用数学术语来思考时，会有一些好处。（事实上，很多时候，问题本身就不是物理问题，只是为了应用弹簧阻尼装置而用物理术语重新表述。）

Like the friction law, the force law for springs is a surprisingly accurate approximation to the macroscopic behavior that is the result of complicated microscopic interactions. Consider a spring with one end fixed and the other end free to move in one dimension. When the spring is at equilibrium with no external forces on it, it has a natural length, called the rest length. If we stretch the spring, then it will pull back to try to regain its rest length. Likewise, if we compress the spring, it will push back. But how do we know the strength of the force in each case? That's what the force law tells us.
与摩擦定律类似，弹簧的力学定律对由复杂的微观相互作用产生的宏观行为有着惊人的精确近似。设想一根弹簧，一端固定，另一端在一维空间内自由移动。当弹簧处于平衡状态且没有外力作用时，它有一个自然长度，称为静止长度。如果我们拉伸弹簧，它会向后拉，试图恢复到静止长度。同样，如果我们压缩弹簧，它也会向后推。但是，我们如何知道每种情况下力的强度呢？这就是力学定律告诉我们的。

The force law for springs is known as Hooke's law, and it basically says that the magnitude of the restorative force is proportional to the difference from the current length and the rest length (provided the force does not exceed a value called the elastic limit, which varies with the material used to construct the spring). If we let l be the current length of the spring and l rest denote the rest length, then the magnitude of the restoring force f r is calculated by Equation (12.7).
弹簧的力学定律称为胡克定律，其基本原理是：恢复力的大小与弹簧当前长度与静止长度之差成正比（前提是恢复力不超过弹性极限，该极限随弹簧材料的不同而变化）。设弹簧当前长度为 l ，静止长度为 l rest ，则恢复力 f r 的大小可通过公式 (12.7) 计算。

Hooke's Law for Spring Forces
胡克弹簧力定律
(12.7)f r =k(l rest −l).

The constant k is known as the spring constant and essentially describes how “stiff” the spring is. The constant is not dimensionless. In order for Equation (12.7) to make sense, we must have
常数 k 称为弹簧常数，本质上描述了弹簧的“刚度”。该常数不是无量纲的。为了使公式 (12.7) 有意义，我们必须

[ML / T2]=k[L],[ML / T2] / [L]=k,[M / T2]=k,

or you can just think of k as having units of “unit force per unit length.”
或者您可以将 k 视为“单位力/单位长度”的单位。

The really interesting thing about springs is how they behave over time. To see this, let's restate Hooke's law in a way that focuses on the kinematics of a particle that is being acted on by restorative forces. Specifically, we're interested in functions for the position, velocity, and acceleration of a particle.
弹簧真正有趣的地方在于它们随时间的变化。为了理解这一点，我们重新表述胡克定律，重点关注粒子在恢复力作用下的运动学。具体来说，我们感兴趣的是粒子的位置、速度和加速度函数。

Things get easier if we adopt a reference frame where the position x=0 designates the “rest” position, where there are no restorative forces. Furthermore, since we are interested in the acceleration of the particle rather than the forces acting on it, we will introduce a constant K=k / m , and since K contains both the spring constant k and the mass of the particle m , it measures the spring's ability to accelerate the specific particle of interest to us. With those notational changes, we can rewrite Equation (12.7) as
如果我们采用一个参考系，其中位置 x=0 表示“静止”位置，即没有恢复力的位置，事情就会变得简单。此外，由于我们感兴趣的是粒子的加速度，而不是作用于粒子上的力，我们将引入一个常数 K=k / m ，由于 K 同时包含弹簧常数 k 和粒子的质量 m ，它衡量的是弹簧加速我们感兴趣的特定粒子的能力。通过这些符号上的改变，我们可以将公式 (12.7) 重写为

Acceleration due to Hooke's law
胡克定律产生的加速度
(12.8)a(t)=−Kx(t).

You should convince yourself that this is equivalent to Equation (12.7) before continuing.
在继续之前，你应该确信这等同于公式 (12.7)。

Equation (12.8) makes a statement about the relationship between the position function and the acceleration function; but what we really want is the function x(t) itself. Equations like this are called differential equations; they describe the relationship between some unknown function (in this case, x(t) ) and one or more of its derivatives (remember that acceleration is the second derivative of position). To “solve” a differential equation is to find the unknown function x(t) that satisfies the equation. We have been able to just barely scratch the surface of basic differential and integral calculus in this book, so we're not going to be able to cover the techniques of solving differential equations. Luckily, you don't need to know differential equations in order to verify that a proposed function x(t) is a solution—that requires only the ability to differentiate the function x(t) . As it turns out, this will be sufficient in the few cases in which we bump up against differential equations in this book.
方程 (12.8) 描述了位置函数和加速度函数之间的关系；但我们真正想要的是函数 x(t) 本身。像这样的方程称为微分方程；它们描述某个未知函数（在本例中为 x(t) ）与其一个或多个导数之间的关系（记住，加速度是位置的二阶导数）。“解”微分方程就是找到满足该方程的未知函数 x(t) 。本书中我们只是粗略地介绍了基本的微积分和积分知识，因此我们不会涉及求解微分方程的技巧。幸运的是，你不需要了解微分方程就可以验证所提出的函数 x(t) 是否为解——这只需要能够对函数 x(t) 进行微分。事实证明，在本书中少数涉及微分方程的情况下，这已经足够了。

We can make a pretty good guess at the form of x(t) by looking at a graph. We are not engaging in circular logic here; we don't need to know x(t) in order to get a graph, all we need is a spring with some sort of marking device attached to it.11 Such a graph is shown in Figure 12.5.
通过观察图表，我们可以相当准确地猜测 x(t) 的形式。我们这里不涉及循环逻辑；我们不需要知道 x(t) 就能得到图表，我们只需要一个弹簧，并在其上附加某种标记装置。11 图 12.5 显示了这样的一个图表。

Figure 12.5  图 12.5 The graph of the motion of a spring. Hey, that looks familiar…
弹簧运动的曲线图。嘿，看起来很熟悉……

This function ought to look familiar to you: it's the graph of the cosine function. Let's see what happens if we just try x(t)=cos⁡(t) as our position function. Differentiating twice to get the velocity and acceleration functions (remember, we learned about the derivative of the sine and cosine functions in Section 11.4.6), we get
这个函数你应该很熟悉：它是余弦函数的图像。让我们看看如果我们尝试用 x(t)=cos⁡(t) 作为位置函数会发生什么。对它进行两次微分，得到速度和加速度函数（记住，我们在 11.4.6 节学过正弦和余弦函数的导数），我们得到

Close, but not quite right
接近，但不完全正确
x(t)=cos⁡(t), x˙ (t)=−sin⁡(t), x¨ (t)=−cos⁡(t),

which is very close, but we're missing the factor of K .
这非常接近，但是我们缺少 K 这个因素。

To understand where K should appear in x(t) , consider what happens to the graph of x(t) when we change the value of K . In other words, we repeat our physical experiment and vary the stiffness of the spring or the mass of the marking device attached to the end of the spring. The result is that larger values of K (stiffer springs or less massive marking devices) result in a graph that is horizontally “compressed”: the frequency of oscillation is increased. Likewise, smaller values of K cause the spring to oscillate more slowly, and the graph is expanded. Furthermore, we observe that the frequency is proportional to the square root of K —when we increase K by a factor of four, the frequency doubles. This gives us a hint as to where K should appear, since all we are doing is scaling the time axis.
要理解 K 应出现在 x(t) 中的什么位置，请考虑当我们改变 K 的值时 x(t) 的图形会发生什么变化。换句话说，我们重复物理实验，并改变弹簧的刚度或连接到弹簧末端的标记装置的质量。结果是， K 的值较大（弹簧刚度较大或标记装置质量较小）会导致图形在水平方向上被“压缩”：振荡频率增加。同样， K 的值较小会导致弹簧振荡得更慢，图形会扩大。此外，我们观察到频率与 K 的平方根成正比 - 当我们将 K 增加四倍时，频率就会翻倍。这为我们提供了关于 K 应出现位置的提示，因为我们所做的只是缩放时间轴。

A solution, but is it the only one?
有一个解决方案，但它是唯一的解决方案吗？
x(t)=cos⁡(Kt), x˙ (t)=−Ksin⁡(Kt), x¨ (t)=−Kcos⁡(Kt).

One verifies that this is a solution to the differential equation by plugging it into Equation (12.8). Remembering that a(t)= x¨ (t) , we have
将其代入公式 (12.8) 中，即可验证这是微分方程的解。记住 a(t)= x¨ (t) ，我们有

a(t)=−Kx(t),−Kcos⁡(Kt)=−K(cos⁡(Kt)).

The quantity K is the angular frequency and comes up often enough that we find it helpful to introduce the notation
量 K 是角频率，并且经常出现，因此我们发现引入符号很有帮助

Angular frequency  角频率
ω=K=k / m,

and we can write the solution as
我们可以将解决方案写为

(12.9)x(t)=cos⁡(ωt);

hence the reason for the name “angular frequency” becomes apparent.
因此“角频率”这个名称的原因就显而易见了。

So we have found the kinematics equation for the spring. Or, perhaps we should say that we have found a solution to the differential equation. There are some degrees of freedom inherent in the motion of the spring that are not accounted for in Equation (12.9). First, we are not accounting for the maximum displacement, known as the amplitude of the oscillations and denoted A . Our equation always has an amplitude of 1. Second, we are assuming that x(0)=A , meaning the spring was initially stretched to the maximum displacment A and released with zero initial velocity. However, in general, we could have pulled it to some displacement x0≠A and then given it a shove so it has some initial velocity v0 .
因此，我们找到了弹簧的运动学方程。或者，我们应该说，我们找到了微分方程的解。弹簧运动中固有的一些自由度在方程 (12.9) 中没有得到考虑。首先，我们没有考虑最大位移，即振荡的振幅，用 A 表示。我们的方程的振幅始终为 1。其次，我们假设 x(0)=A ，这意味着弹簧最初被拉伸到最大位移 A ，并以零初速度释放。然而，通常，我们可以将其拉到某个位移 x0≠A ，然后给它一个推力，这样它就有了某个初速度 v0 。

It would appear that we have three more variables which need to be somehow accounted for in our equation if it is going to be completely general. As it turns out, the three variables we have just discussed—the amplitude, initial position, and initial velocity—are interrelated. If we pick any two, the value for the third is locked in. We'll keep A as is, but we'll replace x0 and v0 with the phase offset θ0 , which describes where in the cycle the spring is at t=0 . Adjustments to the phase offset have the simple effect of shifting the graph horizontally on the time axis. Adding these two variables, we arrive at the general solution, the equations of simple harmonic oscillation.
如果我们的方程要具有普遍性，似乎还需要以某种方式考虑另外三个变量。事实证明，我们刚刚讨论的三个变量——振幅、初始位置和初始速度——是相互关联的。如果我们选取任意两个，第三个变量的值就会固定。我们将保持 A 不变，但将 x0 和 v0 替换为相位偏移 θ0 ，它描述了弹簧在周期中处于 t=0 的位置。调整相位偏移只会在时间轴上水平移动图形。将这两个变量相加，我们就得到了通解，即简谐振动方程。

Simple Harmonic Motion  简谐运动
(12.10)x(t)=Acos⁡(ωt+θ0), x˙ (t)=−Aωsin⁡(ωt+θ0), x¨ (t)=−Aω2cos⁡(ωt+θ0).

Now let's make some observations. First, remember that the sine and cosine functions are just shifted versions of each other: sin⁡(t+π / 2)=cos⁡(t) . Thus we could have written x(t) using sine instead of cosine, the choice being mostly a matter of preference and an adjustment in the phase by π / 2 . The term “sinusoidal” can be used to refer to the shape of the sine and cosine functions, and we use it when either function will do.
现在让我们做一些观察。首先，记住正弦函数和余弦函数只是彼此的移位版本： sin⁡(t+π / 2)=cos⁡(t) 。因此，我们可以用正弦函数代替余弦函数来表示 x(t) ，选择哪种方式主要取决于个人喜好，并且需要对相位进行 π / 2 的调整。“正弦”一词可以用来指正弦函数和余弦函数的形状，当两个函数都可以时，我们就会使用它。

Second, consider the frequency of oscillation. The sine and cosine functions have a period of 2π ; thus the oscillator will complete one cycle in the time it takes for ωt to increase by 2π . The angular frequency ω is measured in radians per unit time, but we can also measure the frequency F , which is in cycles per unit time, as
其次，考虑振荡频率。正弦函数和余弦函数的周期为 2π ；因此，振荡器在 ωt 增加 2π 的时间内完成一个周期。角频率 ω 以弧度/单位时间测量，但我们也可以测量频率 F ，其以周期/单位时间测量，如下所示

Frequency of simple harmonic motion
简谐运动的频率
F= ω 2π = K 2π = 1 2π km .

Notice that the frequency of oscillation depends only on ratio of the spring stiffness to the mass. In particular, it does not depend on the initial displacement x0 : if we stretch the spring farther before letting it go, the amplitude increases, but the frequency will not change.
请注意，振动频率仅取决于弹簧刚度与质量的比值。具体来说，它与初始位移 x0 无关：如果我们在松开弹簧之前将其拉伸得更长，振幅会增加，但频率不会改变。

In many situations, the frequency is the important number we wish to control. This is especially the case for “virtual springs,” which are really control systems in disguise. In these situations, we don't need to bother with spring constants or masses, and we can write the equation of motion directly in terms of frequency, as
在许多情况下，频率是我们希望控制的重要数字。对于“虚拟弹簧”尤其如此，它们实际上是伪装的控制系统。在这种情况下，我们无需考虑弹簧常数或质量，可以直接用频率来表示运动方程，如下所示

Simple harmonic motion in terms of frequency
简谐运动的频率
x(t)=Acos⁡(2πFt+θ0).

So far, we have been studying a physically nonexistent situation in which the restorative force is the only force present, and the spring will oscillate forever. In reality, there are usually at least two more interesting forces. The first of these forces is an external force, sometimes called the driving force, that acts as the “input” to the system and causes the motion to begin in the first place. The other force is the friction that any real spring experiences, which eventually causes the motion to cease. The general term used to describe any effect that tends to reduce the amplitude of an oscillatory system is damping, and we call oscillation where the amplitude decays over time damped oscillation. Damping forces are particularly important for our purposes, so let's discuss them in more detail.
到目前为止，我们一直在研究一种物理上不存在的情况，其中恢复力是唯一存在的力，弹簧将永远振荡。实际上，通常至少还有两种更有趣的力。第一种力是外力，有时称为驱动力，它作为系统的“输入”，并首先导致运动开始。另一种力是任何真实弹簧都会遇到的摩擦力，它最终会导致运动停止。用于描述任何倾向于降低振荡系统振幅的效应的通用术语是阻尼，我们将振幅随时间衰减的振荡称为阻尼振荡。阻尼力对我们的目的尤为重要，因此让我们更详细地讨论它们。

The most common model for the damping force is a simple one that acts proportional to velocity but in the opposite direction, similar to the friction law. (Unlike the friction laws from the previous section, we don't have any of the business concerning the normal force.) The force is simply
最常见的阻尼力模型很简单，它与速度成正比，但方向相反，类似于摩擦定律。（与上一节的摩擦定律不同，这里不讨论法向力。）该力简单地表示为

Damping force  阻尼力
f d =−c x˙ ,

where f d indicates the instantaneous magnitude and direction of the damping force, x˙ is the instantaneous velocity, and c is a constant that describes the viscosity, roughness, etc.
其中 f d 表示阻尼力的瞬时大小和方向， x˙ 表示瞬时速度， c 是描述粘度、粗糙度等的常数。

The damping force has an extremely simple form, but just as with the restorative force, things get interesting when we study the motion over time. Qualitatively, we can make some basic predictions about how damped oscillation of a spring would differ from undamped oscillation of the same spring. The more obvious prediction is that we would expect the amplitude of oscillation to decay over time, meaning the maximum displacement at the crest of each cycle is a bit less than the previous one. Like the force of friction, damping tends to remove energy from the system. The second observation is only slightly less obvious: since damping in general slows the velocity of the mass on the end of the spring, we would expect the frequency of oscillation to be reduced compared to undamped oscillation. Those two intuitive predictions turn out to be correct, although, of course, to be more specific we will need to analyze the math.
阻尼力具有极其简单的形式，但就像恢复力一样，当我们研究运动随时间的变化时，事情会变得有趣。从定性上讲，我们可以对弹簧的阻尼振动与同一弹簧的无阻尼振动有何不同做出一些基本预测。更明显的预测是，我们预计振动的幅度会随着时间的推移而衰减，这意味着每个周期波峰处的最大位移比前一个略小。与摩擦力一样，阻尼往往会从系统中带走能量。第二个观察结果只是稍微不那么明显：由于阻尼通常会减慢弹簧末端质量的速度，我们预计振动的频率与无阻尼振动相比会降低。这两个直观的预测被证明是正确的，当然，为了更具体地说明，我们需要进行数学分析。

Combining the restorative and damping forces, the net force can be written as
结合恢复力和阻尼力，净力可以写成

f net =f r +f d =−kx−c x˙ .

To derive the equation of motion, we will need accelerations, not forces. Applying Newton's second law and dividing both sides by the mass, we have
为了推导运动方程，我们需要加速度，而不是力。应用牛顿第二定律，将两边除以质量，可得

(12.11) x¨ = f net m =− km x− cm x˙ ,

Next we rewrite this in terms of two new quantities. The first quantity, ω0 , is the undamped angular frequency and is not really new. It is identical to the ω=k / m introduced earlier; we are adding the zero subscript just to emphasize that it is the frequency that would occur without the damping rather than the actual frequency. (Remember, our prediction is that the actual frequency will be slower in some way.)
接下来，我们用两个新的量来重写这个公式。第一个量 ω0 是无阻尼角频率，这并不是什么新量。它与之前介绍的 ω=k / m 相同；我们添加下标零只是为了强调它是无阻尼时的频率，而不是实际频率。（记住，我们预测实际频率会在某种程度上变慢。）

The second quantity is called the damping ratio, not to be confused with the damping coefficient c . The damping ratio is traditionally denoted by ζ , the Greek letter zeta, which looks weird and takes some practice to write by hand. The damping ratio is related to the damping coefficient, mass, and undamped angular frequency by the formula
第二个量称为阻尼比，不要与阻尼系数 c 混淆。阻尼比传统上用希腊字母 ζ 表示，即 ζ ，这个字母看起来很怪异，需要练习才能手写。阻尼比与阻尼系数、质量和非阻尼角频率的关系如下：

Damping ratio  阻尼比
ζ= c 2mk = c 2mω0 .

In just a moment, when we explain the qualitative meaning of ζ , the utility in using this arbitrary formula will become apparent.
稍后，当我们解释 ζ 的定性含义时，使用这个任意公式的实用性就会变得显而易见。

Substituting the undamped frequency ω0 and damping ratio ζ into Equation (12.11), we have
将无阻尼频率 ω0 和阻尼比 ζ 代入公式（12.11），可得

Differential equation for damped harmonic oscillation
阻尼谐振动的微分方程
(12.12) x¨ =−ω02x−2ζω0 x˙ .

Readers with training in differential equations should recognize Equation (12.12) as a second-order linear homogenous differential equation with constant coefficients, which is one of the very nicest differential equations we could hope for, meaning we can actually solve it with pencil and paper. Readers without this training shouldn't worry, because it won't be needed to understand the answer, to which we now fast forward, skipping the derivation. There are three distinct cases: underdamping, critical damping, and overdamping.
受过微分方程训练的读者应该能认出 (12.12) 式是一个二阶常系数线性齐次微分方程，这是我们所能期待的最完美的微分方程之一，这意味着我们实际上可以用纸笔来求解它。没有受过微分方程训练的读者也不必担心，因为理解答案并不需要，我们现在直接快进，跳过推导部分。有三种不同的情况：欠阻尼、临界阻尼和过阻尼。

When 0≤ζ<1 , we say that the system is underdamped. In this case, as we have been predicting, the motion will continue to oscillate indefinitely with an amplitude that decays exponentially over time. The equation that describes this motion is
当 0≤ζ<1 时，我们称系统为欠阻尼。在这种情况下，正如我们之前预测的那样，运动将无限期地持续振荡，其振幅随时间呈指数衰减。描述该运动的方程为

Kinematic equation for underdamped system
欠阻尼系统的运动学方程
(12.13)x(t)= (k1cos⁡(ωdt)+k2sin⁡(ωdt)) e −ζω0t ,

where ωd is the actual frequency of the damped oscillation and is related to the undamped frequency ω0 by
其中 ωd 是阻尼振荡的实际频率，与无阻尼频率 ω0 的关系为

Damped angular frequency  阻尼角频率
(12.14)ωd=ω01−ζ2.

The constants k1 and k2 are determined by the initial position and velocity:
常数 k1 和 k2 由初始位置和速度决定：

k1=x(0),k2= ζω0x(0)+ x˙ (0) ωd.

Using ζ=0 produces undamped oscillation, and Equation (12.13) is equivalent to Equation (12.10).
使用 ζ=0 产生无阻尼振荡，且公式 (12.13) 等价于公式 (12.10)。

Your common sense tells you that as we increase the damping ratio, the frequency of oscillation decreases; consulting Equation (12.14), we see that at ζ=1 the frequency completely vanishes. At this threshold, known as critical damping, the behavior of the system changes qualitatively. The system no longer oscillates, but instead decays exponentially. The kinematic equation in this situation is
常识告诉我们，随着阻尼比的增加，振荡频率会降低；根据公式 (12.14)，我们发现在 ζ=1 处频率完全消失。在这个阈值（称为临界阻尼）下，系统的行为发生了质的变化。系统不再振荡，而是呈指数衰减。在这种情况下，运动学方程为

Equation of motion at critical damping
临界阻尼运动方程
(12.15)x(t)= (k1+k2t) e −ω0t ,

where k1 and k2 are again determined by the initial conditions:
其中 k1 和 k2 再次由初始条件决定：

k1=x(0),k2=ω0x(0)+ x˙ (0).

Critical damping is just the right amount such that the system decays as quickly as possible without oscillation. If the damping is decreased, the system is underdamped, as previously described, and will oscillate. If the damping is increased, the system is overdamped; it will not oscillate, and the rate of decay will be slower than the rate at critical damping. Figure 12.6 shows how the damping value affects the behavior of a system.
临界阻尼是指系统能够尽可能快地衰减而不发生振荡的合适值。如果阻尼减小，系统就会像前面描述的那样处于欠阻尼状态，并会发生振荡。如果阻尼增大，系统就会处于过阻尼状态，系统不会振荡，衰减速度也会低于临界阻尼时的衰减速度。图 12.6 显示了阻尼值如何影响系统的行为。

Figure 12.6  图 12.6Undamped, underdamped, and critically damped systems.
无阻尼、欠阻尼和临界阻尼系统。

Now that we've reviewed the classic equations that may be found in any physics textbook or on wikipedia.org, let's say a few words about how spring-damper systems are used in video games as control systems. In
既然我们已经回顾了在任何物理教科书或 wikipedia.org 上都能找到的经典方程式，那么让我们来简单介绍一下弹簧阻尼系统在电子游戏中是如何作为控制系统使用的。在

general, a control system12 takes as input a function of time that represents some target value. For example, our camera code might compute a desired camera position based on the player's position each frame; some AI code might determine an exact targeting angle for an enemy; we may have a desired player character velocity based on the instantaneous amount of control stick deflection; or we might have a desired screen-space position for some highlight effect, based on the currently selected choice in a menu. In any case, the current value of the input signal is known as the set point in control system terminology. The set point is essentially the rest position of the spring, and the input signal is like somebody taking the other end of the spring and yanking it around. (So it's similar to a driving force, only usually what we have is a function describing a position rather than a force or acceleration.)
一般来说，控制系统 12 将表示某个目标值的时间函数作为输入。例如，我们的摄像机代码可能会根据玩家每帧的位置计算出所需的摄像机位置；某些 AI 代码可能会确定敌人的精确瞄准角度；我们可能会根据控制杆的瞬时偏转量来确定所需的玩家角色速度；或者，我们可能会根据菜单中当前选择的选项来确定某些高亮效果所需的屏幕空间位置。无论如何，输入信号的当前值在控制系统术语中称为设定点。设定点本质上是弹簧的静止位置，而输入信号就像有人抓住弹簧的另一端并猛拉。（因此，它类似于驱动力，只是通常我们得到的是描述位置而不是力或加速度的函数。）

The job of any control system is to take this input signal and produce an output signal. To go back to our earlier examples, the output signal might be the actual camera position to use for each frame, or the actual animated targeting angle the enemy will use to aim the weapon, the actual player character velocity, or the actual screen-space position of the highlight. For many control systems, the actual position and set point are not used; rather, only the error is needed. Of course, an obvious question is, if we know the “desired” value, why don't we just use that directly? Because it's too jerky. In the same way that the shocks and springs on a car (a classic example of a spring-damper system) don't just pass along the elevation of the road directly to the car, a control system in a video game is often designed to “smooth out the bumps” caused by sudden state changes that might make the camera snap to a new position or the player jerk into motion. The camera or screen-space highlight are nonphysical examples in which the quantity of “mass” is not really appropriate and is dropped. But the differential equations are still the same, and they have the same solution. Stripped of the spring metaphor, we are left with what is known as a PD controller. The P stands for proportional, and this is the spring part of the controller, since it acts proportional to the current error. The damper is the D part, which stands for derivative, because the action of the damper at any given instant is proportional to the derivative (the velocity). PD controllers (and their more robust cousin, the PID controller, where the I stands for integral and is used to remove steady-state error) are broadly applicable tools; they have been standard engineering tools for decades (centuries?) and are well understood. Nevertheless, they are one of the most frequently reinvented wheels in video gameprogramming.
任何控制系统的任务都是接收输入信号并产生输出信号。回到我们之前的例子，输出信号可能是每帧实际使用的摄像机位置，或者敌人瞄准武器时使用的实际动画瞄准角度，或者玩家角色的实际速度，或者高光在屏幕空间的实际位置。许多控制系统并不使用实际位置和设定点；相反，只需要误差。当然，一个显而易见的问题是，如果我们知道“期望”值，为什么不直接使用它呢？因为它太不稳定了。就像汽车上的减震器和弹簧（弹簧减震系统的经典例子）不会将路面的高低直接传递给汽车一样，电子游戏中的控制系统通常被设计为“平滑颠簸”，这些颠簸是由突然的状态变化引起的，可能会导致摄像机突然移动到新的位置或玩家突然运动。摄像机或屏幕空间的高光部分是非物理的例子，其中“质量”的数量并不恰当，因此被省略了。但微分方程仍然相同，并且它们的解也相同。去掉弹簧的比喻，我们剩下的就是所谓的 PD 控制器。P 代表比例，这是控制器的弹簧部分，因为它的作用与当前误差成比例。阻尼器是 D 部分，代表导数，因为阻尼器在任何给定时刻的作用都与导数（速度）成比例。 PD 控制器（以及其更强大的“表亲”PID 控制器，其中 I 代表积分，用于消除稳态误差）是广泛适用的工具；几十年（甚至几个世纪？）以来，它们一直是标准的工程工具，并且已被广泛理解。然而，它们却是电子游戏编程中最常被重复发明的工具之一。

In practice, the simulation code is a very simple Euler integration of Equation (12.11). As shown in Section 12.6.3, this is a fancy way of describing code that looks like Listing 12.1.
实际上，模拟代码是方程 (12.11) 的一个非常简单的欧拉积分。如第 12.6.3 节所示，这是一种描述代码的巧妙方式，类似于清单 12.1。

struct SpringDamper {
    float value;    // current value
    float setPoint; // "desired" value
    float velocity; // current ``velocity'' (derivative of value)
    float c;        // damping coefficient
    float k;        // spring constant

    // Update the current value and velocity, stepping forward
    // in time by the given time step
    void update(float dt) {

        // Compute acceleration
        float error = value - setPoint;
        float accel = -error*k - c*velocity;

        // Euler integration
        velocity += accel*dt;
        value += velocity*dt;
    }
};

Different cars have suspensions that are tuned differently; sports cars are “tighter” and the cars retirees like to drive are smoother. In the same way, we tune our control systems to get the response we like. Notice that the simulation uses the k and c from Equation (12.11). However, most people don't find those to be the most intuitive dials to have for tweaking. Instead, the damping ratio and frequency of oscillation are used for the designer interface, while k and c are computed as derived quantities. To tune the frequency, we might adjust either the damped or undamped version, using either angular frequency or simply Hertz; the units and absolute value are often not important because the value that feels good will be determined experimentally anyway. For many systems in video games, oscillation is undesirable, so it's common to assume a critically damped system and fix ζ=1 , leaving just the “frequency” (we put it in quotes since the system doesn't oscillate) as the only tunable value. A higher frequency is the sports car (more responsive, but jerkier), and a lower frequency is smoother, but can feel “laggy.”
不同汽车的悬架调校不同；跑车“更紧”，而退休人员喜欢驾驶的汽车则更平稳。同样，我们调整控制系统以获得我们喜欢的响应。请注意，模拟使用公式 (12.11) 中的 k 和 c 。然而，大多数人并不认为这些是用于调整的最直观的刻度盘。相反，阻尼比和振荡频率用于设计器界面，而 k 和 c 则作为派生量计算。为了调整频率，我们可以使用角频率或简单的赫兹来调整阻尼或无阻尼版本；单位和绝对值通常并不重要，因为感觉良好的值无论如何都会通过实验确定。对于许多电子游戏系统来说，振荡是不可取的，因此通常假设系统具有临界阻尼并固定 ζ=1 ，只留下“频率”（我们将其放在引号中，因为系统不会振荡）作为唯一可调的值。较高的频率就像跑车（响应更快，但抖动更大），而较低的频率则更平滑，但会感觉“迟钝”。

Notice that the kinematic equations (12.13) and (12.15) are not needed directly by the simulation, nor do we need to explicitly distinguish between underdamped, critically damped, or overdamped.
请注意，模拟并不直接需要运动学方程 (12.13) 和 (12.15)，我们也不需要明确区分欠阻尼、临界阻尼或过阻尼。

Before we leave this discussion, we must mention that the second-order systems we have described here are certainly not the only type of control system, nor even the simplest, but they do behave nicely under a very broad set of circumstances and are easy to implement and tune. Another commonly used control system is a simple first order lag, x˙ =kx , under which the error decays exponentially. This is similar to a critically damped second-order system, but with a bit jerkier response to a sudden change in the set point. Another important and common technique is to “chase” the set point at a fixed velocity.
