A filter is another broad class of control system, in which the output is computed by taking some linear combination of set points or values on previous frames.
在结束讨论之前，我们必须指出，我们在此描述的二阶系统当然不是唯一的控制系统类型，甚至不是最简单的，但它们在很多情况下都表现良好，并且易于实现和调整。另一个常用的控制系统是简单的一阶滞后 x˙ =kx ，在此情况下误差呈指数衰减。这类似于临界阻尼二阶系统，但对设定点的突然变化的响应稍微急促一些。另一种重要且常见的技术是以固定速度“追逐”设定点。滤波器是另一类广泛的控制系统，其中输出是通过对先前帧的设定点或值进行某种线性组合来计算的。

12.3Momentum  12.3 动量

Let's say that Moe's box from Section 12.1.3 has a mass m , and at a certain instant we observe it moving with a velocity v . Coming in late to the story, we cannot tell what magnitude of forces were used to achieve that motion, or how long the forces were applied, or what the history of the box's velocity was. For example, it could have been that the box was accelerated as a result of a constant net force f being applied over a duration Δt . But we have no way of knowing the values of f and Δt . Was a large force used for a small duration, or a small force for a longer duration? In fact, we have no reason to assume that the force was constant at all! Moe could have given the box a good shove and set it in motion, and then gave it another shove to speed it up.
假设第 12.1.3 节中 Moe 的盒子质量为 m ，在某一时刻我们观察到它以速度 v 运动。由于时间太晚，我们无法判断实现了这一运动使用了多大的力，或者力作用了多长时间，或者盒子速度的变化过程如何。例如，盒子可能是由于在持续时间 Δt 内施加了恒定的净力 f 而加速的。但我们无法知道 f 和 Δt 的值。是使用了较大的力但持续时间较短，还是使用了较小的力但持续时间较长？事实上，我们根本没有理由假设力是恒定的！Moe 可以用力推一下盒子使其运动起来，然后再推一下使其加速。

While we don't know the exact history of Moe's pushes, we do know what the “total” was, in the sense about to be described. Assume that Moe did make one push with a constant force f applied for a duration Δt . Then according to Newton's second law, the acceleration was a = f / m . Assuming the initial velocity was zero, we know that
虽然我们不知道莫推力的确切过程，但我们知道“总推力”是多少，也就是我们即将描述的那个量。假设莫确实用一个恒定的力 f 推了一次，持续时间为 Δt 。那么根据牛顿第二定律，加速度为 a = f / m 。假设初速度为零，我们知道

v = a Δt.

Substituting a = f / m and rearranging, we get
代入 a = f / m 并重新排列，我们得到

Two ways to think of momentum
思考动量的两种方式
v =( f / m)Δt,(12.16)m v = f Δt.

The left- and right-hand sides of Equation (12.16) illustrate two different ways of thinking about the important concept of momentum. Momentum is the correct quantity to track in order to quantify the “total amount of pushing.”
等式（12.16）的左右两边阐述了对动量这一重要概念的两种不同思考方式。为了量化“推动的总量”，动量才是应该追踪的正确量。

Let's do dimensional analysis on Equation (12.16), first just to verify that it makes physical sense—it isn't intuitively obvious that these two products would bear the same physical meaning—and also to see what the units of momentum should be:
让我们对方程 (12.16) 进行量纲分析，首先只是为了验证它是否具有物理意义——这两个乘积具有相同的物理意义并不是直观上显而易见的——同时也看看动量的单位应该是什么：

m v = f Δt,M(L / T)=(ML / T2)T,ML / T=ML / T.

Note that momentum is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction.
请注意，动量是一个矢量，既有大小又有方向。

To understand what momentum is, let's look at the two sides of Equation (12.16). First consider the left side, which interprets momentum as a product of mass and velocity. In fact, somewhere in almost every physics textbook you can find Equation (12.17).
为了理解动量是什么，我们来看看公式 (12.16) 的两边。首先考虑左边，它将动量解释为质量和速度的乘积。事实上，几乎在每本物理教科书中都能找到公式 (12.17)。

Momentum as Product of Mass and Velocity
动量是质量和速度的乘积
(12.17) P =m v .

The variable P is the traditional variable used to represent momentum. (Despite the capital letter, P is a vector quantity. We use capital P to avoid confusion with the notation p , which we sometimes use to refer to the position of a particle.)
变量 P 是用来表示动量的传统变量。（尽管 P 是大写字母，但它是一个矢量。我们使用大写字母 P 是为了避免与符号 p 混淆，后者有时用于表示粒子的位置。）

Equation (12.17) makes it clear that the momentum of an object is an instantaneous property of an object. By saying this, we mean that we can define its value knowing only its instantaneous state, without worrying about how it got into that state. Furthermore, if you think of momentum as the “total amount of pushing” required to stop a moving object, then it certainly is intuitively appealing that it should be the product of mass and velocity. If the object is small and moving slowly (a pencil rolling on a desktop), only a small total force will suffice. If it's fast (a bullet) or heavy (a car that somebody left parked on an incline without the emergency brake set), a larger amount will be needed. If it's fast and heavy (an airplane coming in for a landing), then you'd better get out of the way. The equation P =m v quantifies the idea of “hard to stop.”
公式 (12.17) 清楚地表明，物体的动量是其瞬时属性。我们这样说的意思是，我们只需知道物体的瞬时状态就可以定义其值，而无需考虑它是如何进入该状态的。此外，如果你将动量视为使运动物体停止所需的“总推力”，那么它应该是质量和速度的乘积，这在直观上很有吸引力。如果物体很小且移动缓慢（例如在桌面上滚动的铅笔），则只需施加较小的总推力即可。如果它速度很快（例如子弹）或很重（例如停在斜坡上而未拉紧紧急刹车的汽车），则需要施加更大的推力。如果它速度很快且很重（例如即将降落的飞机），那么你最好躲开。公式 P =m v 量化了“难以停止”的概念。

Although the memorable equation P =m v from the left-hand side of Equation (12.16) is perhaps the more common way of explaining momentum, the right-hand side actually provides the most insight. The relation P = f Δt shows that momentum, as the product of force and time, is what results when force acts over time. This is what was meant by the sloppy phrase “total amount of pushing.” We don't mean that the magnitude of the force pushing itself is changing or accumulating, but rather that the continued application of a net force always results in a buildup of momentum (or a reduction of momentum, when the directions of the force and momentum are opposed).
虽然公式 (12.16) 左边那个令人难忘的公式 P =m v 或许是解释动量的更常用方式，但右边实际上提供了最深刻的见解。关系式 P = f Δt 表明，动量是力与时间的乘积，是力随时间作用的结果。这就是“推力总量”这个不严谨的说法的含义。我们的意思并非推力本身的大小在变化或累积，而是净力的持续作用总是会导致动量的增加（或者，当力和动量的方向相反时，动量会减小）。

In fact, if we generalize the equation P = f Δt , we can discover an even deeper relationship between force and momentum. What if, instead of pushing the box with a constant force, Moe pushed it with a force that varied over time? Then we can express the acceleration at any given time t as
事实上，如果我们推广方程 P = f Δt ，就能发现力和动量之间更深层次的关系。如果 Moe 不是用恒定的力推动盒子，而是用一个随时间变化的力来推动它，会怎么样？那么，我们可以将任意给定时间 t 的加速度表示为

(12.18) a (t)= f (t) / m,

which is just Newton's second law to which we've added the notation “ (t) ” to be more explicit that a and f vary with time. We learned in Chapter 11 that if we integrate acceleration over time, we get the velocity as a function of time:
这其实就是牛顿第二定律，我们添加了符号“ (t) ”，以便更明确地表示 a 和 f 随时间变化。我们在第 11 章中学习过，如果对加速度进行时间积分，就能得到速度随时间的变化：

Velocity is the time integral of acceleration, remember?
速度是加速度的时间积分，记得吗？
(12.19) v (t)=∫ a (t) dt.

Substituting Equation (12.18) into Equation (12.19), assuming that the mass does not vary over time, we have
将方程 (12.18) 代入方程 (12.19)，假设质量不随时间变化，我们得到

v (t)=∫ f (t) / m dt,m v (t)=∫ f (t) dt.

Finally, if we let P (t) be the momentum of a body as a function of time, then by substituting P (t)=m v (t) , we arrive at the important relation
最后，如果我们让 P (t) 成为物体的动量随时间的变化函数，那么通过代入 P (t)=m v (t) ，我们得到重要的关系

Momentum as force accumulated over time
动量是随着时间推移而积累的力量
(12.20) P (t)=∫ f (t) dt.

Since integration is a “summing up” process, Equation (12.20) confirms our interpretation of momentum as the result of continued application of force over time. (Note: in the preceding integrals we omitted the constant of integration, essentially assuming the initial velocity was zero.)
由于积分是一个“求和”的过程，公式（12.20）证实了我们对动量的解释，即力随时间持续作用的结果。（注意：在前面的积分中，我们省略了积分常数，本质上假设初速度为零。）

Remember that integration and differentiation are inverse operations. By taking the derivative of both sides with respect to t , we state the flip side of the relationship between momentum and force.
记住，积分和微分是互逆运算。通过对两边分别对 t 求导，我们得到了动量和力之间关系的另一面。

Force as the Derivative of Momentum
力是动量的导数
(12.21)d dt   P (t)= f (t).

The net external force on a system is equal to the rate of change of momentum of the system.
系统所受的净外力等于系统动量的变化率。

Equation (12.21) is not just an interesting observation about force and momentum, it's a completely valid way to define force. In fact, although the modern presentation of Newton's laws is in terms of forces and masses, when Newton himself first expressed the laws, he wrote in terms of momentum. He used the word “motion,” but from his writings we understand that he used that word in a very particular sense, and he really was talking about momentum. (The word momentum hadn't been attached to that concept yet. Remember, he was the guy laying down all the ground rules.) Newton's second law was originally expressed in a form that more closely resembles Equation (12.21) than the f =m a form you will more commonlysee.
公式 (12.21) 不仅是关于力和动量的有趣观察，它还是一种完全有效的定义力的方式。事实上，虽然牛顿定律的现代表述方式是用力和质量来表达的，但牛顿本人首次表述这些定律时，却是用动量来表达的。他使用了“运动”一词，但从他的著作中我们可以理解，他使用这个词的意义非常特殊，他实际上指的是动量。（动量这个词当时还没有与这个概念联系在一起。记住，他是所有基本规则的制定者。）牛顿第二定律最初的表述形式与公式 (12.21) 更为相似，而不是您更常见的 f =m a 形式。

12.3.1Conservation of Momentum
12.3.1 动量守恒

Let's return to our investigation into what happens when Moe pushes against the Earth to get his box moving. Newton's law tells us that the Earth, not having anything else to push back on, receives a net force, and thus an acceleration (and a torque, which we discuss later). Yes, you cause the Earth to accelerate when you push boxes as well as when you take each and every step! Of course, the Earth's mass is so large compared to Moe's force that this acceleration is small. Not only that, but Moe's force pushing the box to the east might be canceled out by Joe's force in North Dakota pushing his box to the west at the same time. An issue even more important than these two facts involves the “accounting laws” of physics: “there is no such thing as free momentum.” Moe doesn't need Joe to balance out his force; as it turns out, he can't help but do it all byhimself!
让我们回到之前的研究，看看当莫推地球推动箱子时会发生什么。牛顿定律告诉我们，地球没有其他物体反推，会受到一个净力，从而产生加速度（以及扭矩，我们稍后会讨论）。没错，你推箱子时，以及你迈出的每一步，都会使地球加速！当然，地球的质量与莫的推力相比非常大，以至于这个加速度很小。不仅如此，莫向东推箱子的力可能会被同时在北达科他州的乔向西推箱子的力抵消。一个比这两个事实更重要的问题涉及物理学的“会计定律”：“自由动量根本不存在。”莫不需要乔来平衡他的推力；事实证明，他必须自己完成这一切！

Observe that once Moe sets the box in motion, he will need to eventually stop it. According to Newton's first law, the only way to stop a moving box is through a force, and according to the third law, this can happen only if there is some other object involved to receive the opposite force. Perhaps the box bumps into a tree and comes to a stop. (We consider the tree to be part of the Earth. Remember that Newton's third law justifies our treatment of connected objects as a single object, provided that they remain rigidly connected.) To stop the box, the Earth must push against it with a force that is in the opposite direction that Moe pushed to start it moving. However, we know that the “total amount” of pushing must be the same, meaning the Earth must push back with a strong enough force, or for a long enough duration (perhaps Moe's box rolls into a patch of tall grass) to bring the momentum of the box down to zero. So you see that whatever acceleration the Earth received as a result of getting Moe's box in motion must always be exactly canceled by the force required to bring the box to a stop.
请注意，一旦莫启动了盒子，他最终需要让它停止。根据牛顿第一定律，停止移动盒子的唯一方法是施加力；而根据牛顿第三定律，只有当有其他物体受到反作用力时，才能发生这种情况。也许盒子撞到一棵树然后停了下来。（我们将树视为地球的一部分。记住，牛顿第三定律证明了我们将连接的物体视为单个物体是合理的，前提是它们保持刚性连接。）为了停止盒子，地球必须以与莫启动盒子时施加的力方向相反的力推它。然而，我们知道推力的“总量”必须相同，这意味着地球必须以足够大的力推回盒子，或者推回的时间足够长（也许莫的盒子滚进了一片高高的草丛），以使盒子的动量降至零。因此，您会看到，地球因使莫伊的盒子运动而受到的任何加速度都必须与使盒子停止所需的力完全抵消。

But perhaps Moe's box does not come to a stop by pushing directly against the Earth. Let's say it bumps up against Joe's box. Voila! We have stopped Moe's box, and no force has been applied to the Earth. But now, by Newton's third law, Joe's box must begin accelerating, and we are back to where we started with a moving box that will continue moving unless it receives a force to bring it to a stop. Eventually, the only way we can stop this chain reaction started by Moe's push against his box is for something, eventually, to push against the Earth.
但或许莫的盒子并非直接推向地球而停下来。假设它撞到了乔的盒子。瞧！莫的盒子停了下来，地球也未受到任何力。但现在，根据牛顿第三运动定律，乔的盒子必然开始加速，我们又回到了最初的状态：一个运动的盒子，除非受到力使其停止，否则它会继续运动。最终，我们能阻止莫推盒子引发的连锁反应的唯一方法是，最终让某个东西推向地球。

We can generalize this idea even further. We are justified in treating the entire Earth, and all of its moving parts, as a single particle with all of its mass centered at some location known as the center of mass. (We talk more about this special point in Section 12.3.2.) The pushing against the Earth of people like Moe results in transfers of momentum between the objects in the system. Each part will move around within this very complicated system relative to the other parts and relative to the center of mass of the system. However, the total amount of momentum of the entire system is always a constant, unless there are external forces acting on the system. This is known as the law of conservation of momentum.
我们可以进一步推广这个想法。我们有理由将整个地球及其所有运动部件视为一个粒子，其所有质量都集中在某个位置，称为质心。（我们将在 12.3.2 节中详细讨论这个特殊点。）像 Moe 这样的人对地球的推挤会导致系统中物体之间的动量转移。在这个非常复杂的系统中，每个部件都会相对于其他部件以及系统的质心移动。然而，除非有外力作用于系统，否则整个系统的总动量始终为常数。这被称为动量守恒定律。

The Law of Conservation of Momentum
动量守恒定律
The momentum of a system is constant unless external forces act on that system.
除非外力作用于该系统，否则系统的动量是恒定的。

The conservation of momentum is precisely what Equation (12.21)is saying. It's certainly an experimentally verified fact, but it also follows naturally as a result of Newton's laws. Section 12.4 discusses how to use this important law to simulate the collision of objects. However, before we get to that, we need to take a closer look at the center ofmass.
动量守恒正是公式 (12.21) 所表述的。这当然是经过实验验证的事实，但它也是牛顿定律的自然结果。12.4 节讨论了如何运用这一重要定律来模拟物体的碰撞。然而，在讨论这一点之前，我们需要仔细研究一下质心。

12.3.2The Center of Mass  12.3.2 质心

Our discussion of momentum has led us to consider the center of mass of an object. Let's say a few more words concerning this important concept. For everyday purposes, the center of mass is equivalent to the center of gravity, which is essentially the point around which the object is perfectly balanced. If we balance an object on the tip of a very thin rod or hang it from a wire, then the rod or wire will be in a line that contains the center of mass.
我们对动量的讨论引导我们思考物体的质心。让我们再多说几句关于这个重要概念的话。在日常生活中，质心相当于重心，重心本质上是物体完美平衡的点。如果我们将一个物体平衡地悬挂在一根非常细的杆的尖端或一根金属丝上，那么这根杆或金属丝就会位于质心所在的一条线上。

Before we discuss how to compute the center of mass mathematically, let's see how we can measure it experimentally. Imagine that we have some object with an odd shape, or of an irregular density. We can determine its center of gravity by hanging the object from any arbitrary point on the surface of the object. This defines a vertical line upon which the center of gravity must lie. By repeating the experiment with a different point on the object and finding the intersection of those two lines, we can locate the center of gravity.
在讨论如何用数学方法计算质心之前，我们先来看看如何用实验测量它。假设我们有一个形状奇特或密度不规则的物体。我们可以通过将物体悬挂在其表面的任意一点来确定其重心。这样就定义了一条垂直线，重心必定位于这条垂直线上。通过在物体上不同的点重复实验，并找到这两条线的交点，我们就能找到重心。

The authors performed this experiment on a piece of particle board, as shown in Figure 12.7. First, the board was cut into a purposefully asymmetric shape. Next, we chose three arbitrary locations from which to hang the board, and when the board had finished swinging around, we drew a heavy line on it, coincident with the string by which the board was suspended. Sure enough, physics worked, and the third line passed right through the intersection of the first two lines, at the board's center ofmass.
作者在一块刨花板上进行了这项实验，如图 12.7 所示。首先，我们特意将刨花板切割成不对称的形状。接下来，我们任意选择三个位置悬挂刨花板，待刨花板旋转完毕后，在三个位置上画一条粗线，与悬挂刨花板的绳子重合。果然，物理定律成立，第三条线正好穿过前两条线的交点，也就是刨花板的质心。

Figure 12.7  图 12.7Experimentally measuring the center of mass of a odd-shaped piece of particle board
实验测量异形刨花板的质心

To compute the center of mass mathematically, we imagine the object being divided up into a very large number of small “mass elements.” If there are n such elements, and we denote the mass and position of the i th element as mi and r i , respectively, then the center of mass r c is simplify the weighted average of the positions of all the mass elements.
为了从数学上计算质心，我们设想将物体分成大量小的“质量元素”。如果有 n 个这样的元素，并且我们将第 i 个元素的质量和位置分别表示为 mi 和 r i ，则质心 r c 就是所有质量元素位置的加权平均值。

Calculating the Center of Mass
计算质心
(12.22) r c=1M∑inmi ri .

In Equation (12.22), M is the total mass of the object
在公式（12.22）中， M 是物体的总质量

M=∑inmi.

For our purposes, the most important property of the center of mass is that if the object rotates, it will rotate about its center of mass. This assumes, of course, that the object is freely rotating and there isn't a constraint compelling it to rotate about some other point.
就我们的目的而言，质心最重要的属性是，如果物体旋转，它将绕其质心旋转。当然，这假设物体可以自由旋转，并且没有其他约束迫使它绕其他点旋转。

As an example, consider a sledge hammer. Clearly, the center of mass of the sledge hammer is close to the heavy end of the sledge, not in the middle of the handle. Assume we throw the hammer across the room. As it tumbles through space, any arbitrary point on the hammer will trace out a complicated spiraling shape. The center of mass, however, moves in a parabola, in perfect agreement with the kinematics equations we learned in Chapter 11.
举个例子，考虑一把大锤。显然，大锤的质心靠近锤子的重端，而不是锤柄的中间。假设我们把锤子扔到房间的另一边。当它在空间中翻滚时，锤子上的任意一点都会描绘出一个复杂的螺旋形。然而，它的质心却沿着抛物线运动，这与我们在第 11 章学到的运动学方程完全一致。

The authors couldn't resist the opportunity to chuck big objects around, so we verified this hypothesis experimentally, and you can, too.13 We started with the odd-shaped piece of particle board, whose center of mass had been experimentally located and clearly marked. Next, the fun part:
作者们无法抗拒将大物体扔来扔去的机会，所以我们通过实验验证了这一假设，你也可以。13 我们从一块形状奇特的刨花板开始，它的质心已经通过实验确定，并清晰地标记出来。接下来，有趣的部分来了：

we threw it in the air and took a series of pictures of its trajectory with a camera mounted on a tripod. Finally, we merged these frames together into a single image, and used least-squares to fit a parabola through the points marking the center of mass. The result of the experiment is Figure 12.8.
我们把它抛向空中，并用安装在三脚架上的相机拍摄了一系列关于其轨迹的照片。最后，我们将这些帧合并成一张图片，并用最小二乘法拟合出一条通过质心点的抛物线。实验结果如图 12.8 所示。

Figure 12.8  图 12.8 The center of mass is the special point that obeys the simple kinematic equations from Chapter 11. Any other point traces out a spiraling path as the object rotates.
质心是遵循第 11 章中的简单运动学方程的特殊点。当物体旋转时，任何其他点都会描绘出一条螺旋路径。

One small note: When fitting the parabola, we did not include the first frame in the data set. As you can see, on the first frame the board is still in the assistant's hand, and thus has not yet begun its (parabolic) free fall trajectory.
一个小提示：在拟合抛物线时，我们没有将第一帧的数据纳入数据集。正如你所见，在第一帧中，滑板仍在助手手中，因此尚未开始其（抛物线）自由落体轨迹。

Because an object will rotate about its center of mass when allowed to rotate freely, in a physics simulation is it highly advantageous to select the origin of your object to be at its center of mass. Of course, you may have good reasons to put the origin of the object elsewhere. For example, you may have a graphical representation of an object with the origin placed somewhere that made sense to the artist who made that model. In general, if you place the origin somewhere other than the center of mass, then you will likely have to deal with two “positions” of the object: one position within the physics system that describes the world coordinates of the center of mass, and another, perhaps in the rendering system, for the origin of your
由于物体在允许自由旋转时会绕其质心旋转，因此在物理模拟中，将物体的原点选择在其质心位置非常有利。当然，你也可以有充分的理由将物体的原点放在其他位置。例如，你可能有一个物体的图形表示，其原点位于创建该模型的艺术家认为合理的位置。一般来说，如果你将原点放置在质心以外的某个位置，那么你可能需要处理物体的两个“位置”：一个是物理系统中描述质心世界坐标的位置，另一个可能是渲染系统中的原点。

graphical model. The code that translates between these two conventions is likely to be found either in the interface with the physics engine (for example, the code that updates the position of the objects after the physics simulation has run), or the code that sets up the reference frame for the object during rendering.
图形模型。在这两种约定之间进行转换的代码很可能出现在与物理引擎的接口中（例如，在物理模拟运行后更新对象位置的代码），或者在渲染期间为对象设置参考框架的代码中。

The center of mass is fixed for a rigid body such as a sledge hammer; this assumption has been implicit in the whole discussion; otherwise, it wouldn't make sense to advise setting the origin at the center of mass. However, for a general system with moving parts, such as Earth, the center of mass is a dynamic property, not a constant. The center of mass shifts around within the object as the parts are reconfigured.
对于像大锤这样的刚体来说，质心是固定的；这一假设在整个讨论中都是隐含的；否则，建议将原点设置在质心处是没有意义的。然而，对于像地球这样由运动部件组成的一般系统来说，质心是一个动态属性，而不是一个常数。随着部件的重新配置，质心会在物体内部移动。

For example, imagine if all of the people in the world decided to visit the North Pole at the same time. Assuming we would all fit and there were enough earmuffs to go around, the Earth's center of mass would shift towards the North Pole. This new center of mass, however, would trace out the exact same trajectory as the old one would have. In other words, while the trajectory of the Earth's geometric center would be slightly “southward” from where it would have been if we all stayed at home, the trajectory traced out by the center of mass is the same in either case.
例如，想象一下，如果世界上所有的人都决定同时前往北极。假设我们都能挤进去，而且耳罩数量足够，那么地球的质心就会向北极移动。然而，新的质心轨迹与之前的轨迹完全相同。换句话说，虽然地球几何中心的轨迹会比我们都待在家里时略微“偏南”，但无论哪种情况，质心的轨迹都是相同的。

Or, let's say that instead of visiting the North Pole, we all decided to go to the Galapagos Islands, which is very near the equator. Would Earth's rotation suddenly get all “wobbly” like an out-of-balance ceiling fan? No! Instead, the center of mass would shift towards the Galapagos Islands, and the Earth would rotate about this new center of mass. So although the rotation, when viewed from above, might appear asymmetrical, since the rotation would not be about the center of the spherical Earth (assuming the Earth were perfectly spherical), the rotation would be smooth. An unbalanced ceiling fan is wobbly because it is not free to choose its axis of rotation, and so it must be balanced in order to align the center of mass with the fixed axis of rotation. Earth, however, is not connected to anything, and it is free to rotate about its center of mass, wherever that center of mass may be.
或者，假设我们决定不去北极，而是去加拉帕戈斯群岛，那里离赤道很近。地球的自转会像失衡的吊扇一样突然变得“摇晃”吗？不会！相反，地球的质心会向加拉帕戈斯群岛移动，并围绕这个新的质心旋转。因此，尽管从上方看，由于旋转不是围绕球形地球的中心（假设地球是完美的球形），自转可能看起来不对称，但旋转仍然是平稳的。失衡的吊扇会摇晃，因为它无法自由选择自转轴，因此必须保持平衡才能使质心与固定的自转轴对齐。然而，地球不与任何物体连接，它可以自由地围绕其质心旋转，无论质心位于何处。

Of course, all the people on Earth put together have less mass than our moon, so our discussion has been misleading. The point that traces an ellipse as we orbit the sun isn't the Earth's center of mass at all! It is the center of mass of the entire Earth-moon system. This point isn't really close to Earth's geometric center, although it is beneath the surface, but only because Earth is so much more massive than the moon. As the moon orbits the Earth, the center of mass of the system shifts around within Earth. It is this imaginary point that orbits the sun, not the center of mass of Earthitself.
当然，地球上所有人的质量加起来都比月球的质量小，所以我们的讨论具有误导性。绕太阳公转时，画出椭圆形轨迹的点根本不是地球的质心！它是整个地月系统的质心。这个点实际上并不靠近地球的几何中心，尽管它位于地表之下，但这仅仅是因为地球的质量比月球大得多。当月球绕地球公转时，系统的质心会在地球内部移动。正是这个假想的点绕着太阳公转，而不是地球本身的质心。

12.4Impulsive Forces and Collisions
12.4 冲击力和碰撞

In video games, things are always ramming into each other, so it seems appropriate for us to spend some time talking about collisions. As we've mentioned, in the real world, momentum does not change instantaneously; rather, a large force acts over a very small period of time. However, despite reality (remember the first law of video game physics), it is frequently the case that the interval during which these forces act is below the resolution of our physics time step, and for practical purposes we can consider the change in momentum to have happened instantaneously. The most important and common scenario is when the object is involved in a collision. Since the mass of most objects is constant, an instantaneous change in momentum usually boils down to an instantaneous change in velocity.
在电子游戏中，物体之间总是会发生碰撞，所以我们花点时间讨论一下碰撞似乎很合适。正如我们之前提到的，在现实世界中，动量不会瞬间改变；相反，一个很大的力会在很短的时间内起作用。然而，尽管现实如此（记住电子游戏物理第一定律），这些力作用的时间间隔通常低于我们物理时间步长的分辨率，因此出于实际目的，我们可以将动量的变化视为瞬时发生的。最重要和最常见的情况是物体发生碰撞。由于大多数物体的质量是恒定的，动量的瞬时变化通常归结为速度的瞬时变化。

Consider two objects traveling towards each other in one dimension, with masses m1 and m2 and velocities v1 and v2 , as illustrated in Figure 12.9.
考虑两个物体在一维方向上相向运动，质量分别为 m1 和 m2 ，速度分别为 v1 和 v2 ，如图 12.9 所示。

Figure 12.9  图 12.9A collision  碰撞

Using the momentum relation p=mv , we can calculate the momentum of the two objects (denoted p1 and p2 ) and the system as a whole (denoted as simply p ) before and after the collision. We assume that the masses remain constant and put primes on the symbols that refer to the values after the collision:
利用动量关系 p=mv ，我们可以计算碰撞前后两个物体（分别记为 p1 和 p2 ）以及整个系统（简称为 p ）的动量。我们假设质量保持不变，并在表示碰撞后值的符号上加上撇号：

p1=m1v1,p2=m2v2,p=p1+p2=m1v1+m2v2,p1′=m1v1′,p2′=m2v2′,p′=p1′+p2′=m1v1′+m2v2′.

The change in momentum of each object, according to the law of conservation of momentum, is actually the result of a force acting over time. However, we think of the collision here as producing an instantaneous change in momentum of the two objects. A force that is treated in this way is known as an impulsive force, or more simply, an impulse. Since an impulse is an immediate change in momentum, it has the same units as momentum: ML / T . Note that an impulse is a very different beast from a regular force, which has units ML / T2 . It is very common programmer mistake to use impulses and forces incorrectly, so be sure to watch your units.
根据动量守恒定律，每个物体的动量变化实际上是力随时间变化的结果。然而，我们认为碰撞会导致两个物体动量的瞬时变化。以这种方式处理的力被称为冲量力，或者更简单地称为冲量。由于冲量是动量的即时变化，因此它的单位与动量相同： ML / T 。请注意，冲量与常规力截然不同，常规力的单位是 ML / T2 。程序员经常会犯错误，错误地使用冲量和力，因此请务必注意单位。

When two objects collide, many things can happen, even if we assume they remain intact. A likely scenario is for them to bounce off of each other, changing the signs of both v1 and v2 . Or they may stick together. The former is known as an elastic collision and the latter an inelastic collision. (Actually, only a “perfect bounce” is considered truly elastic. The terms “perfectly inelastic” and “perfectly elastic” are used to refer to the two extremes, while an intermediate collision is described as simply “inelastic.” Section 12.4.2 defines these terms a bit more precisely by using the coefficient of restitution, but to fully understand the distinction requires an understanding of kinetic energy. As we mentioned at the beginning of Chapter 11, energy is certainly an important concept in physics, but it actually doesn't play a central role in the Newton-Euler dynamics used by most real-time simulations, and it isn't discussed much in this book.) The velocity (and momentum) of each object is likely to change, but the law of conservation of momentum says that the total momentum of the system of both objects must remain constant. That is, p=p′ .
当两个物体碰撞时，即使我们假设它们保持完整，也可能会发生许多事情。一种可能的情况是它们相互反弹，从而同时改变 v1 和 v2 的符号。或者它们可能粘在一起。前者称为弹性碰撞，后者称为非弹性碰撞。 （实际上，只有“完美弹跳”才被认为是真正有弹性的。“完全非弹性”和“完全弹性”这两个术语用于指代两个极端，而中间碰撞被简单地描述为“非弹性”。第 12.4.2 节通过使用恢复系数更精确地定义了这些术语，但要完全理解这种区别，需要了解动能。正如我们在第 11 章开头提到的，能量无疑是物理学中的一个重要概念，但它实际上并不在大多数实时模拟使用的牛顿 - 欧拉动力学中扮演核心角色，本书也没有过多讨论。）每个物体的速度（和动量）都可能发生变化，但动量守恒定律规定两个物体系统的总动量必须保持不变。也就是说， p=p′ 。

In general, we cannot predict the individual velocities v1 and v2 using just the law of conservation of momentum, since the conservation of momentum law gives us one equation ( p=p′ ) and there are two unknowns. Before we consider what other bit of information we need, let's look at some simpler cases of collisions and conservation of momentum. Assume for the moment that the collision is perfectly inelastic, that is, the objects stick together upon impact. This gives us the other equation we needed to solve the system of equations: v1′=v2′ .
一般来说，我们无法仅使用动量守恒定律来预测各自的速度 v1 和 v2 ，因为动量守恒定律只给出了一个方程 ( p=p′ )，并且有两个未知数。在考虑我们需要的其他信息之前，让我们先看一些更简单的碰撞和动量守恒情况。暂时假设碰撞是完全非弹性的，也就是说，物体在撞击时会粘在一起。这样我们就得到了解方程组所需的另一个方程： v1′=v2′ 。

12.4.1Perfectly Inelastic Collisions
12.4.1 完全非弹性碰撞

A classic example of an inelastic collision is a gun firing a bullet into a block. Assume that, as illustrated in Figure 12.10, a block of wood weighing 2.00 kg is at rest, hanging from a wire whose mass is neglected. We fire a gun at the block, and the bullet, which has a mass of 10 g, strikes the block with a speed of 350 m/s. The bullet remains stuck in the block. What is the horizontal speed of the block immediately after the impact?
非弹性碰撞的一个典型例子是用枪发射子弹撞击木块。如图 12.10 所示，假设一块重 2.00 千克的木块静止不动，悬挂在一根质量忽略的金属丝上。我们用枪向木块发射子弹，一颗质量为 10 克的子弹以 350 米/秒的速度撞击木块。子弹卡在木块内。撞击后木块的水平速度是多少？

Figure 12.10  图 12.10 A bullet fired into a block suspended by a wire (in other words, a typical episode of MythBusters)
一颗子弹射入一根电线悬挂的木块（换句话说，这是《流言终结者》的典型一集）

First, we compute the initial momentum of the system, which is all contained in the bullet:
首先，我们计算系统的初始动量，它全部包含在子弹中：

p=m1v1+m2v2=(2.00  kg )(0)+(10.0  g )(350  m / s )=3.50  kg m / s .

Now we look for the resulting common velocity, which we'll denote simply as v′ , using the law of conservation of momentum, p=p′ , and the knowledge that this is an inelastic collision, v′=v1′=v2′ :
现在我们利用动量守恒定律 p=p′ 和这是非弹性碰撞的知识 v′=v1′=v2′ 来寻找由此产生的共同速度，我们将其简单地表示为 v′ ：

p′=m1v1′+m2v2′,3.50  kg m / s =(2.00  kg )v′+(10.0  g )v′,3.50  kg m / s =(2.00  kg +10.0  g )v′,(3.50  kg m / s ) / (2.01  kg )=v′,1.74  m / s =v′.

Let's look at one more example of an inelastic collision, this time in 2D. Consider a driver who runs a red light and crashes into a car crossing the intersection. Let's say that Grant is the safe driver, and at the time of the collision, Grant and his fuel-efficient hybrid have a combined mass of 1,500 kg and are traveling west at 35 km/hr. Kari,14 who is not paying attention, sees Grant's car too late, and swerves to the left. She and her car have a combined mass of 2,500 kg. At impact, she is traveling at 65 km/hr, heading 25° west of north, as shown in Figure 12.11. Assume that we can treat the collision as inelastic. What is the velocity of the crash just after the collision?15
让我们再看一个非弹性碰撞的例子，这次是二维的。假设一名司机闯红灯，撞上了一辆正在穿过十字路口的汽车。假设格兰特是安全驾驶员，碰撞发生时，格兰特和他的省油混合动力汽车总质量为 1,500 公斤，正以 35 公里/小时的速度向西行驶。14 岁的卡丽没有注意，太晚才看到格兰特的车，于是向左急转弯。她和她的车总质量为 2,500 公斤。撞击时，她的行驶速度为 65 公里/小时，方向为北偏西 25°，如图 12.11 所示。假设我们可以将这次碰撞视为非弹性碰撞。碰撞后，碰撞速度是多少？15

Figure 12.11  图 12.11A car crash  一场车祸

To solve this problem, let's set up a 2D coordinate space where +x is east and +y is north. We compute the total momentum before the crash as
为了解决这个问题，我们设置一个二维坐标空间，其中 +x 为东， +y 为北。我们计算碰撞前的总动量为

P =m1 v 1+m2 v 2=(1,500  kg )(35  km / hr ) [ −1 0 ] +(2,500  kg )(65  km / hr ) [ cos⁡115 o sin⁡115 o ] =(52,500  kg km / hr ) [ −1 0 ] +(162,500  kg km / hr ) [ −0.423 0.906 ] = ( [ −52,500 0 ] + [ −68,700 147,000 ] )   kg km / hr = [ −121,200 147,000 ]   kg km / hr .

The resulting velocity of the glob of two cars is simply the momentum we have just computed divided by the total combined mass:
两辆车组合在一起的最终速度就是我们刚刚计算出的动量除以总质量：

v ′= P ′ / (m1+m2)= ( [ −121,200 147,000 ]   kg km / hr ) / (1,500  kg +2,500  kg )= ( [ −121,200 147,000 ]   kg km / hr ) / (4,000  kg )= [ −30.3 36.8 ]   km / hr .

12.4.2General Collision Response
12.4.2 通用碰撞响应

Simple inelastic collisions can be solved by using the principle of conservation of momentum, but how do we compute the velocities in the general case? Before we can fully answer that question, we need to consider the context in which it is asked. Dealing with collisions is typically a two-step process. First, we must detect that a collision has occurred, meaning the objects are already penetrating, or that a collision is about to occur in this time step. The second step is to take measures to resolve or prevent the collision. The former task is known as collision detection, and the latter as collision response. Our purpose at this time is to discuss collisions in theoretical terms (we touch on a few practical issues related to how physics simulations really work in Section 12.6), so for now let us merely attempt a general explanation of how the momentum of rigid bodies changes in response to collision. We assume that we already know that two objects have collided, and we wish to predict their behavior after thecollision.
简单的非弹性碰撞可以利用动量守恒原理来解决，但在一般情况下，我们如何计算速度呢？在完全回答这个问题之前，我们需要考虑提出这个问题的背景。处理碰撞通常分为两个步骤。首先，我们必须检测到碰撞已经发生，这意味着物体已经穿透，或者在这个时间步长内即将发生碰撞。第二步是采取措施解决或防止碰撞。前一步称为碰撞检测，后一步称为碰撞响应。我们目前的目的是从理论上讨论碰撞（我们将在 12.6 节中讨论一些与物理模拟实际工作原理相关的实际问题），因此现在我们仅尝试对刚体的动量在碰撞过程中如何变化进行一般性解释。我们假设我们已经知道两个物体发生了碰撞，并且我们希望预测它们在碰撞后的行为。

To do this, either in the abstract in a physics problem, or in collision response code in a digital simulation, we typically need to know not just that two objects have collided, but also where they collided, and how the two objects were oriented relative to each other at the point of contact. For example, in the car crash between Grant and Kari, we need to know that Grant's car was hit near the left door, and Kari's in her right front fender. Of course, a collision doesn't necessarily happen at a single point. Often an edge of one object may touch a surface of another, or perhaps entire surfaces are in contact. At the time of this writing, most real-time collision detection systems do not return collisions in such a descriptive manner, nor are collision response systems really capable of making use of that extra information. The closest we get is for the detection system to locate several points of contact (or penetration) and then to process that list in some way (for example, by finding their convex hull or looking for an average surface normal). In any case, the best way to do this quickly is very much at the forefront of research, and as such doesn't belong in an introductory book like this. Here we just consider the principles involved in a single point of contact. More advanced techniques build upon these principles.
为了实现这一点，无论是在抽象的物理问题中，还是在数字模拟的碰撞响应代码中，我们通常不仅需要知道两个物体发生了碰撞，还需要知道它们碰撞的位置，以及两个物体在接触点处的相对方向。例如，在格兰特和卡莉的车祸中，我们需要知道格兰特的车撞到了左车门附近，而卡莉的车撞到了右前挡泥板。当然，碰撞不一定发生在单个点上。通常，一个物体的边缘可能接触另一个物体的表面，或者整个表面都接触。在撰写本文时，大多数实时碰撞检测系统并没有以这种描述性的方式返回碰撞，碰撞响应系统也无法真正利用这些额外的信息。我们最接近的做法是让检测系统找到几个接触点（或穿透点），然后以某种方式处理该列表（例如，通过找到它们的凸包或寻找平均表面法线）。无论如何，快速实现这一目标的最佳方法正处于研究的前沿，因此不宜写进这样的入门书籍。我们这里只讨论单点接触所涉及的原理。更先进的技术将基于这些原理。

Figure 12.12 shows some example collision results that might be returned from a collision detection system. Note that each collision result (black arrow) has a point of contact (at the tail of the arrow), and a surface normal, usually assumed to be a unit vector. An arbitrary convention is chosen for which way the normal will point; in Figure 12.12 it points away from the “first” object. Furthermore, the two objects may be arbitrarily assigned the roles of “first” and “second” objects, perhaps by the luck of the draw that the objects happened to be in some space-partitioning structure. These assignments can even vary frame-by-frame, so the response calculation must be symmetric. What is not depicted in the diagram is that a penetration depth is often returned if the objects are already penetrating.
图 12.12 显示了一些碰撞检测系统可能返回的碰撞结果示例。请注意，每个碰撞结果（黑色箭头）都有一个接触点（位于箭头尾部）和一个表面法线，通常假定为单位向量。法线指向的方向可以随意约定；在图 12.12 中，它指向远离“第一个”物体的方向。此外，这两个物体可能被任意分配“第一个”和“第二个”物体的角色，这可能是碰巧碰巧它们位于某种空间分区结构中。这些分配甚至可能逐帧变化，因此响应计算必须是对称的。图中未显示的是，如果物体已经穿透，通常会返回穿透深度。

Figure 12.12  图 12.12 Examples of the types of results returned by collision detection.
碰撞检测返回的结果类型的示例。

And always, we should bear in mind the first law of video game physics. Not all collisions in video games must be between “real” objects, meaning those objects that are represented in the physics system. For example, consider a game with a kick mechanic. It may be helpful to treat a kick as a “collision” with an object, even if the character's foot is not in the physics system or if this collision was determined by simple proximity tests or raycasting that were designed based on gameplay goals and not reality. (The player character may have been too far away or too close for the kick to really have hit the target; but that is irrelevant.) It might be highly useful for the response to this action to be handled in a manner similar to ordinary collisions. For example, a sound and particle effect plays, the object receives a reduction in hit points, and its visual appearance changes, etc. In this case, in order to use the same collision response code for both ordinary collisions and “virtual” collisions such as player kicks (even if it is just to get the cosmetic effects right), you may need to synthesize values ordinarily provided by the collision detection system for your “virtual” collisions, such as the mass and velocity of the foot, and the point of contact and surface normal.
我们应该始终牢记电子游戏物理第一定律。电子游戏中的碰撞并非都必须发生在“真实”物体之间，也就是物理系统中所呈现的物体。例如，假设一款包含踢球机制的游戏。将踢球视为与物体的“碰撞”可能会有所帮助，即使角色的脚不在物理系统中，或者这种碰撞是通过基于游戏目标而非现实设计的简单接近度测试或光线投射确定的。（玩家角色可能距离目标太远或太近，导致踢球无法真正击中目标；但这无关紧要。）以类似于普通碰撞的方式处理对此动作的响应可能非常有用。例如，播放声音和粒子效果，对象的生命值减少，其视觉外观发生变化等。在这种情况下，为了对普通碰撞和“虚拟”碰撞（如玩家踢腿）使用相同的碰撞响应代码（即使只是为了获得正确的外观效果），您可能需要合成碰撞检测系统通常为“虚拟”碰撞提供的值，例如脚的质量和速度，以及接触点和表面法线。

One final caveat is that we are concerned only with linear momentum for now; our objects do not rotate. This means that the explanation we give in this section will be incomplete. However, it will be helpful to cover the general principles here in a context free of the extra complexity that comes with rotation.
最后需要注意的是，我们目前只关注线性动量；我们的物体不旋转。这意味着我们在本节中给出的解释是不完整的。然而，在一个不受旋转带来的额外复杂性影响的环境中讲解一般原理将会很有帮助。

Now to the heart of the matter. Assuming we have somehow detected a collision and obtained a position and normal, how do we determine the resulting velocities for the collision response? Here we show the usual method, following an article by Chris Hecker [7]. We start by reviewing our guiding principles.
现在回到问题的核心。假设我们以某种方式检测到了碰撞，并获得了位置和法线，那么我们如何确定碰撞响应的最终速度呢？这里我们展示了一种常用的方法，参考了 Chris Hecker [7] 的一篇文章。我们首先回顾一下我们的指导原则。

Our first guiding principle is that, although we know that in reality a very large force acts for a short period of time, the period of time is so short relative to our time step that we will consider the collision response to occur instantaneously. That is, we will not be calculating a force, but rather an impulse, which will result in an instantaneous change in momentum of the objects.
我们的第一个指导原则是，虽然我们知道现实中很大的力作用的时间很短，但相对于我们的时间步长来说，这段时间太短了，所以我们将碰撞响应视为瞬时发生的。也就是说，我们计算的不是力，而是冲量，这将导致物体动量的瞬时变化。

The second guiding principle is given to us by Newton's third law: whatever (impulsive) force is applied to one object, the opposite force must be applied to the other object. The conservation of momentum law essentially says the same thing: if we change the momentum of one object, we must make the opposite change in momentum to the other object so that the total momentum of the system after the collision is the same as the total momentum before the collision.
第二个指导原则来自牛顿第三定律：无论对一个物体施加什么（冲量）力，都必须对另一个物体施加相反的力。动量守恒定律本质上也表达了同样的意思：如果我们改变一个物体的动量，就必须对另一个物体做出相反的动量改变，以使碰撞后系统的总动量与碰撞前的总动量相同。

Thus, to resolve a collision between two objects, the game plan is to compute an impulse with the proper magnitude and apply that impulse to both objects, but in opposite directions. An impulse is a vector quantity, and so we need to know its magnitude and direction. The direction is given to us already: it is the surface normal provided by the collision detection system. The details of selecting a surface normal is a matter of collision detection, not response, and will not be discussed here. But notice that if the objects move parallel to this normal, they are either making the problem worse (penetrating further) or better (moving apart and resolving the penetration). In contrast, if we assume the penetration distance is relatively small and the surfaces are locally flat and perpendicular to the normal near the point of contact, then any motion perpendicular to the surface normal does not cause the penetration distance to change. So the surface normal is really the only direction that matters.
因此，为了解决两个物体之间的碰撞，策略是计算一个具有适当幅值的冲量，并将该冲量以相反的方向施加于两个物体。冲量是矢量，因此我们需要知道它的大小和方向。方向已经给定：它是碰撞检测系统提供的表面法线。选择表面法线的细节与碰撞检测有关，而非响应，本文不作讨论。但请注意，如果物体平行于该法线移动，它们要么会使问题变得更糟（进一步穿透），要么会使问题变得更好（移开并解决穿透问题）。相反，如果我们假设穿透距离相对较小，并且表面局部平坦且垂直于接触点附近的法线，那么任何垂直于表面法线的运动都不会导致穿透距离发生变化。因此，表面法线实际上是唯一重要的方向。

In summary, our task is to determine the proper magnitude of an impulse that will be directed along the surface normal and will resolve (or prevent) the penetration. To merely prevent a penetration that has not yet occurred, we need only remove any relative velocity acting parallel to the surface normal. This portion of the relative velocity is the velocity that, if applied to move the objects forward in time, would result in penetration. Any relative velocity acting perpendicular to the normal is OK and does not need to be counteracted, according to our assumption that the surfaces are locally flat near the point of contact. As illustrated in Figure 12.13, the velocity of m1 relative to m2 is computed as v rel = v 1− v 2 , and the length of this projection onto the normal is given by n ⋅ v rel .
总而言之，我们的任务是确定沿表面法线方向的冲量的适当幅值，该冲量将解决（或阻止）穿透。如果仅仅为了阻止尚未发生的穿透，我们只需消除任何平行于表面法线的相对速度。这部分相对速度是这样的，如果应用该速度来使物体随时间向前移动，就会导致穿透。根据我们假设表面在接触点附近局部是平坦的，任何垂直于法线的相对速度都是可以的，不需要抵消。如图 12.13 所示， m1 相对于 m2 的速度计算为 v rel = v 1− v 2 ，该速度在法线上的投影长度由 n ⋅ v rel 给出。

Figure 12.13  图 12.13 Computing the amount of relative velocity acting parallel to the surface normal
计算平行于表面法线的相对速度

Canceling the relative velocity will prevent penetration, but it's not always the correct response. When objects collide, they don't just come to a stop next to each other—they bounce off each other. So we're missing an ingredient that describes the difference in the collision responses of a dropped beanbag and a dropped SuperBall. A simple and popular collision law (though not the only one) that can be used to discriminate between these cases is Newton's collision law. This law introduces the coefficient of restitution, denoted e , which is a fractional number that relates the magnitude of the relative velocity along the surface normal after the collision with the same value measured just before the collision. When e=0 , the post-collision velocity along the normal is zero, and we have a perfectly inelastic collision. Using e=1 produces a perfectly elastic collision, where the relative velocity along the normal has the same magnitude (but opposite sign) as before the collision. Dropping a beanbag onto carpet is a close example of an inelastic collision, whereas dropping a SuperBall is a highly elastic collision. Using the formulas from Section 11.6, we can also show that, if an object is dropped and allowed to bounce multiple times, the coefficient of restitution gives the ratio of apex heights at successive bounces.
消除相对速度可以防止穿透，但这并不总是正确的反应。当物体碰撞时，它们不会只是彼此相邻地停止——它们会相互弹开。因此，我们缺少一个能够描述掉落的豆袋和掉落的超级球的碰撞响应差异的要素。一个简单而流行的碰撞定律（尽管并非唯一定律）可以用来区分这两种情况，那就是牛顿碰撞定律。该定律引入了恢复系数，表示为 e ，它是一个分数，它将碰撞后沿表面法线的相对速度大小与碰撞前测量的相同值联系起来。当 e=0 时，碰撞后沿法线的速度为零，我们得到的是完全非弹性碰撞。使用 e=1 会产生完全弹性碰撞，其中沿法线的相对速度与碰撞前的大小相同（但符号相反）。将豆袋掉落在地毯上是一个接近非弹性碰撞的例子，而将超级球掉落在地毯上则是高度弹性碰撞。使用第 11.6 节中的公式，我们还可以证明，如果一个物体掉落并允许其多次弹跳，则恢复系数给出了连续弹跳时顶点高度的比率。

Let's denote the magnitude of the collision response impulse as k . The first mass, m1 , will receive the (vector) impulse −k n , while m2 undergoes the opposite change in momentum of k n . The signs are based on our arbitrary choice of the direction of the surface normal. Now that we know what we want, calculating the proper k to cancel the relative velocity is a straightforward algebraic exercise. As before, we denote the post-collision values with primes. An impulse is an instantaneous change of momentum, so the post-collision momentum of the first object is P 1′= P 1−k n . Dividing by the mass and remembering P =m v , we express the post-collision velocities as
我们将碰撞响应冲量的幅值表示为 k 。第一个质量 m1 将受到（矢量）冲量 −k n ，而 m2 则经历相反的动量变化 k n 。符号基于我们对表面法线方向的任意选择。现在我们知道了我们想要什么，计算适当的 k 来抵消相对速度就是一个简单的代数练习。和以前一样，我们用撇号表示碰撞后的值。冲量是动量的瞬时变化，因此第一个物体碰撞后的动量为 P 1′= P 1−k n 。除以质量并记住 P =m v ，我们将碰撞后速度表示为

Post-collision velocities
碰撞后速度
v 1′= v 1−k n / m1, v 2′= v 2+k n / m2.

The post-collision relative velocity is simply their difference, v rel ′= v 1′− v 2′ . We solve for k by expressing the resulting relative velocity along the normal as the desired multiple of the relative velocity along the normal before impact.
碰撞后的相对速度就是它们的差值 v rel ′= v 1′− v 2′ 。我们通过将碰撞后沿法线的相对速度表示为碰撞前沿法线的相对速度的期望倍数来求解 k 。

Solving for k , the magnitude of the impulse
解出 k ，即脉冲的幅度
v rel ′⋅ n =−e v rel ⋅ n ,( v 1′− v 2′)⋅ n =−e v rel ⋅ n ,[( v 1−k n / m1)−( v 2+k n / m2)]⋅ n =−e v rel ⋅ n ,[( v 1− v 2)−(k n / m1+k n / m2)]⋅ n =−e v rel ⋅ n ,[ v rel −k(1 / m1+1 / m2) n ]⋅ n =−e v rel ⋅ n , v rel ⋅ n −k(1 / m1+1 / m2) n ⋅ n =−e v rel ⋅ n ,k(1 / m1+1 / m2) n ⋅ n =(e+1) v rel ⋅ n ,(12.23)k= (e+1) v rel ⋅ n (1 / m1+1 / m2) n ⋅ n .

Equation (12.23) can be simplified slightly in the common case that n is known to have unit length. If n is not a unit vector, then the change to k as a result of the length of n is balanced by the calculation of the (vector) impulse k n . Thus k is the true magnitude of the impulse only when n is a unit vector.
在已知 n 为单位长度的常见情况下，公式 (12.23) 可以稍微简化。如果 n 不是单位向量，则 n 的长度导致的 k 的变化可以通过计算（向量）冲量 k n 来平衡。因此，只有当 n 为单位向量时， k 才是冲量的真实幅值。

Let's work through a few examples of Equation (12.23). First, let's see how the coefficient of restitution can be used to describe the difference between dropping a beanbag and a SuperBall. We'll be dropping these objects onto a concrete floor, which is an enlightening example because it shows how immovable objects can be easily handled in most physics engines by acting as if they have infinite mass. As it turns out, the inverse mass is the quantity we usually work with in calculations involving such special objects (as illustrated in Equation (12.23)). Furthermore, the inverse mass (and its analog, the inverse inertia tensor, to be discussed later) are derived quantities that are needed so frequently that they are often precomputed. This means that physics code can often work with immovable16 objects without treating them as a special case, simply by setting the inverse mass equal to zero. When one of the inverse masses is zero, we could actually deal directly with velocities and bypass Equation (12.23), since k will be proportional to the mass but the velocity change as a result of applying k is inversely proportional to the mass. Later, we solve a general case example where no such simplifications are possible.
让我们来研究一下公式 (12.23) 的几个例子。首先，我们来看看如何用恢复系数来描述豆袋和超级球落地的区别。我们会把这些物体落地到混凝土地板上，这是一个很有启发性的例子，因为它展示了大多数物理引擎如何通过将不可移动的物体视为具有无限质量来轻松处理它们。事实证明，质量倒数是我们通常在涉及此类特殊物体的计算中使用的量（如公式 (12.23) 所示）。此外，质量倒数（以及它的类似物，惯性张量倒数，稍后将讨论）是派生量，它们非常常用，因此通常需要预先计算。这意味着物理代码通常可以处理不可移动的 16 个物体，而无需将它们视为特例，只需将质量倒数设置为零即可。当其中一个质量倒数为零时，我们实际上可以直接处理速度，而绕过公式 (12.23)，因为 k 与质量成正比，而施加 k 引起的速度变化与质量成反比。稍后，我们将求解一个无法进行此类简化的一般情况。

Let's say we have one SuperBall and one beanbag, each weighing 50 grams. To avoid making the solution to our example completely obvious without Equation (12.23), we will arrange for the point of impact to occur on an inclined surface, so that n is not a trivial cardinal axis. Since we are not bound to use a unit vector, let's say that n =[1,3] . In our imagination, we throw both objects in exactly the same way, such that the impact velocity in both cases is v 2=[−4,−4] . This is illustrated in Figure 12.14.
假设我们有一个超级球和一个豆袋，每个重 50 克。为了避免在没有公式 (12.23) 的情况下使示例的解完全显而易见，我们将撞击点安排在一个倾斜的表面上，这样 n 就不是平凡的主轴。由于我们不必使用单位向量，因此我们假设 n =[1,3] 。想象我们以完全相同的方式抛出这两个物体，使得两种情况下的撞击速度均为 v 2=[−4,−4] 。如图 12.14 所示。

Figure 12.14  图 12.14 Bouncing a beanbag or SuperBall off of an inclined surface
将豆袋或超级球从倾斜的表面弹起

To determine the resulting velocity, we first solve for k , the scale factor for the impulse. To do this, we must choose a coefficient of restitution. For the SuperBall collision, we'll use e=0.9 , which is near the advertised value. Solving for k (remember that v rel = v 1− v 2 ) we get
为了确定最终速度，我们首先求解冲量的尺度因子 k 。为此，我们必须选择一个恢复系数。对于 SuperBall 碰撞，我们将使用 e=0.9 ，它接近官方给出的值。求解 k （记住 v rel = v 1− v 2 ），我们得到

Calculating the impulse multiplier k for the SuperBall
计算超级球的冲量乘数 k
k= (e+1) v rel ⋅ n (1 / m1+1 / m2) n ⋅ n = (0.9+1) [ 4  m / s 4  m / s ] ⋅ [ 1 3 ] (0+1 / (50  g )) [ 1 3 ] ⋅ [ 1 3 ] = 1.9(16  m / s ) 10 / (50  g ) =152  g   m / s .

To compute the post-collision velocity, we add an impulse of k n to the momentum of the SuperBall. Since momentum is mass times velocity, the change in velocity is equal to this impulse divided by m2 , the mass of the SuperBall:
为了计算碰撞后的速度，我们在超级球的动量上加上一个冲量 k n 。由于动量等于质量乘以速度，因此速度的变化等于这个冲量除以超级球的质量 m2 ：

Calculating the post-impulse velocity for the SuperBall
计算 SuperBall 的冲击后速度
v 2′= v 2+ k n m2 = [ −4  m / s −4  m / s ] + (152  g   m / s ) [ 1 3 ] 50  g = [ −4  m / s −4  m / s ] + [ 3.04  m / s 9.12  m / s ] = [ −0.96  m / s   5.12  m / s ] .

Before we show this velocity graphically, let's look at the beanbag. We treat the beanbag collision as almost completely inelastic and use e=0.01 . Other than the change to e , the procedure is the same as for the SuperBall:
在用图形展示这个速度之前，我们先来看一下豆袋。我们将豆袋碰撞视为几乎完全非弹性的，并使用 e=0.01 。除了更改为 e 之外，该过程与超级球相同：

Calculating the impulse multiplier k and post-impulse velocity for the beanbag
计算豆袋的冲量乘数 k 和冲量后速度
k= (e+1) v rel ⋅ n (1 / m1+1 / m2) n ⋅ n = 1.01(16  m / s ) 10 / (50  g ) =80.8  g   m / s , v 2′= v 2+ k n m2 = [ −4  m / s −4  m / s ] + (80.8  g   m / s ) [ 1 3 ] 50  g = [ −2.38  m / s   0.85  m / s ] .

Notice that the reduced coefficient of restitution caused the beanbag to receive a smaller impulse scale, and the resulting bounce velocity was also lower. This difference is shown graphically in Figure 12.15. For comparison, we've also included a perfectly inelastic collision ( e=1 ). The perfectly inelastic collision ( e=0 ) is very close to the beanbag result and is not depicted.
请注意，降低的恢复系数导致豆袋受到的冲量较小，因此产生的弹跳速度也较低。图 12.15 以图形方式显示了这一差异。为了进行比较，我们还添加了一个完全非弹性碰撞 ( e=1 )。完全非弹性碰撞 ( e=0 ) 与豆袋碰撞的结果非常接近，因此未显示出来。

Figure 12.15  图 12.15 Post-impact velocities for different values of e , the coefficient of restitution
不同恢复系数 e 值的撞击后速度

It is obvious from the beanbag trajectory in Figure 12.15 that an important aspect of collisions is not captured by the model: friction. The velocity perpendicular to the normal is the same before and after the collision. We would expect an object like a beanbag to scrub off a great deal of horizontal velocity as a result of the collision—in fact, it might come to a stop completely. The correct thing to do is to add in a perpendicular component to the impulse. However, correct handling of friction is, in general, a tricky business, and it remains at the forefront of real-time simulation research. Many current methods for calculating the horizontal impulse (especially for sliding contact) fall under the category of “completely fudged.”
从图 12.15 中的豆袋轨迹可以明显看出，模型没有捕捉到碰撞的一个重要方面：摩擦力。垂直于法线的速度在碰撞前后相同。我们预计像豆袋这样的物体会因碰撞而消除大量的水平速度——事实上，它可能会完全停止。正确的做法是在冲量中添加一个垂直分量。然而，正确处理摩擦力通常是一项棘手的工作，并且它仍然是实时模拟研究的前沿。许多当前计算水平冲量（尤其是滑动接触）的方法都属于“完全敷衍了事”的范畴。

In the previous example, we only had one “live” object and the other object was inert. This is a special case, and the equations could be simplified. (As we mentioned earlier, the mass of the projectile cancels itself out and is not needed.) In Exercise 9, we ask you to consider what would happen if Grant and Kari's collision were not perfectly inelastic; the full power of this law is needed in this case. We show how to handle collisions where the objects are free to rotate in Section 12.5.4.
在前面的例子中，我们只有一个“活”物体，另一个物体是惰性的。这是一个特例，方程可以简化。（正如我们之前提到的，抛射体的质量会自行抵消，因此不需要考虑。）在练习 9 中，我们要求你思考，如果 Grant 和 Kari 的碰撞不是完全非弹性的，会发生什么；在这种情况下，需要充分利用这条定律的威力。我们将在 12.5.4 节中展示如何处理物体可以自由旋转的碰撞。

We have been assuming thus far that the objects are in contact, but are not yet penetrating. This might not be the case, depending on the overall strategy used to resolve collisions. One technique is to attempt to reverse the simulation in time back to the point of contact. This can be difficult to do efficiently because there are frequently many, many collisions that happen at different times within a single time step. Furthermore, defining “exactly in contact” is difficult when using floating point math. Another strategy is to simply allow penetration, and apply the impulse to objects that are already penetrating. In this case, the impulse must do more than remove the relative velocity to prevent (further) penetration. The resulting relative velocity must be sufficiently large to separate the objects by the end of the time step, after it has been integrated into the position. In other words, the positions of the objects will be advanced at a rate according to the calculated velocities; after this update, the penetration needs to be resolved. Or at least it needs to be mostly resolved. There are some advantages to allowing some small penetration. All of these issues are a bit outside the realm of established principles and fall more under the heading of current research,17 and they will not be discussed here.
到目前为止，我们一直假设物体接触，但尚未穿透。实际情况可能并非如此，这取决于解决碰撞的整体策略。一种技术是尝试将模拟时间反转回接触点。这可能很难有效地实现，因为在一个时间步长内，不同的时间点经常会发生很多次碰撞。此外，使用浮点数学时，定义“精确接触”也很困难。另一种策略是简单地允许穿透，并将冲量施加到已经穿透的物体上。在这种情况下，冲量的作用不仅仅是消除相对速度以阻止（进一步）穿透。产生的相对速度必须足够大，以便在时间步长结束时，在积分到位置之后将物体分开。换句话说，物体的位置将根据计算出的速度以一定的速率前进；在此更新之后，需要解决穿透问题。或者至少需要基本解决。允许少量穿透有一些好处。所有这些问题都有点超出既定原则的范围，更多地属于当前研究的范畴，17 因此本文不再讨论。

12.4.3The Dirac Delta  12.4.3 狄拉克δ

Before we leave linear dynamics and talk about rotational dynamics, let's mention briefly one bit of mathematical notation you might see, especially in the context of impulses. As we've said, many natural phenomena (such as momentum) do not change instantaneously in theory, but for practical purposes we treat them as changing instantaneously. Furthermore, it is often the case where a body of mathematical tools exists to handle continuous functions (or, equivalently, “signals”), and we wish to apply those tools to signals with discontinuities. There is a handy mathematical kludge that can be used to encode a discontinuity in a function such that it can be integrated. It is known as the Dirac delta, and is usually denoted with the lowercase letter delta, for example δ(a) .
在我们结束线性动力学并讨论旋转动力学之前，让我们简要介绍一下你可能会看到的一些数学符号，尤其是在脉冲的背景下。正如我们所说，许多自然现象（例如动量）在理论上不会瞬时变化，但出于实际目的，我们将其视为瞬时变化。此外，通常情况下，存在一套数学工具来处理连续函数（或等效地称为“信号”），我们希望将这些工具应用于具有不连续性的信号。有一个方便的数学组合可以用来对函数中的不连续性进行编码，以便对其进行积分。它被称为狄拉克δ（Dirac delta），通常用小写字母 delta 表示，例如 δ(a) 。

The symbol δ(t) is a special sort of function, which is a spike, or impulse. Its value is zero everywhere except at t=0 , where it is infinite. But the actual values of the Dirac delta are not to be taken too literally—what is more important is that its integral (the “area” of this infinite spike) is equal to 1. The best way to think about the Dirac delta is as a box centered at 0 with width w and height 1 / w . (Other shapes may be chosen, but the important point is that the shape must have unit area.) The Dirac delta is defined as the limit of such a function, as the width approaches zero, and the height approaches infinity, all the while maintaining the unit area. We like the advice of Bracewell [2], which is to avoid using the term “function” when referring to special, uh, functions such as the Dirac delta, and instead use the word “symbol.” This is because whenever we see the Dirac delta symbol, the entire surrounding expression should be interpreted as a limit. We are considering the limit as the width approaches zero of some shape with unit area centered at the origin.
符号 δ(t) 是一种特殊的函数，它是一个尖峰或脉冲。除了在 t=0 处它的值无穷大之外，其他处它的值都为零。但狄拉克δ的实际值不能过于字面地理解——更重要的是它的积分（这个无穷尖峰的“面积”）等于 1。理解狄拉克δ的最佳方式是将它看作一个以 0 为中心、宽度 w 和高度 1 / w 的盒子。（也可以选择其他形状，但重点是形状必须具有单位面积。）狄拉克δ被定义为此类函数的极限，即宽度趋近于零，高度趋近于无穷大，同时保持单位面积。我们喜欢 Bracewell [2] 的建议，即在提及诸如狄拉克δ之类的特殊函数时避免使用“函数”一词，而应使用“符号”一词。这是因为每当我们看到狄拉克δ符号时，整个周围的表达式都应该被解释为极限。我们正在考虑当单位面积以原点为中心时某些形状的宽度趋近于零时的极限。

Armed with the Dirac delta, we can differentiate functions with discontinuities. For example, let's say the velocity of a baseball being struck by a bat at time t=2 is approximated by the discontinuous function
有了狄拉克δ函数，我们就可以对不连续函数进行微分。例如，假设在时间 t=2 处，棒球被球棒击中的速度可以用不连续函数来近似

v(t)= {−130  ft / s t<2,130  ft / s t≥2.

We can differentiate this expression by using the Dirac delta as
我们可以用狄拉克 delta 来区分这个表达式

v′(t)=260δ(t−2),

which can be read as “an impulse of magnitude 260 at 2.” Remember that the δ symbol is not an ordinary function, and so we interpret the above as “the limit of a total change in velocity of 260 ft/s that takes place over an interval of duration Δt surrounding the time t=2 , as Δt approaches zero.”
可以理解为“在 2 处产生幅度为 260 的脉冲”。请记住，符号 δ 不是普通函数，因此我们将上述内容解释为“在时间 t=2 附近的持续时间 Δt 间隔内，当 Δt 趋近于零时，速度总变化量为 260 ft/s 的极限”。

The Dirac delta comes up in a variety of contexts where tools from continuous math are applied to discontinuous signals. For example, in graphics, the screen-space image is a signal with inherent discontinuities, and we need to sample this signal and reconstruct it. The user's input via the controller is another signal that exhibits discontinuities. The Dirac delta and other related symbols (such as the ramp function and Heaviside's step function) are helpful in discussing and manipulating such signals.
狄拉克δ函数在各种情况下都会出现，这些情况下，连续数学工具会应用于不连续信号。例如，在图形学中，屏幕空间图像是一个具有固有不连续性的信号，我们需要对该信号进行采样并重建。用户通过控制器的输入是另一个表现出不连续性的信号。狄拉克δ函数和其他相关符号（例如斜坡函数和赫维赛德阶跃函数）有助于讨论和处理此类信号。

12.5Rotational Dynamics  12.5 旋转动力学

We are now ready to extend the ideas we have learned about particles to rigid bodies. Particles have position, but until now we have not concerned ourselves with orientation. Likewise, particles have mass, but until now we have not thought about the size or shape of a particle and how that mass was distributed. The key linear quantities and laws each have rotational analogs, and there is a certain beautiful correspondence between them. This correspondence is certainly pedagogically convenient and will be leveraged in our discussion. As we did for linear dynamics, we first define the basic kinematics quantities and consider those issues related to describing the rotation without worrying about the causes of the rotation. We then examine the rotational analogs to mass, force, and momentum, although we will discuss these topics in a different order.
现在，我们准备将所学的粒子概念扩展到刚体。粒子具有位置，但迄今为止我们还没有考虑其方向。同样，粒子具有质量，但迄今为止我们还没有考虑过粒子的大小、形状以及质量的分布。关键的线性量和定律都有相应的旋转对应物，它们之间存在着某种巧妙的对应关系。这种对应关系在教学上非常方便，并将在我们的讨论中得到运用。正如我们在线性动力学中所做的那样，我们首先定义基本的运动学量，并考虑与描述旋转相关的问题，而无需考虑旋转的原因。然后，我们将研究质量、力和动量的旋转对应物，不过我们将以不同的顺序讨论这些主题。

You might notice that this section is surprisingly brief, both compared to our discussion of linear matters, and also similar presentations of other sources. There are two reasons for this. First, we spent considerable time in the previous chapter building up intuition about derivatives and linear dynamics, and these ideas need not be repeated here—though there will be some important differences concerning integration of angular displacement. Second, there are certain prerequisites that are usually bundled in this discussion in traditional physics books; in this book, it has been more appropriate to place these prerequisites elsewhere. You should make sure you have read and understood these prerequisites before reading the rest of this section. In particular, we use the cross product, which we covered in Section 2.12, and basic methods for describing rotation in three dimensions, which were the subject of Chapter 8.
你可能会注意到，本节内容出奇地简短，无论是与我们之前关于线性问题的讨论相比，还是与其他资料的类似介绍相比。原因有二。首先，我们在上一章中花费了大量时间建立关于导数和线性动力学的直观理解，这些概念无需在此重复——尽管在角位移积分方面会有一些重要的差异。其次，在传统的物理书籍中，某些先决条件通常会与本节讨论捆绑在一起；而在本书中，将这些先决条件放在其他地方更为合适。在阅读本节的其余部分之前，你应该确保已经阅读并理解了这些先决条件。特别是，我们使用了第 2.12 节中介绍的叉积，以及描述三维旋转的基本方法，这些方法是第 8 章的主题。

12.5.1Rotational Kinematics
12.5.1 旋转运动学

Chapter 11 was about linear kinematics: we considered a function p (t) that described the position of a particle as a function of time. We also considered its first and second derivatives, the velocity and acceleration functions, which we denoted v (t)= p˙ (t) and a (t)= p¨ (t) , respectively. The rotational analog of position is, of course, orientation. Several methods can be used to describe the orientation of a body. A considerable number of pages were spent explaining and comparing these methods in Chapter 8, and in this chapter we assume you are familiar with the basics. In a rigid body simulator, it's common to keep on hand redundant copies of the orientation in alternate formats. Typically, both a quaternion and rotation matrix are maintained. We will adopt a similar policy here with our notation. We let R (t) be the object-to-upright rotation matrix at time t ; it is the orientation of the body expressed in matrix form. We also use q (t) to refer to that same rotation as a quaternion. Although both functions express the same value, they are different “data types.”
第 11 章讲的是线性运动学：我们考虑了一个函数 p (t) ，它将粒子的位置描述为时间函数。我们还考虑了它的一阶和二阶导数，即速度函数和加速度函数，分别记为 v (t)= p˙ (t) 和 a (t)= p¨ (t) 。位置的旋转模拟当然是方向。描述物体方向的方法有很多种。第 8 章用了大量篇幅来解释和比较这些方法，本章假设您熟悉这些基础知识。在刚体模拟器中，通常会以不同的格式保存方向的冗余副本。通常，四元数和旋转矩阵都会被保留。在这里，我们将采用类似的策略来表示符号。我们令 R (t) 为时间 t 时物体到直立方向的旋转矩阵；它是以矩阵形式表示的物体方向。我们还使用 q (t) 来表示相同的旋转，即四元数。虽然这两个函数表达相同的值，但它们是不同的“数据类型”。

The analog of linear velocity and acceleration are called angular velocity and angular acceleration. We denote them as ω ω (t) and α α (t) , respectively, and both of these quantities are 3D vectors, or infinitesimal exponential maps (see Section 8.4) if you will. We were able to define linear velocity as the time derivative of position, but things are a bit more complicated with orientation. In general, ω ω (t) is not the derivative of the orientation in any format (even exponential map). We have more to say on this when we look at what the derivatives of angular values really arein Section 12.6.4.
线速度和加速度的类似物称为角速度和角加速度。我们分别将它们表示为 ω ω (t) 和 α α (t) ，这两个量都是三维矢量，或者也可以称之为无穷小指数映射（参见 8.4 节）。我们可以将线速度定义为位置对时间的导数，但对于方向来说，情况会更加复杂。通常， ω ω (t) 在任何形式（即使是指数映射）下都不是方向的导数。我们将在 12.6.4 节中讨论角度值的导数的真正含义时对此进行更详细的说明。

So our first order of business is to understand how to express and measure angular velocity. This is tricky, not just because rotation in 3D is more complicated than position, but also because there are two slightly different types of angular velocity. The first is known as spin angular velocity, and the second is orbital angular velocity. Spin angular velocity describes the rate of change of orientation of an object and is not affected by translation of the object. Orbital angular velocity is actually not concerned with orientation at all; instead, it measures the rate at which the position of an object traces out an orbit around some other point. We already introduced orbital angular velocity in Section 11.8.2, so if you skipped that section, now would be a good time to review it.
因此，我们的首要任务是理解如何表达和测量角速度。这很棘手，不仅因为三维空间中的旋转比位置更复杂，还因为角速度有两种略有不同的类型。第一种称为自旋角速度，第二种是轨道角速度。自旋角速度描述的是物体方向的变化率，不受物体平移的影响。轨道角速度实际上与方向完全无关；相反，它测量的是物体位置绕其他点描绘轨道的速度。我们已经在 11.8.2 节中介绍了轨道角速度，所以如果你跳过了该节，现在是复习一下的好时机。

To see the relationship between spin angular velocity and orbital angular velocity, let's look at an example. Consider an object that is rotating about its center of mass c , which is fixed in space. To describe this rotation, we must specify two things. First, we describe the direction of the rotation; we choose to do this by naming n ^ , a unit vector parallel to the axis of rotation whose sign (in combination with the left hand rule) establishes a direction of positive rotation. Note that n ^ tells us only the direction of the axis; the position comes from our assumption that the axis passes through the center of mass c . The other element necessary to describe the rotation is, of course, the rate of rotation, which we measure in radians per unit time and denote by the scalar ω . Now, we can define the spin angular velocity of the rigid body by the angular velocity vector ω ω (note the boldface), which is simply the multiplication of the rotation rate with the axis:
为了理解自旋角速度和轨道角速度之间的关系，我们来看一个例子。考虑一个物体绕其质心 c 旋转，而质心在空间中是固定的。为了描述这种旋转，我们必须指定两件事。首先，我们描述旋转的方向；我们选择通过命名 n ^ 来实现这一点，它是一个平行于旋转轴的单位矢量，其符号（结合左手定则）确定正旋转方向。请注意， n ^ 仅告诉我们轴的方向；位置来自于我们假设轴穿过质心 c 。描述旋转所需的另一个元素当然是旋转速率，我们以每单位时间的弧度为单位来测量，并用标量 ω 表示。现在，我们可以用角速度矢量 ω ω （注意粗体）来定义刚体的自旋角速度，它只是旋转速率与轴的乘积：

ω ω =ω n ^ .

These ideas should be familiar to you, if you read Section 8.4, which talked about exponential maps, and Section 11.8.2, which discussed uniform circular velocity of a particle and defined orbital velocity. If so, then you can probably already see the connection between spin angular velocity and orbital angular velocity.
如果你读过讨论指数映射的 8.4 节，以及讨论粒子均匀圆周速度和定义轨道速度的 11.8.2 节，你应该对这些概念很熟悉。如果读过，那么你可能已经明白了自旋角速度和轨道角速度之间的联系。

Spin and Orbital Angular Velocity
自旋和轨道角速度
The spin angular velocity of a rigid body is equal to the orbital angular velocity of every point on the rigid body.
刚体的自旋角速度等于刚体上每一点的轨道角速度。

When talking about orbital angular velocity, we must be clear about what point o we are measuring the angular velocity relative to. We do not measure the orbital angular velocity relative to the center of mass c ! We measure the orbital angular velocity relative to the point that is actually being orbited, and only those points on the “equator” of the object are actually orbiting around c . Given any other arbitrary point, it will orbit a point o that lies on the axis of rotation, as shown in Figure 12.16.
在讨论轨道角速度时，我们必须清楚测量的是相对于哪个点 o 的角速度。我们测量的不是相对于质心 c 的轨道角速度！我们测量的是相对于实际绕行点的轨道角速度，而只有物体“赤道”上的点才是真正绕 c 运行的。任何其他任意点，它都会绕位于自转轴上的点 o 运行，如图 12.16 所示。

Figure 12.16  图 12.16 The spin angular velocity of the robot is the same as the orbital velocity of every point on the robot, provided that we choose o carefully.
只要我们仔细选择 o ，机器人的自旋角速度就与机器人上每个点的轨道速度相同。

Now, the astute reader may have noticed some circularity in the definitions just given. We said that the spin angular velocity of the rigid body is equal to the orbital angular velocity of each and every point, provided that the orbital velocity is measured relative to the closest point on the axis of rotation. But how did we know the axis of rotation in the first place? The question is typically moot because, both in analytical kinematics equations and in a digital simulation in a computer, the angular velocity vector ω ω is simply one of the fundamental state variables that we track, so we do not need to infer it from the point velocities. Still, it is worth pointing out that this axis is uniquely determined (up to the reversal of signs). Remember that the axis of rotation is perpendicular to the velocity an orbiting particle. (We must measure the velocity of the particle relative to the center of mass of the rigid object, if the center of mass is moving.) There is only one direction that is simultaneously perpendicular to all the velocities of all the particles, and this direction is the axis of rotation.
现在，精明的读者可能已经注意到刚才给出的定义中存在一些循环。我们说过，刚体的自旋角速度等于每个点的轨道角速度，前提是轨道速度是相对于旋转轴上最近的点测量的。但我们最初是如何知道旋转轴的呢？这个问题通常没有实际意义，因为无论是在解析运动学方程中还是在计算机的数字模拟中，角速度矢量 ω ω 都是我们追踪的基本状态变量之一，因此我们无需根据点速度推断它。不过，值得指出的是，这个轴是唯一确定的（直到符号反转）。记住，旋转轴垂直于轨道粒子的速度。（如果质心在移动，我们必须测量粒子相对于刚体质心的速度。）只有一个方向同时垂直于所有粒子的所有速度，这个方向就是旋转轴。

We started with “a simple example” of an object rotating about an axis that passes through its center of mass, but, as it turns out, this is the general case, at least if we consider instantaneous velocity. The only simplification we made is to fix the center of mass, but, in general, an object can translate as well as rotate. It is somewhat surprising to realize, when you imagine an object tumbling through space, that it will always rotate about an axis passing through the center of mass (though the axis can be arbitrarily oriented). When an object receives a force that induces rotation (known as a torque, to be discussed shortly), the induced rotation will always occur about the center of mass. In fact, to rotate an object about an axis that does not pass through the center of mass requires continual application of some sort of constraint force. In the absence of any external torque (say, the constraint force is removed), the object will rotate about an axis passing through its center of mass, and the angular velocity will be constant—the axis of rotation will not change direction, and the rate of rotation will not change. We are getting a bit ahead of ourselves talking about torques, but we wanted to make it clear that this situation of angular velocity is, in fact, the only situation we need to understand.
我们从一个“简单的例子”开始，一个物体绕着通过其质心的轴旋转，但事实证明，这通常是一种普遍情况，至少在我们考虑瞬时速度的情况下是如此。我们唯一的简化是固定质心，但通常情况下，物体既可以平移也可以旋转。想象一个物体在空间中翻滚，你会惊讶地发现它总是绕着通过质心的轴旋转（尽管轴的方向可以任意改变）。当物体受到一个引起旋转的力（称为扭矩，稍后讨论）时，引起的旋转总是围绕质心发生。事实上，要使物体绕不通过质心的轴旋转，需要持续施加某种约束力。在没有任何外部扭矩（即移除约束力）的情况下，物体将绕着通过其质心的轴旋转，角速度保持不变——旋转轴的方向和旋转速率都不会改变。我们在谈论扭矩时有点超前了，但我们想明确的是，这种角速度的情况实际上是我们需要了解的唯一情况。

Of course, if torques are acting on the object, then the axis and rate of rotation will change over time. This leads us to consider angular acceleration, which is a vector quantity that we denote α α . Angular velocity was not simply the derivative of orientation, as one might naïvely expect by analogy with the linear counterparts. However, the analogy does work for angular acceleration, which is the vector time derivative of angular velocity:
当然，如果扭矩作用于物体，那么旋转轴和旋转速率将随时间变化。这引出了角加速度，它是一个矢量，我们用 α α 表示。角速度并非仅仅是方向的导数，尽管人们可能会天真地通过与线性对应物的类比来推断。然而，这种类比对于角加速度确实适用，它是角速度的矢量时间导数：

α α (t)= ω ω ˙ (t).

The analogy to the linear equation a (t)= v˙ (t) is clear.
与线性方程 a (t)= v˙ (t) 的类比很明显。

12.5.22D Rotational Dynamics
12.5.22D 旋转动力学

Now that we've defined the simple kinematics quantities involved—which was primarily an exercise in notation and reusing the ideas developed elsewhere—let's consider the dynamics of rotation. We first simplify the situation to the case of rotation in the plane (or alternatively, we can think about this as fixing the axis of rotation). In this situation, the angular velocity and acceleration are scalar rather than vector quantities, since there is only one degree of freedom. After we develop some basic ideas in two dimensions in this section, we extend these ideas into three dimensions in Section 12.5.3.
既然我们已经定义了一些简单的运动学量——这主要是为了练习符号，并复用了其他地方提出的思想——那么让我们来考虑旋转动力学。我们首先将情况简化为平面旋转的情况（或者，我们可以将其视为固定旋转轴的情况）。在这种情况下，角速度和加速度是标量而不是矢量，因为只有一个自由度。在本节中，我们先在二维空间中阐述一些基本概念，然后在 12.5.3 节中将这些概念扩展到三维空间。

Imagine a point with mass m that is attached to a rigid disk whose mass is neglected. The center of the disk is fixed at a pivot, and this constrains the mass to a circular path. Let r be the vector from the pivot to the mass. Thus the orbital radius of the mass is r= ∥ r ∥ . We draw a line on the disk outward from its center, and we assume that we can affix the mass to the disk at any distance r along this line. Note that the radius of the disk itself (being massless) is not relevant, so try to shut off your intuition that a really big disk would be hard to rotate. The only source of resistance to the rotation—the only source of inertia—is the point mass. We are neglecting the inertia of the disk.
想象一个质量为 m 的点，它附着在一个忽略质量的刚性圆盘上。圆盘的中心固定在一个枢轴上，这将质量约束在圆形轨道上。令 r 为从枢轴到质量的矢量。因此，质量的轨道半径为 r= ∥ r ∥ 。我们在圆盘上从中心向外画一条线，并假设我们可以将质量沿着这条线以任意距离 r 附着在圆盘上。注意，圆盘本身（没有质量）的半径与此无关，所以试着消除你的直觉，即一个非常大的圆盘很难旋转。旋转阻力的唯一来源——惯性的唯一来源——是点质量。我们忽略了圆盘的惯性。

Consider what happens when a force f is applied directly at m . According to Newton's second law, the mass wants to accelerate in the direction of f . However, any portion of f parallel to r will be repelled by a contact force from the disk and will have no effect on the mass. In contrast, the portion of f perpendicular to r , tangential to the orbit of the mass, will cause the point mass to accelerate. Let F denote the magnitude of f , and F⊥ denote the amount of f that is perpendicular r . This is depicted in Figure 12.17.
考虑当力 f 直接作用于 m 时会发生什么。根据牛顿第二定律，质量块会沿 f 方向加速。然而， f 平行于 r 的任何部分都会受到圆盘接触力的排斥，不会对质量块产生任何影响。相反， f 垂直于 r 的部分（与质量块轨道相切）将导致点质量块加速。令 F 表示 f 的大小， F⊥ 表示 f 垂直于 r 的量。如图 12.17 所示。

Figure 12.17  图 12.17 A disk is constrained to rotate about o . A mass m is attached to the disk at a radius r , and a force f is applied on the mass.
一个圆盘被约束为绕 o 旋转。一个质量块 m 附着在圆盘上，半径为 r ，并且一个力 f 施加在质量块上。

With a bit of trig, we can compute F⊥ from ϕ , which is the angle between f and r :
利用一些三角函数，我们可以根据 ϕ 计算出 F⊥ ，即 f 和 r 之间的角度：

F⊥ / F=sin⁡(π−ϕ),(π−ϕ  is the interior angle )F⊥ / F=sin⁡πcos⁡ϕ−cos⁡πsin⁡ϕ,(using \refeqlongch{cartesianspace_sin_diff_identity})F⊥ / F=(0)cos⁡ϕ−(−1)sin⁡ϕ,F⊥=Fsin⁡ϕ.

By applying Newton's second law, we can compute the magnitude of the tangential acceleration as
利用牛顿第二定律，我们可以计算切向加速度的大小

a⊥=F⊥ / m.

(Don't confuse tangential acceleration, which causes a change in the rate of rotation, with centripetal acceleration, which is created by contact force with the disk and maintains the orbital path.)
（不要混淆切向加速度（它会导致旋转速度发生变化）和向心加速度（它是由与磁盘的接触力产生并维持轨道的。）

By definition, the linear tangential acceleration a = p ¨ is simultaneously an angular acceleration α= θ¨ about the pivot, and they are related by
根据定义，线性切向加速度 a = p ¨ 同时也是绕枢轴的角加速度 α= θ¨ ，它们之间的关系为

α=a⊥ / r.

To understand where this comes from, remember from Section 11.8.1 the relationship between linear speed and angular velocity: v⊥=s=rω .
要理解这一点，请回想一下第 11.8.1 节中线速度和角速度之间的关系： v⊥=s=rω 。

Figure 12.18  图 12.18 Applying a force at an arbitrary point on the disk with lever arm l .
使用杠杆臂 l 在磁盘上的任意点施加力。

Now imagine that we keep the mass fixed at r , but instead of applying our force directly onto the mass, we push against a peg that sticks up out of the disk at some other location, at a distance l= ∥ l ∥ . The vector l goes from the fulcrum o to the point where the force is applied and is known as the lever arm. This is shown in Figure 12.18.
现在假设我们将质量固定在 r 处，但力不是直接作用在质量上，而是作用在圆盘上另一个位置（距离 l= ∥ l ∥ ）的一个突出的桩子上。矢量 l 从支点 o 指向力的作用点，称为杠杆臂。如图 12.18 所示。

Allow us to clarify a point which is potentially confusing. Earlier, in Figure 12.17, the vectors r and l were the same, since we were applying the force directly onto the (one and only) point mass. But in general, mass is distributed around the disk, so there are many m 's and r 's. The portion of the applied force that is effective at rotating the disk is perpendicular to the lever arm, not the radius vector r , as you might infer from Figure 12.17.
请允许我们澄清一个可能令人困惑的点。之前在图 12.17 中，矢量 r 和 l 是相同的，因为我们将力直接施加到（唯一的）点质量上。但通常情况下，质量分布在圆盘周围，因此存在多个 m 和 r 。施加的力中，能够有效旋转圆盘的部分垂直于杠杆臂，而不是像你可能从图 12.17 推断的那样垂直于半径矢量 r 。

Let's consider how changes to the lever arm affect the resulting accelerations. First, we note that if we apply the force anywhere on the circle with the same radius as the mass, meaning l=r , then the whole apparatus gains angular momentum, just as if we had pushed against the mass directly. In other words, the only thing that matters about l is the distance from the fulcrum l= ∥ l ∥ and the angle ϕ between the lever arm and the applied force. Rotating both the lever arm and the applied force does not change the resulting angular acceleration.
让我们考虑一下杠杆臂的变化如何影响由此产生的加速度。首先，我们注意到，如果我们在半径与质量相同的圆上的任意位置施加力，即 l=r ，那么整个装置都会获得角动量，就像我们直接推向质量一样。换句话说，关于 l 唯一重要的因素是与支点的距离 l= ∥ l ∥ 以及杠杆臂与施加力之间的角度 ϕ 。同时旋转杠杆臂和施加力不会改变由此产生的角加速度。

If the peg is closer to the fulcrum than the mass ( l<r ), then we must push harder in order to produce the same acceleration of the mass. If l>r , a smaller force will accomplish the job. Thus, increasing the lever arm l has a proportionate effect on the tangential acceleration a⊥ of the mass. This is the basic principle of mechanical advantage of a lever, which Archimedes discovered. But what effect does changing l have on α , the angular acceleration of the apparatus? It, too, is directly proportional: if we push on the disk at a point twice as far out, the angular acceleration is twice as much. This is clear from the relation α=a⊥ / r . If this seems too obvious to bother pointing out, then keep reading.
如果桩子比质量块 ( l<r ) 更靠近支点，那么我们必须用更大的力推才能使质量块产生相同的加速度。如果是 l>r ，则较小的力即可完成该工作。因此，增加杠杆臂 l 对质量块的切向加速度 a⊥ 有成比例的影响。这是阿基米德发现的杠杆机械效益的基本原理。但是改变 l 对装置的角加速度 α 有什么影响呢？它也是成正比的：如果我们在两倍远的地方推圆盘，角加速度也会是两倍。这从关系式 α=a⊥ / r 中可以清楚地看出。如果这看起来太明显而懒得指出，那么请继续阅读。

Let's summarize what we've found out. When a force is applied to an object, it has a tendency to rotate that object. This “cause” of angular acceleration is known as torque, which we denote by using the Greek letter tau:18 τ τ . Although the linear acceleration of a body as a result of an applied force does not depend on where the force is applied, the amount of torque that results from an applied force depends on how effectively the force is applied. The effectiveness of the force to create rotational acceleration—the magnitude of the torque—depends on several factors:
让我们总结一下我们的发现。当力作用于物体时，它有使物体旋转的趋势。这种角加速度的“起因”被称为扭矩，我们用希腊字母 tau 表示：18 τ τ 。虽然物体因受力而产生的线性加速度与力的施加位置无关，但施加力产生的扭矩大小取决于力的施加效率。力产生旋转加速度的有效性（扭矩的大小）取决于以下几个因素：

  • It is proportional to the magnitude of the applied force f .
    它与施加的力 f 的大小成正比。
  • It is proportional to the length of the lever arm l , which is the vector from the fulcrum to the point of application of the force.
    它与杠杆臂的长度 l 成比例，杠杆臂是从支点到力的作用点的矢量。
  • Only the portion of the force perpendicular to the lever arm counts. Equivalently, the torque is proportional to sin⁡ϕ , where ϕ is the angle between f and l .
    只有垂直于杠杆臂的力才有效。等效地，扭矩与 sin⁡ϕ 成比例，其中 ϕ 是 f 和 l 之间的角度。

In two dimensions, we can state this succinctly by
在二维中，我们可以简洁地表述为

Torque in two dimensions  二维扭矩
(12.24)τ=Flsin⁡ϕ.

The dimensions of torque are not the same as force. Torque has units of “force times length.” The SI unit for torque is the Newton meter. (This is dimensionally equivalent to the joule, but torque and energy are distinct concepts, and the joule is not really the proper unit to use fortorque.)
扭矩的量纲与力不同。扭矩的单位是“力乘以长度”。扭矩的国际单位制（SI）是牛顿米。（扭矩的量纲与焦耳相同，但扭矩和能量是不同的概念，焦耳实际上并不是扭矩的合适单位。）

In might not be intuitively obvious that torque increases with the length of the lever arm. For example, your intuition might be inclined to tell you that it would be more difficult to push at an increased radius because you have to push faster just to keep up. If so, your intuition is wrong, but don't feel bad. Our experience with force is often via an everyday type of physical push like we might make with our hands against some object. But this is not necessarily a good example because the push must move faster and faster as the object accelerates in order to maintain contact. But the speed of some source of force has nothing to do with the magnitude of the force itself. So try replacing the physical push with either a gust of wind or a quick “thump” (an impulse). You can conduct this experiment on a door. If you blow on the door or whack it close to the hinge (shorter lever arm), your action won't cause the door to rotate as easily if you do the same thing nearer to side with the handle (longer lever arm). That's exactly why we put door handles on the side opposite the hinge: to make it easier to open the door!
扭矩会随着杠杆臂长度的增加而增大，这一点可能在直觉上并不明显。例如，你的直觉可能会告诉你，在更大的半径下推动会更加困难，因为你必须加快推力才能跟上。如果是这样，你的直觉是错误的，但不要感到难过。我们对力的体验通常来自于日常的物理推力，比如我们用手推某个物体。但这未必是一个好的例子，因为为了保持接触，物体加速时，推力必须越来越快。但力源的速度与力本身的大小无关。所以，试着用一阵风或快速的“砰”的一声（一个脉冲）来代替物理推力。你可以在门上做这个实验。如果你对着门吹气或用力猛击靠近铰链（杠杆臂较短）的地方，那么如果你在靠近把手（杠杆臂较长）的地方做同样的事情，你的动作就不会像在靠近门把手（杠杆臂较长）的地方那样轻易地使门旋转。这就是我们将门把手放在铰链另一侧的原因：这样更容易打开门！

The relationship between torque and force is an important one to understand. Any force applied to a body can produce both a linear acceleration and a torque. Of course, it is the net force and torque that determine the acceleration(s) of the body. Two key examples in Figure 12.19 illustrate this point. On the left, a force is acting along a line that passes through the center of mass, resulting in no torque. In this case, sin⁡ϕ=0 since the line of action of the force is parallel to the lever arm. The right side of Figure 12.19 shows a different extreme case: two forces with equal magnitudes but opposite directions are acting on opposite lever arms. A pair of forces coordinated like this are known as a couple, and they result in a net torque, but zero net linear force. When you turn a bolt with a wrench, what you are really doing is supplying two or more contact forces.
