由于执行第二种方法的成本略高，因此一个有效的问题是：它值得吗？在角速度恒定的常见情况下，第二种方法对于任何步长 h 都是精确的，忽略由于浮点舍入引起的误差。在这种情况下，如果角速度很高，或者所需的精度很高（例如，时钟的指针），那么切换到这种替代方法可能会成功。然而，欧拉积分引入的误差可能会以建设性或破坏性的方式干扰逐分量导数方法引入的误差，因此无法保证减少一个误差源实际上会在所有情况下提高最终结果的精度。这就是为什么积分角位移的方法在某些物理引擎中是一种选择的原因。

12.7Suggested Reading  12.7 建议阅读

Our discussion has been necessarily compact, and we cringe at the derision actual physics experts must feel towards our presentation. Clearly, a student with a serious interest in computer simulation will need a more thorough background in physics than was provided here. The basics of mechanics are usually covered in the first semester of a traditional physics course, for which there are numerous textbooks of high quality. In preparing this book, we used Resnick and Halliday's venerable textbook [12], which has a distinct advantage of being incredibly inexpensive, and also a textbook by Knight [9]. No one should ever learn this material without in-class demonstrations; a student engaged in self-study (or stuck with a lame physics teacher) need not miss out, as many demonstrations can be found online. We recommend Professor Walter Lewin's lectures, available from MIT OpenCourseWare at ocw.mit.edu.
我们的讨论必然紧凑，而真正的物理学专家们对我们的演讲所抱有的嘲笑，让我们感到尴尬。显然，一个对计算机模拟真正感兴趣的学生，需要比这里提供的更全面的物理学背景。力学的基础知识通常在传统物理课程的第一学期讲授，而这门课程有许多高质量的教科书。在编写本书时，我们使用了 Resnick 和 Halliday 编著的经典教科书[12]，它有一个明显的优势，那就是价格极其低廉，此外我们还使用了 Knight 编著的教科书[9]。任何人都不应该在课堂上没有演示的情况下学习这些内容；自学的学生（或者遇到一个不靠谱的物理老师）也不必错过，因为网上有很多演示。我们推荐 Walter Lewin 教授的讲座，可从麻省理工学院开放课程网站 ocw.mit.edu 获取。

Three books are recommended for their discussion of physics simulation tailored to the needs of video games. Bourg's Physics for Game Developers [1] is an introductory text, with good coverage of the basics and a unique presentation of numerous force laws applied towards different types of vehicle simulations. Physics-Based Animation [5] contains a wealth of information for both rigid-body and continuous simulations, including a survey of several different approaches to multibody simulation; this text is your best bet for filling in the gaps left by the vague hand-waving we've had to do here. Eberly's Game Physics [3] considers physics engines for games in a slightly more academic and mathematically oriented manner. It contains good discussions on techniques of numerical integration and a unique section concerning the potential (currently unrealized) advantages of Lagrangian dynamics. For Bourg's book, the calculus covered in this book is sufficient, but exposure to differential equations is recommended before tackling the two more advanced books.
推荐三本探讨如何根据电子游戏需求定制物理模拟的书籍。Bourg 的《游戏开发者物理学》[1] 是一本入门教材，涵盖了基础知识，并以独特的方式呈现了应用于不同类型车辆模拟的众多力定律。《基于物理的动画》[5] 包含丰富的刚体和连续模拟信息，并概述了几种不同的多体模拟方法；这本书是填补我们之前含糊其辞的解释所留下的空白的最佳选择。Eberly 的《游戏物理学》[3] 则以略微学术化和数学化的方式探讨了游戏物理引擎。它对数值积分技术进行了深入的讨论，并专门开辟了一个章节，探讨了拉格朗日动力学的潜在优势（目前尚未实现）。对于 Bourg 的教材而言，本书涵盖的微积分知识已经足够，但建议在阅读另外两本更高级的书籍之前，先学习一些微分方程。

Another excellent way to learn about a real-time physics simulation is to study the code of one. Two well-designed and documented open source physics engines that have been used in commercial video games were influential in the writing of this book and are worth mentioning. Russell Smith's Open Dynamics Engine [14], available online at http://ode.org/, is slightly older and is not under active development, but has been influential in the industry and is a useful resource. A newer collaboration by various industry experts called Bullet Physics (http://bulletphysics.org/) is actively maintained and has been used in many games and even some Dreamworks movies. The engine and the website are both useful resources.
学习实时物理模拟的另一个绝佳方法是研究其代码。两个设计精良、文档齐全的开源物理引擎曾用于商业视频游戏，它们对本书的写作产生了影响，值得一提。Russell Smith 的 Open Dynamics Engine [14] 可在 http://ode.org/ 在线获取。它开发时间稍长，目前开发进度不快，但在业界颇具影响力，是一个实用的资源。Bullet Physics（http://bulletphysics.org/）是由多位业内专家合作开发的一个新引擎，目前仍在积极维护中，并已在许多游戏甚至梦工厂的一些电影中使用。该引擎及其网站都是实用的资源。

Collision detection is a large portion of any physics engine, both in terms of lines of code and CPU time consumed. Unfortunately, it's difficult to say “a little” about collision detection, and we haven't had the space to do it justice in this book. Ericson's Real-Time Collision Detection [4] is our top recommendation, but van den Bergen's text [16] is also useful. A significant amount of material on collision detection material can be found in Eberly's books on physics engines [3] and geometric tools for games [13].
碰撞检测在任何物理引擎中都占了很大一部分，无论是代码行数还是 CPU 时间消耗。遗憾的是，很难用“一点点”来概括碰撞检测，而且本书也没有足够的篇幅来充分阐述它。Ericson 的《实时碰撞检测》[4] 是我们最推荐的，但 van den Bergen 的教材 [16] 也很有用。在 Eberly 的物理引擎书籍 [3] 和游戏几何工具书籍 [13] 中，可以找到大量关于碰撞检测的资料。

Many of the mathematical problems that arise in computer simulation fall under the broad category of scientific computing. (Older names for this same basic subject area are “applied mathematics” and “numerical analysis.”) Numerical Recipes in C [11] is a classic work for engineers, with clear explanations and a large toolkit of source code. Several good textbooks exist on the subject; we can recommend Scientific Computing by Heath [6]. Strang's textbook [15] has the compelling feature that an entire course of accompanying lectures are available free from MIT OpenCourseWare at ocw.mit.edu.
计算机模拟中出现的许多数学问题都属于科学计算的范畴。（这一基础学科领域的旧称是“应用数学”和“数值分析”。）《C 语言数值方法》[11]是一本面向工程师的经典著作，解释清晰，并提供了丰富的源代码工具包。该领域有几本优秀的教科书；我们推荐 Heath 的《科学计算》[6]。Strang 的教科书[15]有一个引人注目的特点，那就是可以从麻省理工学院开放课程（ocw.mit.edu）免费获取整套配套课程的讲座。

Chris Hecker has a collection of resources for real-time physics athttp://chrishecker.com/Physics_References.
Chris Hecker 在 http://chrishecker.com/Physics_References 上收集了实时物理资源。

Exercises  练习

  1. In a cartoon universe, a sailboat can be propelled by placing a fan in the sailboat and pointing it at the sail. Explain why this doesn't work in the real world, by using Newton's laws.
    在卡通世界里，帆船可以通过在船内放置一个风扇并将其指向船帆来推进。请用牛顿定律解释为什么这在现实世界中行不通。
  2. A boy and a girl are playing tug of war. The girl begins to win. Name all of the important forces involved, and describe which force imbalance is causing the girl to begin winning.
    一个男孩和一个女孩正在玩拔河。女孩开始赢了。说出所有涉及的重要力量，并描述哪种力量的不平衡导致女孩开始获胜。
  3. True or false: Lighter objects fall faster than heavier ones because the force of gravity is a constant near Earth's surface.
    对还是错：较轻的物体比较重的物体下落得更快，因为地球表面附近的重力是恒定的。
  4. The International Space Station orbits Earth at approximately 340 km above Earth's surface at a speed of approximately 27,740 km/hr. (The orbit is actually elliptical, but ignore that for now.) What is the acceleration caused by Earth's gravity in this “zero gravity” environment? Also, if the Earth's gravity still has a significant effect, why are astronauts in the space station “weightless”? (Note: see also Exercise 11.12.)
    国际空间站在距地球表面约 340 公里的轨道上运行，速度约为 27740 公里/小时。（轨道实际上是椭圆形的，但暂时忽略这一点。）在这种“零重力”环境下，地球引力引起的加速度是多少？另外，如果地球引力仍然有显著的影响，为什么空间站里的宇航员会“失重”？（注：另见练习 11.12。）
  5. A concrete block is placed on a wooden ramp. According to Table 12.1, what is the critical angle of inclination of the ramp at which the block will begin to slide? If we conducted the experiment on the moon, would the critical angle increase, decrease, or stay the same?
    一块混凝土块放在木制斜坡上。根据表 12.1，当斜坡的倾斜角达到多少时，混凝土块开始滑动？如果我们在月球上进行实验，临界角会增加、减少还是保持不变？
    1. (a)A weight with mass m is hung from a spring with a stiffness of k , causing the spring to increase in length by a distance x0 . What is the formula that relates m , x0 , and k ?
      （a）一个质量为 m 的重物悬挂在一个刚度为 k 的弹簧上，使弹簧的长度增加了 x0 。 m 、 x0 和 k 之间的关系公式是什么？
    2. (b)A 5.00 kg object is suspended from a spring, causing the spring to increase in length by 10.0 cm. What is the spring constant k ? (Make sure to include the proper units.)
      （b）一个 5.00 公斤的物体悬挂在弹簧上，弹簧长度增加了 10.0 厘米。弹簧常数 k 是多少？（请确保包含正确的单位。）
    3. (c)A different object is hung from the same spring, this time causing the spring to lengthen by 17.0 cm. What is the mass of this other object?
      （c）将另一个物体悬挂在同一根弹簧上，这次弹簧伸长了 17.0 厘米。这个物体的质量是多少？
    4. (d)Later, in a different environment, a 1.00 kg weight is hung from this same spring, this time causing an increase in length of 8.0 cm. What can you say about this environment that is different from the original environment? What are some possible explanations for these differences?
      （d）之后，在另一个环境中，在同一根弹簧上悬挂一个 1.00 公斤的重物，这次导致其长度增加了 8.0 厘米。你能解释一下这个环境与原始环境有何不同吗？这些差异可能由哪些原因造成？
  7. A horizontal spring with stiffness 1.00×102  N / m is fixed at one end, and a 5.00 kg mass is connected on the other end, such that the mass slides back and forth on a frictionless surface. The spring is extended from its rest position by a distance of 14.7 cm.
    一根刚度为 1.00×102  N / m 的水平弹簧的一端固定，另一端连接一个 5.00 kg 的重物，使重物在无摩擦表面上来回滑动。弹簧从静止位置伸长了 14.7 cm。
    1. (a)What is the frequency of the oscillation?
      （a）振荡的频率是多少？
    2. (b)What is the amplitude of the oscillation?
      （b）振荡的幅度是多少？
    3. (c)What is the speed of the mass as it crosses the rest position?
      （c）当物体穿过静止位置时，其速度是多少？
  8. A man weighing 75.0 kg is standing at one end of a train car. The car weighs 1.00×103  kg, is 20.0 m long, and is from the future, where they have invented a special type of wheel that rolls over the tracks with zero friction. Use a coordinate space where the forward direction is +x . The man walks from the back end of the car to the front end at a rate of 1.25 m/s.
    一名体重 75.0 公斤的男子站在一节火车车厢的一端。这节车厢重 1.00×103 公斤，长 20.0 米，来自未来。未来发明了一种特殊的轮子，可以在轨道上滚动，且摩擦力为零。使用向前方向为 +x 的坐标空间。该男子以 1.25 米/秒的速度从车厢后端走到前端。
    1. (a)What are velocities of the man and the car, relative to Earth, during the man's walk?
      (a) 在男子行走过程中，男子和汽车相对于地球的速度是多少？
    2. (b)When the man reaches the end of the car, how far have the man and the car moved, in world coordinates?
      （b）当该男子到达汽车末端时，在世界坐标中，该男子和汽车移动了多远？
    3. (c)What if, rather than walking at a constant velocity, the man builds up as much speed as he can and then comes to an abrupt stop at the end of the car. What would change about the motion of the car? What about the final positions?
      （c）如果这个人不是匀速行走，而是尽可能地加速，然后在车尾突然停下，会怎么样？汽车的运动会发生什么变化？最终的位置又会怎样？
    The experiment is repeated (the man walks with a constant velocity), only this time the car and man have an initial velocity of +5.00 m/s.
    重复实验（男子以恒定速度行走），只是这次汽车和男子的初始速度为 +5.00 m/s。
    1. (d)What are velocities of the man and the car, relative to Earth, during the man's walk?
      (d) 在男子行走过程中，男子和汽车相对于地球的速度是多少？
    2. (e)At the moment the man reaches the end of the car, how far have the man and the car been displaced relative to Earth?
      （e）当人到达汽车末端时，人和汽车相对于地球的位移有多远？
  9. Consider the car crash between Grant and Kari in Section 12.4.1. Calculate the magnitude of the collision impulse, only this time instead of assuming a perfectly inelastic collision, use a coefficient of restitution of e=0.1 . (Assume a contact normal of 20 o west of south.) What are the resulting velocities of the two cars?
    考虑 12.4.1 节中 Grant 和 Kari 之间的车祸。计算碰撞冲量的幅值。这次我们不再假设完全非弹性碰撞，而是使用恢复系数 e=0.1 。（假设接触法线方向为南偏西方向 20 o 。）两辆车的最终速度是多少？
  10. How does the monkey in Figure 12.21 stay balanced on the tightrope? How does the bend in the bar help?
    图 12.21 中的猴子是如何在绳索上保持平衡的？绳索上的弯曲有什么作用？
    Figure 12.21  图 12.21How does this monkey stay balanced?
    这只猴子如何保持平衡？
  11. Two cylinders have the same shape and mass. One is hollow, and the other is solid with uniform density. Which do you expect would be harder to roll?

    他/她/它……由于外星人拥有三种性别的可能性与两种性别的可能性一样大，英语的局限性无法满足星际政治正确的要求。如果有任何外星人正在读这本书，请注意，我们努力过，所以没有把我们的星球原子化。我们非常喜欢它。
  5. One could easily imagine Yoda saying “To every action, always an equal and opposite reaction, there is.”
    人们很容易想象尤达会说“每一个作用力，总会有一个大小相等、方向相反的反作用力。”
  6. Actually, this is not true. At the time of this writing, physicists believe that there are four fundamental forces. Almost all forces caused by matter bumping up against other matter are essentially electrical because it is electrical forces that keep atoms separated from one another. However, the situations in which matter pushes away from other matter are so diverse that at the macroscopic level it is useful to have many different force laws to describe the behavior.
    事实上，这并非事实。在撰写本文时，物理学家认为存在四种基本力。几乎所有物质碰撞产生的力本质上都是电场力，因为正是电场力使原子彼此分离。然而，物质相互排斥的情况多种多样，因此在宏观层面上，用许多不同的力定律来描述这种行为是有用的。

    与摩擦相反。

    如果您决定这样做，请听取以下建议：(1) 请注意安全。说真的，我们对任何愚蠢的行为不承担任何责任。（说到愚蠢，有位作者不得不更换他父亲的割草机轮子，因为这个轮子虽然有完美的抛物线轨迹，但可惜无法承受落地时的冲击力。）(2) 我们以大约 4 Hz 的频率拍摄静态照片，但使用性能更佳、每秒可拍摄更多帧的相机，或者从视频中提取帧可能效果更好。(3) 请将您的照片发送至 gamemath.com！

    我们选择让卡莉成为糟糕的司机，并不是因为性别歧视，也不是因为她是红头发，而是基于这样的假设：与格兰特相比，可得罪的卡莉要少。
  15. Another MythBusters moment.
    另一个流言终结者时刻。
  16. Actually, an object don't necessarily have to be stationary to be “special” like this. Consider a platform that moves along a spline path created by a level designer, or some other hand-animated object that is not allowed to deviate from its prescribed trajectory. These so-called kinematically controlled objects do move around in the world and must be known to the physics engine if other (nonkinematically controlled!) objects need to interact with them, but such objects do not respond to forces, and their position is not updated by the physics engine. Although the mass of these objects is treated as infinite, proper collision response requires knowledge of the (kinematically determined) velocity.
    实际上，物体并非必须静止不动才能如此“特殊”。想象一下，一个平台沿着关卡设计师创建的样条曲线路径移动，或者其他一些手工动画的物体，这些物体不允许偏离其规定的轨迹。这些所谓的运动学控制物体确实会在世界中移动，如果其他（非运动学控制的！）物体需要与它们交互，物理引擎必须知道这些物体，但这些物体不会对力做出响应，物理引擎也不会更新它们的位置。虽然这些物体的质量被视为无限大，但正确的碰撞响应需要知道（运动学确定的）速度。
  17. As Werner von Braun, who really was a rocket scientist, said, “Research is what I'm doing when I don't know what I'm doing.”
    正如真正的火箭科学家沃纳·冯·布劳恩所说：“当我不知道自己在做什么时，我所做的就是研究。”

    它与“cow”押韵
  19. Remember, our convention in this book is to use row vectors, since the majority of matrices encountered in 3D interactive applications are transformation matrices, and the left-to-right reading order is a useful advantage. In the derivation above, we used column vectors for pedagogical and aesthetic purposes (the inertia tensor is not a transform matrix), but shame on us for being inconsistent. From here on out, we'll stick with our convention and put the vectors on the left.
    请记住，本书的惯例是使用行向量，因为在 3D 交互应用中遇到的大多数矩阵都是变换矩阵，而从左到右的阅读顺序是一个很有用的优势。在上面的推导中，出于教学和美观的目的（惯性张量不是变换矩阵），我们使用了列向量，但我们对此感到惭愧，这不太一致。从现在开始，我们将坚持惯例，将向量放在左侧。

    具体细节取决于数值积分的方法。一些积分方法利用历史值来近似高阶导数。
  21. Usually. Press et al. \cite_need_fixup{numerical-recipes} make a point of stressing that higher order does not always guarantee higher accuracy.
    通常如此。Press 等人 \cite_need_fixup{numerical-recipes} 强调，高阶并不一定能保证更高的准确度。
